models.name: ChirpNet
models.tagline: Neural networks that never saw a real gravitational wave, then found five.
models.question: Is there a black-hole or neutron-star merger in this LIGO data, and how heavy was it?
models.summary: Four small networks trained only on simulated mergers from general relativity. Pointed at real recordings from the two LIGO observatories they find the black-hole and neutron-star mergers, weigh them, and give calibrated posterior ranges. Since v2.1 a physics template bank (a TaylorF2 matched filter) refines the neutron-star chirp mass after the network finds the merger. Everything runs on plain numpy and scipy.
models.reads: Whitened strain from LIGO Hanford and Livingston (GWOSC HDF5, 4 kHz).
returns: Detection statistic and false-alarm rate (upper limit from time slides)
Chirp mass ± 68%, mass ratio, merger time
Posterior samples of masses, effective spin, distance and inclination (DINGO-style flow)
A separate neutron-star detector; its chirp mass refined by a matched filter (v2.1) with a 68% range
models.network: 1-D residual CNN finder + two-stream coincidence checker (882k weights), an 8-layer RealNVP posterior flow, and a 2-D time-frequency CNN for neutron stars, followed (v2.1) by a TaylorF2 matched filter for their chirp mass
models.noise: Simulated Gaussian noise coloured by O1/O2 and design spectra; the exam background is time-slid real LIGO data.

approach.physics_anchor: v2.1: the neutron-star chirp mass is a TaylorF2 matched-filter fit seeded by the network's reading

wins: Finds all four O1/O2 black-hole events with a clear gap above real background.
Posteriors are calibrated (P-P within chance) and contain every GWTC-1 median.
The cascade cuts loud single-detector fakes from 99.6% to 17%.
Unchanged since O1/O2, it finds all seven in-range O3 events named in advance, and every O3 catalogue median lands inside its 90% posteriors.
losses: GW170817: the network alone reads the chirp mass 5% low with too narrow an interval; v2.1's matched filter fixes the value, but its 68% range is one-sided and misses LIGO's median by 0.00003.
GW151226's Hanford signal alone still scores above threshold (so do GW190408's and GW200311's in O3).
Misses GW190521, a merger heavier than anything in its training set.
One O3 exam background window (7.24) clears the 7.0 threshold set on O1/O2 noise; on 10.6 h of non-exam O3 noise 46 windows do (loudest 10.88).
limits: Aligned spins only; no precession or higher modes.
False-alarm rates rest on hours of time slides, so they are upper limits.
The neutron-star model has no coincidence check yet.
The neutron-star matched filter has no spin or tidal templates; its 68% range is the raw likelihood range widened ×52 on simulated injections, and it needs minutes of raw strain.
No network can be retrained on this machine: the LALSuite waveform banks were never kept and LALSuite has no Windows build.
Real events tested come from O1–O3 (2015–2020); O4 is untested.
Very heavy mergers (detector-frame chirp mass above ~45) are outside the training range: GW190521 is missed.

False-alarm rate (audit, 25 Nov 2026): the 7.0 threshold was set above the maximum (6.20) of the 2.006 h time-slide background, so zero exceedances there are by construction. Until 27 Nov 2026 the reader reported 1/T = 0.50/h as an upper bound; it now reports the Poisson 90 % upper limit, 2.303/T = 1.15/h. On O3 dev time slides at least 4 of 64 pieces scored 7.0 or more (at least 0.38/h of slide exposure). A false-alarm rate for continuous data is not measured.
next: Extend the training bank to heavier mergers (GW190521-like) and re-run the ratchet (needs LALSuite on Linux or macOS).
O3: ship the O3 dev background so scan() reports O3 false-alarm rates from O3 noise, then retrain with O3-like glitches next to gates.
A coincidence checker for the neutron-star model.
Spin-aligned templates for the matched filter, and a range from a likelihood over spin instead of a widening factor.
Live posterior sampling in the browser.

physics.summary: Aligned-spin waveforms from general relativity (IMRPhenomD for black holes, IMRPhenomD_NRTidalv2 for neutron stars via LALSuite), projected onto the two detectors with the real light-travel delay and whitened with O1/O2 and design noise spectra.

models.name: SunDoctor
models.tagline: A day-by-day doctor for solar farms, trained on sunlight physics alone.
models.question: Why did this solar array make less power today, and what did each cause cost?
models.summary: SunDoctor reads two weeks of a PV system's power (with or without an irradiance sensor) and diagnoses it day by day: dead strings with their failure and repair days, shading, clipping, outages, soiling, snow and stuck trackers, plus the kWh lost to each. It learned only from a physics simulator and was examined on two real utility-scale farms.

returns: Dead-string count per day, with failure and repair days
Daily loss share for outage, clipping, shading, soiling, snow, stuck trackers and dead strings (± error bars)
kWh lost to each cause
models.network: 2-D CNN over 14 days × 96 solar-time steps, 12 input channels, Gaussian error bars on every output (591k weights)
models.noise: Simulated weather and sensor faults (no instrument archive noise injection; this predates the real-noise recipe)

audit.label: Time ordering, incomplete-day totals & phantom fault calls
audit.finding: Newest-first meter rows produced `0` valid days at two sites; 5 h midday gaps cut `kwh_made` by `60.8%–67.1%` with all 30 days counted. Second pass showed moving just day 0 to EOF collapses both sites to `0` days (`0.00 kWh`), swapping two adjacent days drops 1 day and inflates power-only `outage` `7.4×–9.7×` (`snow` `0% → 1.71%` CO), and 5 h midday gaps fabricate severe `outage` (`29.57%/32.67%` CA) and `shading` (`10.95%/15.29%` CO) faults in both modes (`all_nan_P` cleanly returns `0` days).

models.name: CellSense
models.tagline: Battery health and remaining life from one discharge curve.
models.question: How worn is this battery cell, why, and how many cycles are left? (LFP, and now NMC811)
models.summary: CellSense reads one fast discharge curve of a lithium-ion cell and returns its total capacity, resistance, how much lithium and electrode material it has lost, and a forecast of its cycle life. It learned from an electrochemical simulator calibrated on six real cells, and was examined on 118 others. A second, separate network (v1.2) reads slow C/20 capacity tests of an NMC811 cell (LG M50T), including tests stopped early; there it was calibrated on three real cells and examined on seven, and it mostly loses to guessing the median. Since v1.3 that reader is an ensemble of four networks: cut-short error 135 → 113 mAh, still behind the median guess (105).
models.reads: LFP: one 4C discharge curve (capacity vs voltage, plus temperature) of an A123 LFP/graphite 18650 cell, optionally beside a reference curve from when it was new. NMC811: one C/20 discharge from full (capacity vs voltage) of an LG INR21700-M50T, complete or stopped early, optionally beside the cell's first test.
returns: Total capacity ± error bar, and pulse resistance
Lithium lost, graphite lost, cathode lost (degradation modes)
Cycle-life forecast with a range
A partial-discharge reading for curves that stop before 2.0 V
NMC811 (separate network): capacity to 2.5 V at C/20 ± error bar, fade, and lithium / negative / NMC lost, from a C/20 test complete or stopped early
models.network: Three 1-D residual CNNs along the voltage axis for LFP (health, lifetime, partial discharge) and, for NMC811, an ensemble of four smaller ones (v1.3); β-NLL error bars
models.noise: Measurement noise and cell-to-cell scatter in simulation; six real cells calibrate the LFP aging priors, three the NMC811 ones. NMC811 also: cycler gain error, a few mV of voltage offset, per-cell open-circuit-curve jitter.

wins: Beats the median guess on lifetime from cycle 100, using no real labelled cells for training.
Partial discharges to 0.75 Ah or more read 2–3× better than the no-model baseline.
NMC811: a C/20 test stopped at 2.5 Ah, read with the cell's first test, gives capacity to 86 mAh (dev median 98, classical 152–258; v1.2: 69).
losses: Severson's models, trained on 41 real cells, still forecast lifetime better (13–15% vs 22%).
Last quarter of life — worn cells read about 6% too healthy (36% life error).
Partial discharges stopped at 0.45–0.6 Ah are no better than assuming no fade (52.0 and 46.5 vs 45.7 mAh); at 0.30 Ah it beats no-fade, 41.8 vs 45.7 mAh.

NMC811: over all cut-short C/20 tests it errs by 113 mAh (v1.2: 135); always guessing the dev median errs by 105. Worst stopped at 1.5 Ah with a reference (138 mAh) and at 3.5 Ah with one (117 vs 98; shifting the reference by the gap at the cut gives 84).
NMC811: its 68% error bars cover 39–73% of cut-short readings (39% at 3.5 Ah).
limits: It knows two cells — A123 APR18650M1A at Severson's protocol (4C to 2.0 V, 30 °C), and LG INR21700-M50T NMC811 at a C/20 capacity test (23 °C).
Other chemistries, sizes, rates and temperatures are outside what it learned.
The simulator's graphite-staging features are sharper than real cells'.
NMC811: no lifetime forecast — the Pozzato cells lost only 3–9% and never reached end of life.
NMC811: its open-circuit curves are corrected on three cells; ±15 mV features near the end of discharge remain, and they set the real error.
NMC811: test-to-test variation of the open-circuit curves (measured on the dev cells, 5.1 mV left after a window fit) limits what the simulated frozen set can tell apart.
NMC811: lithium lost versus negative lost is poorly separated by a C/20 curve; the degradation modes have no answer key.

Inputs (audit, 25 Nov 2026): an all-NaN discharge returned a finite capacity (0.82 Ah LFP, 4.03 Ah NMC811); since 27 Nov 2026 it is refused. The NMC811 reader switches from measured end capacity to a network estimate at the 1 mV completion tolerance, so 0.2 mV across it moves capacity 5.3 mAh and its sigma 10.75x; which sigma is better calibrated needs near-cutoff cycles.
next: NMC811: on the dev cells a cut-short reading pulled toward their median by inverse variance reads 126 → 88 mAh (each dev cell left out), but the frozen set, whose cells age up to 2.5x further, scores it 0.033 lower, so the rule rejected it (rung n13). Whether such dev-population steps should be judged by a different rule has to be decided before the next one is scored.

NMC811: the jitter is now measured on the dev cells (scale 1.15 ± 0.09, 7.0 mV per coefficient; frozen set val_ocpd), but every jitter-trained network scores 0.713-0.718 on it, so rungs that read the dev cells better (n10: 114 mAh, n11: 91 mAh, vs n8's 126) cannot clear the 0.01 margin. Next: a frozen-set objective that separates them (e.g. more pairs, or scoring the jitter-free twin of each pair), decided before the rungs are re-judged.
NMC811: a two-material negative (graphite + SiOx) with its own silicon loss, for the features near the end of discharge.
NMC811: read the HPPC pulses in the same tests for resistance, and cut-short tests that start below full.
Multi-chemistry simulator and dev gate once the data is in.
Fix the late-life lifetime bias — feed the lifetime net the health net's capacity reading.
Electrode-scale heterogeneity to soften the staging features.

models.name: SwellCast
models.tagline: One buoy hears a storm thousands of kilometres away.
models.question: How far away was the storm whose swell is arriving at this buoy?
models.summary: From ten days of NOAA buoy wave spectra, SwellCast says whether storm swell is arriving, how far away the storm was, when it peaked and which way it lies. It is Munk's 1963 idea — long waves outrun short ones, so the arriving frequency rises linearly in time at a rate set by the distance — learned by a network from simulated storms laid onto real buoy records.

models.name: StarQuake
models.tagline: Weighing stars by listening to them ring.
models.question: How massive and how big is this red giant, from how it rings?
models.summary: From a Kepler light curve, StarQuake decides whether a red giant's solar-like oscillations are present, then reads where the oscillation hump peaks (νmax) and the spacing of its comb of modes (Δν), each with an error bar. With a temperature, scaling relations turn those into mass and radius. It was trained only on simulated stars laid into real light curves of quiet dwarfs. Since v1.1 a classical SYD-style reading is blended in where the two agree, by a weight that grows with the observing length (fitted on simulations).
models.reads: A Kepler long-cadence light curve (any length from 27 days to 4 years), plus an effective temperature for mass and radius.
returns: Oscillations detected (yes/no)
νmax and Δν (μHz), each with an error bar
Mass and radius (solar units) with error bars, via the scaling relations
models.network: Two CNN branches, 412k parameters — 1-D on the log spectrum, 2-D on a comb map (autocorrelation in units of the expected Δν); v1.1 blends the network's νmax and Δν with a classical SYD-style reading by length-dependent weights fitted on simulations
models.noise: Real Kepler light curves of 232 quiet dwarfs (training) and 42 (validation), after a variability screen

approach.real_backdrop: Kepler light curves of 232 quiet dwarf stars
approach.physics_inputs: A comb map: the autocorrelation in units of the expected Δν
approach.physics_anchor: v1.1: the classical SYD-style reading (background fit, smoothed excess, autocorrelation), blended with the network where they agree

wins: On light curves of 1 year and shorter it beats the classical pipeline (νmax 1.41 % vs 1.67 % at 1 year, 2.2 % vs 3.9 % at 90 days, 3.5 % vs 16.5 % at 27 days).
Finds 100% of giants from 27 days against 39.5% for the classical comb test.
losses: On 4-year light curves the classical pipeline still wins on the median νmax error (0.89 % vs 0.99 %), though v1.1 blends it in — and the truth catalogue was made with a similar pipeline.
The radius scatter against Gaia rose from 7.1 % (v1.0) to 8.1 %, level with Yu et al.'s radii.
Δν from 27 days is within 2% for only 23% of stars (often off by one comb tooth).
limits: Error bars too narrow on short pieces (1σ coverage 58–63% at 27 days) and too wide on whole light curves (81–84%): one widening factor per output, fitted on 18 dev stars over all lengths.
v1.1 runs the classical pipeline on every reading (up to a second on short pieces); the browser instrument shows the network stage only.
The blend weights were fitted on simulations, where the classical νmax reads about 0.7% low; on real stars it agrees with the truth catalogue, which the weights cannot know.
11–15% of unscreened dwarfs are falsely called oscillating.
The most luminous giants (νmax 8–15 μHz) read about 4% high; their twins show the same bias.
Kepler long cadence only; no TESS yet.

False detections (audit, 25 Nov 2026): unstructured Gaussian noise on a real Kepler cadence mask triggers the detector on 5 of 10 draws at 500 ppm and 10 of 10 at 1,000 ppm, the RMS range of real giants. Measured 27 Nov 2026 on 999 pieces of the 18 held-out high-RMS dwarfs that the noise screen dropped (spots, rotation, eclipses): 16.9% are called oscillating, against 6.1% of quiet dwarfs. A rung trained with such stars in the noise bank cut that to 11.1% but failed the ratchet (val3 +0.007, needs +0.01; dev errors +22%). Cadences without good flux at either end of a record lower the duty cycle and change the FFT grid (90 flagged days moved KIC 2695975 from 1.677 to 1.777 solar masses); since v1.1.1 grid_lc trims them by default (36 of 858 archived light curves, 22 of 420 exam stars, start or end on a gap).
next: Per-length σ widening, fitted on dev.
Make the simulator's νmax the one a SYD-style pipeline measures on the noiseless spectrum, so the blend weights learn the real classical reading.
A TESS version on quiet-star noise, examined on TESS giants.

Hard negatives without losing dev accuracy: r6 (27 Nov 2026) cut high-RMS false alarms from 16.9% to 11.1% but read the dev stars 22% worse. A warm start from the released network, or the hard bank as a fine-tuning stage, is the next rung.

physics.summary: Two super-Lorentzian granulation components, a Gaussian oscillation envelope, the universal red-giant mode pattern for l = 0–3 with dipole mixed modes, linewidths and stochastic excitation, generated by inverse FFT and added to real Kepler light curves of quiet dwarfs (which oscillate above Nyquist, so their light curves are pure real noise and real gaps).
checks: χ² statistics: mean 1.004, variance 1.001; Parseval ratio 0.988–0.990
A classical pipeline recovers 24 simulated stars' inputs to 1.4% (νmax) and 0.6% (Δν)
Reproduces Yu et al.'s 16,094 masses and radii (ratio 1.000)

models.name: EnergyNet
models.tagline: How much fuel or electricity will this trip take, before you drive it?
models.question: How much fuel or electricity will this trip take, and where does it go?
models.summary: EnergyNet predicts a trip's fuel or battery energy before the trip, with a 68% and 95% range and a split into air drag, rolling, braking, accessories and powertrain losses. It covers 7 vehicle classes from cars to Class-8 trucks and 7 powertrains. Version 2 learned only from RoadSim physics v2 driven over real Ann Arbor routes and weather (86,400 simulated trips), reads the vehicle's model year, and was examined on 25,793 real trips, EPA tests and 1,115 full Zurich bus missions. Version 2.1 runs the simulated A/C and cold tests under the EPA test conditions, drops idle-stop from the simulated petrol cars and reads two public specs (a hybrid's system, a bus's curb mass).
models.reads: A route at 1 Hz (speed, grade, temperature, wind, heading, air density, surface) and whatever is known about the vehicle (architecture, class, mass, road load, engine, battery, window-sticker label, start charge, model year); unknown fields are masked.
returns: Trip energy (MJ) with 68% and 95% ranges — fuel chemical energy, battery energy, or both for plug-ins
Split into aero, rolling, friction braking, accessories/HVAC and powertrain losses
models.network: Ensemble of 5 MLPs (151 → 256 → 256 → 256 → 128 → 7), predicting a correction to a physics energy estimate, its log σ and 5 energy components; Gaussian NLL; trained on a GPU
models.noise: Real routes and station weather; the simulated car drives slightly different conditions (temperature ± 1.5 °C, wind × 0.4–0.9) than the input reports

models.name: TripDetective
models.tagline: What car was this? Read it from one trip log.
models.question: From a trip log alone: what powertrain, how heavy, what engine, how much drag?
models.summary: TripDetective reads one or more 1 Hz trip logs of a light-duty vehicle — speed plus whatever an OBD logger has — and infers its architecture, total mass, engine size, CdA, rolling resistance, hybrid strategy and each trip's energy ledger, every output with an error bar. It learned only from the RoadSim simulator (physics v2) with an emulated OBD logger, and was graded on 350 real cars it never saw. Version 2.0 added a physics-regression head: the road-load fit of each trip is pooled over a car's trips and solved, so a heavier car reads heavier (+524 kg for +800 kg in simulation; v1.0 +182 kg). Version 2.1 adds a physics constraint (an engine that stops while the car moves is not a conventional one), which fixes the small hybrids, and reads a city bus's legs of one day together: the bus network follows passengers from leg to leg, not from day to day (ZTBus).
models.reads: One or more 1 Hz trip logs (speed, and when logged fuel rate, rpm, HV battery current/voltage/SOC, A/C power), with route grade and weather.
returns: Architecture (7 layouts) with probabilities
Total and curb mass, engine displacement, CdA, Crr — each with a 1σ range
Hybrid control strategy and engine-off share
Each trip's energy ledger in kJ/km (aero, rolling, grade, friction braking, powertrain losses, accessories)
models.network: 1-D CNN over each trip window (23 channels, incl. a source-power channel) plus 16 classical estimates; trip embeddings pooled across a car's trips together with the road-load regression's normal equations, which are solved per car (physics-regression head: mass = fitted b0 x a learned efficiency correction); heads for architecture, strategy and 7 regressions (Gaussian NLL); 0.40 M parameters. v2.1: an engine-stop constraint on the architecture output (rpm < 100 at v > 5 m/s on more than 5 % of moving seconds rules out a conventional car; threshold from simulation). A second, separately trained copy reads buses; v2.1 maps its reading day-relative (3 numbers fitted on ZTBus dev legs).
models.noise: Real routes and weather; the emulated logger reproduces real OBD cadences, holds, quantisation and MAF-based fuel estimates

approach.real_backdrop: Real VED and ZTBus routes and weather, through an emulated OBD logger
approach.physics_inputs: 16 classical per-trip estimates and the road-load regression's normal equations
approach.physics_anchor: Mass = the fitted road-load coefficient b0 × a learned efficiency correction; an engine that stops while moving rules out a conventional car

Missing data (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): the bus reader used to read missing power as zero and keep the leg in its bus-day, so one leg without power moved the other 13 legs of the packaged day by +239 kg each. It now reads only 1,024 s windows that are at least 90 % valid; a leg with none returns NaN and leaves the day's means. With half of the longest leg's power missing, that leg moves -101 kg and the others at most 30 kg (was -790 and +142 kg). No ZTBus exam leg has missing power (0 of 35.7 M samples), so the exam is unchanged. The car reader now refuses logs with under 60 s of motion (all-NaN or all-zero speed returned 1,182 kg, conventional).
ZTBus: the logged power and the logged traction force both regress to ~0.7 × (19 t + passengers), so the bus mass level is not verified; per leg the physics fit scatters ±15%.
The energy ledger has only simulated truth; no skill on net grade work.

models.name: HybridPilot
models.tagline: A learned hybrid controller, raced against the dynamic-programming optimum.
models.question: How should a hybrid run its engine, second by second? *(graded in simulation)*
models.summary: HybridPilot is a learned, causal energy-management policy for hybrids: every second it decides engine on/off and engine power, holding charge in hybrids and depleting-then-sustaining in plug-ins. It learned by imitating the dynamic-programming (DP) optimum inside the RoadSim simulator. Version 2.1 runs on RoadSim physics v3.1 (chosen on dev: closer engine starts and fuel on the dev twins), with a dead band on its SOC feedback and a fixed equivalence factor for buses and mild hybrids. Version 2.2 adds a charge-sustaining rule for plug-ins at their CS level and a weak SOC feedback for buses. It was examined on 432 trips — real VED routes driven by calibrated twins of the exam cars, bus legs and cycles — against rule-based control, ECMS, adaptive ECMS and MPC.
models.disclaimer: Graded inside the simulator. With HybridPilot driving the calibrated twins, simulated hybrid fuel is within 3.5 % of VED's logged fuel (exam trip median), but plug-ins read 20–31 % low, and the strategies differ by only 0.5–1.5 %, so the ranking holds only inside RoadSim's physics.
models.reads: The vehicle's parameters and, each second, the state (SOC, coolant temperature, timers, power limits), current demand (speed, acceleration, grade, wheel power), trip history and optionally a navigation preview.
returns: Engine on/off and engine power (series, power-split) or torque share (P2) every second
The resulting fuel, battery use and engine starts over the trip, compared against DP and the classical strategies
models.network: MLP 66 → 96 → 96 → 2 (15,938 parameters) predicting the equivalence factor s (buses and mild hybrids use a fixed s of 2.6–2.8 instead; plug-ins at their CS level use at least the HEV costate, 2.42 power-split / 2.70 series); the decision minimises fuel + s × battery power among RoadSim's candidate controls, with A-ECMS-style SOC feedback (Kp 12 beyond a ±0.03 dead band, Ki 0.02; plug-ins below CS Kp 24 without the band; buses Kp 3, no integral)
models.noise: Real routes, grades and weather; random start SOC, temperatures from −20 to 36 °C, warm and cold starts

approach.real_backdrop: Real VED and ZTBus routes, grades and weather
approach.physics_inputs: Wheel power demand from RoadSim's road-load model
approach.physics_anchor: Its output, the equivalence factor s, sets an ECMS cost over candidate controls scored by the powertrain model

exam.summary: 432 exam trips (430 trip ids, since two routes were drawn twice for the same generated vehicle), graded as % of the DP optimum (DP with the same 8 s / 3 s on/off timers) at matched final charge, on RoadSim physics v3.1. Real routes, simulated cars. Every baseline, v2.1 and v2.0 were re-scored on the same physics. v2.2 was run once, after its release choice was committed (48e9985). Earlier versions' numbers are in the notes.

rows.metric: All 432 trips, % of DP optimum
rows.note: Beats every causal baseline: +0.49 points over A-ECMS, 95% CI [−0.07, +0.98] (bootstrap by vehicle); +0.38 [+0.13, +0.64] over constant-s ECMS, which holds charge on only 75% of trips. Level with MPC, which sees 15 s of the future: 98.686 vs 98.665, +0.02 [−0.58, +0.54], so a tie, not a win. Holds charge on 93% of trips (A-ECMS 97%). Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 98.66 on 430, verdict mixed with MPC 0.01 higher). v2.1: 98.58 (published 98.57); v2.0 on physics v2 98.86 (published 98.84), a win; v2.0 re-scored on v3.1: 98.45.

rows.metric: Power-split hybrids (148 trips), % of DP
rows.note: +0.59 points [+0.42, +0.78] over A-ECMS, +0.20 [−0.02, +0.42] over constant-s ECMS. Holds charge on 93% (A-ECMS 97%, rule 93%, ECMS 72%). Same as v2.1 (v2.2 changes only plug-ins and buses). v2.0: 98.41 on physics v2.

rows.metric: P2 and series hybrids (64 trips), % of DP
rows.note: P2 +1.39 [+0.31, +3.29], series +0.88 [+0.57, +1.18] over A-ECMS. Holds charge on 94% (A-ECMS 92%; constant-s ECMS 59%). Same as v2.1. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 99.63 on 63 trips, A-ECMS 98.42). v2.0: 99.85 on physics v2 (published 99.84).

rows.metric: Mild P1 hybrids, CR-Z-type twins (56 trips), % of DP
rows.note: +1.08 [+0.79, +1.51] over A-ECMS, but holds charge on only 79% of trips (A-ECMS 96%; v2.0 re-scored on v3.1: 91%). Constant-s ECMS scores 0.21 higher (CI of the difference [−0.53, +0.10]) and holds charge on 34%. Unchanged from v2.1: a mild rule without the dead band was rejected on dev (R20). v2.0: 98.10 on physics v2 (holds 95%).

rows.metric: Plug-in hybrids (104 trips), % of DP
rows.note: Power-split plug-ins −0.91 [−4.51, +2.16], series plug-ins −0.73 [−1.78, −0.07] against A-ECMS; the charge-depleting rule 99.35. The v2.2 CS rule raised plug-in charge holding from 98 to 102 of 104 trips, not their fuel score. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 99.22 on 103 trips, A-ECMS 100.17). v2.1: 99.26 (published 99.25); v2.0: 99.33 on physics v2 (published 99.27; A-ECMS 99.56, published 99.59).

rows.metric: Hybrid buses (24 trips), % of DP
rows.note: Against constant-s ECMS: series buses 99.36 vs 98.30 (+1.06 [+0.86, +1.23]), P2 buses 99.66 vs 99.48 (+0.18 [−0.02, +0.42]). Against A-ECMS: series +3.87 [+2.00, +7.04], P2 +1.13 [+0.62, +1.47]. The cost: series buses hold charge on 9 of 12 trips (v2.1 12, ECMS 11); P2 buses 12 of 12. v2.1: 97.66, a loss to ECMS; v2.0: 97.50 on physics v2.

rows.metric: Charge held within its window (all trips)
rows.note: 401 of 432 trips (A-ECMS 420). v2.1: 400 (93%): v2.2 gains 4 plug-in trips and loses 3 series-bus trips; mild hybrids still 79%. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 399 of 430; A-ECMS 418). v2.0 on physics v2: 95% (A-ECMS 96%); v2.0 re-scored on v3.1: 96%.

rows.metric: Engine starts per km (all trips)
rows.note: v2.1: 3.0. v2.0: 4.0 vs 4.5 on physics v2 (v3.1's 2 s run-on into braking lowers starts for every strategy).

rows.metric: Against v2.1 re-scored on the same exam, % of DP
rows.note: +0.11 points [+0.01, +0.24] (series buses +2.88, P2 buses +0.83, plug-ins about +0.04; every other trip identical). Charge held on 401 vs 400 trips. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 98.66 vs 98.55; the gap between v2.1's published 98.57 and that re-score came from the same bug, not from RoadSim).

rows.metric: Against v2.0 re-scored on the same exam (v2.0 network and settings on physics v3.1), % of DP
rows.note: +0.23 points [+0.09, +0.41] (mild +0.44, buses +1.6 to +3.2), but holds charge on 93% of trips against v2.0's 96%. v2.1: +0.14. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 98.66 vs 98.43).

rows.metric: Against the v1 release re-scored on the same exam (v1 network and settings on physics v3.1), % of DP
rows.note: +0.12 points [−0.02, +0.31]; v1 holds charge on 91% of trips (v2.2 93%). v2.1: +0.03. v2.0 on physics v2: 98.86 vs 99.02 (published 98.84 vs 99.00), a loss. Corrected 15 Nov 2026: two duplicate trip ids were graded against each other's baselines; now all 432 trips are scored (was 98.66 vs 98.54).

rows.metric: Simulated vs logged fuel, calibrated twins driven by HybridPilot (exam, trip median)
rows.note: v2.2, the same as v2.1 on these cars: power-split HEVs +2.2% (168 trips, 56 cars), mild +2.3%, P2 +3.4% (5 trips); plug-in power-split −20.1%, plug-in series −30.9% (fuel + battery energy). Engine starts on power-splits 2.42 per km vs 1.94 real (v2.0 on physics v2: 3.65). Under the 8% target for hybrids, not for plug-ins.

wins: Beats every causal baseline on all 432 exam trips: 98.69% of the DP optimum against 98.20% for adaptive ECMS (+0.49 points, CI [−0.07, +0.98]), 98.31% for constant-s ECMS and 97.00% for rule-based control, and level with MPC, which sees 15 s of the future (98.67%).
Buses (v2.2): 99.51% of DP against 98.89% for constant-s ECMS and 97.01% for A-ECMS; series buses +1.06 points over ECMS.
Clear gains against A-ECMS on power-split hybrids (+0.59 points), P2 (+1.39), series hybrids (+0.88), mild hybrids (+1.08), series buses (+3.87) and P2 buses (+1.13).
Fewer engine starts than A-ECMS (3.0 vs 3.2 per km).

With HybridPilot driving them, the calibrated twins' fuel is within 3.5% of logged fuel for exam hybrids (trip median), and their engine starts are much closer to the real cars' than on physics v2 (2.4 vs 1.9 per km real; was 3.7).
losses: No clear margin over MPC, which sees 15 s of the future: 98.69% vs 98.67% overall, +0.02 [−0.58, +0.54].
Plug-ins: −0.91 points (power-split) and −0.73 (series) against A-ECMS.
Holds charge on 93% of trips against A-ECMS's 97% (v2.0 on the same exam: 96%); mild hybrids only 79%, series buses 75% (v2.2's weak bus feedback).
Mild hybrids: constant-s ECMS scores 98.57% against 98.36%, though it holds charge on only 34% of those trips.
limits: Graded in simulation; plug-ins on real roads read 20–31% low in RoadSim, and simulated power-split hybrids still start their engine more often than the real cars (2.4 vs 1.9 starts per km).

For buses and mild hybrids the network's s is not used: a fixed s (series bus 2.8, P2 bus 2.6, mild 2.8, fitted on 30 training-distribution simulations) with SOC feedback, which makes it an adaptive ECMS there (for buses a weak one, Kp 3).

RoadSim never runs the engine of a P2 or P1 hybrid at a stop, so on long stops the auxiliaries drain a mild hybrid's 0.6 kWh pack below its window whatever the controller does (a dev mild trip falls from 0.64 to 0.11–0.16).
The policy outputs no uncertainty; intervals are cluster-bootstrap intervals of paired differences.
DP ignores RoadSim's forced-on production rules (Toyota-type engine-on above 45 km/h, warm-up holds), so causal strategies cannot reach 100% on those cars.

Preview, a timed-DP teacher, a start penalty, a distance-to-go plug-in plan, a larger network, a re-teach on physics v3.1, a mild rule without the dead band and a stronger HEV feedback did not pass the ratchet.
next: Mild charge holding: a frozen mild stratum (the frozen set has none, so no mild rung can pass) and RoadSim engine-at-stop charging for P1/P2 hybrids; then a mild rule judged on it.
Charge holding on HEVs: Kp 18 reaches A-ECMS's frozen holding (96%) but costs 0.022 of frozen skill; a terminal term using the known trip length (nav) is untried.
A plug-in teacher conditioned on the trip-length uncertainty (nav known or not), and a dedicated plug-in frozen stratum.

Physics v2 → v3.1 decided on dev: HybridPilot v2.0 driving the dev twins, power-split fuel −4.6 → −2.4 % of the logs, engine-on gap −9.3 → −4.4 points, starts 3.67 → 2.66 per km (real 2.32)

audit.label: No-preview grade gap and optional preview boundary
audit.finding: RoadSim bidirectional grade interpolation across a 10 s gap flipped an earlier engine state and shifted earlier engine power up to `11.51 kW` (complete-grade controls: `0`); bounding the optional 30 s preview endpoint shifted fuel by `−0.273 g`. Second pass mapped `4` RoadSim consumers (`49` files) and showed full-trip `interp − ffill` divergence up to `+9.004 g` fuel (`1` flip, `10.23 kW`) on `VED_125_1275` and `+5.078 g` (`15.35 kW`) on `VED_428_465`.

resolutions.finding: RoadSim interpolates a grade gap from both sides, so a no-preview controller "sees" grade from after the gap
resolutions.text: RoadSim's `normalize_trip` is the plant's estimate of the road that exists at each second; a real car's inclinometer reads that current grade. A causal forward-fill would make the simulated road less accurate, not the controller more honest. More to the point, HybridPilot's sets (`training/sets.py`) apply `np.nan_to_num` to grade before RoadSim sees it, so the interpolation path never runs on its dev or exam cases.

models.name: GridPulse
models.tagline: How big was the trip, and how stiff is the grid, from one second of frequency at a time?
models.question: From the grid frequency after a trip: MW lost, inertia, and how low it will go
models.summary: GridPulse reads the 1 s grid frequency from 20 s before to up to 60 s after a sudden loss of generation. It returns the MW lost, the system inertia (GVA s), the frequency response (MW/Hz), and a forecast of the nadir and the frequency at 60 s from the first N seconds, each with a 1-sigma band. GB (50 Hz) and ERCOT (60 Hz) are a conditioned input, and so is transmission demand (optional). It learned only from 28,201 GridSim events laid into real quiet NESO frequency noise. It was examined on 412 real GB events (NESO 1 s data, 2018-2025) and, through a small summary head, on 292 ERCOT events from ERCOT's operations reports.
models.reads: 1 s grid frequency (Hz) from >= 60 s before to 60 s after a trip; the system (GB 50 Hz or ERCOT 60 Hz); optionally the transmission demand (MW); N, the seconds after the trip to use (2-60). GridPulse-Summary reads ERCOT report numbers: frequency drop (Hz), inertia (MW s), load (MW), renewable share.
returns: MW lost, with a 1-sigma band (dev-widened ×1.11)
System inertia (GVA s) with a 1-sigma band
Frequency response (MW/Hz, NERC point B), governor headroom and triggered FFR (weak; no real truth)
Forecast of the nadir (lowest frequency in 0-60 s) and of the frequency at 60 s, from the first N seconds, each with a 1-sigma band (settling ×1.28)
GridPulse-Summary (ERCOT reports): MW lost from the drop, inertia and load; the drop from the MW lost; inertia from the drop and loss
models.network: MLP 86 → 512 → 512 → 256 → 2×7 (Gaussian mean and log-sigma per target), GELU, 0.44 M parameters, Gaussian NLL, AdamW one-cycle, 120 epochs, re-augmented every epoch (phase, noise slice, N, demand dropped 25 % of the time); trained on CPU. GridPulse-Summary: three 4 → 64 → 64 → 2 MLPs on the ERCOT simulations.
models.noise: Real quiet NESO 1 s frequency: 56,090 slices of 140 s from 2018-07, 2020-07 and 2022-01, at least 1 h from any detected event (2022-01 days 21+ held for the frozen set). The simulated deviation is turned into 1 s means with a random sub-second phase and added to a slice; then griddata's onset rule picks the window, as on the real events. ERCOT noise = GB noise × 0.8-1.4 (no ERCOT 1 s data exist).

A better 30-60 s model (secondary response as droop plus delayed reserve) before trusting the 60 s forecast.

A wrapper (training/gpsim.py, version p1) rescales GridSim's generated fleets to real GB and ERCOT operating points and adds each grid's services.

models.name: BatteryPilot
models.tagline: When should a grid battery charge and discharge, knowing only the past?
models.question: When should a grid battery buy and sell, knowing only what is known before the hour?
models.summary: BatteryPilot is a causal dispatch policy for a 1 MW grid battery doing energy arbitrage. Before each hour it returns a value curve: the worth of one stored MWh at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % full. The battery uses that curve as its offer for the hour, cleared against the real-time price, with 85 % round trip and rainflow wear. v1.3 (shipped) is a hybrid: the rolling day-ahead optimiser's plan, written as a value curve, plus a small network's residual on it. It was trained only on simulated price paths (GridSim fleets, a scarcity model calibrated on dev years, and from v1.3 GridSim's real-time scarcity that the day-ahead market cannot see) and examined once per version on real ERCOT 2023-25 and CAISO 2024-25 prices. v1.3 earns 67 % (ERCOT) and 59 % (CAISO) of perfect hindsight net of wear: better than the daily-spread and threshold rules, worse than the rolling day-ahead optimiser (69 % and 68 %), and worse than v1.1 (68 % and 61 %) although it was better on the real dev years. It wins only with 4 h ERCOT batteries. v1.3.1 (27 Nov 2026) is the same network with the day-ahead plan's wear cost read from temperatures known at issue (48 h earlier) instead of realized ones; a dated re-score on every exam node-year moved the pooled shares by at most 0.05 points (ERCOT 67.1 %, CAISO 59.3 %).
models.reads: Hourly and causal: real-time prices of the last 24 h, day-ahead prices for the rest of today (and tomorrow after 14:00 local; 36 h, masked where not yet published), the RT-DA spread of the last 6 h, the balancing authority's day-ahead demand forecast for 24 h (EIA-930, relative to its 30-day max), the last temperature, hour, day of year, weekend, and the battery (duration, wear cost / price scale, price scale). Prices are scaled by the 7-day median DA price and squashed with asinh; 135 features. v1.3 also reads the day-ahead backbone curve at the 5 knots (a backward dynamic programme over the DA prices known before the hour; 140 inputs).
returns: Value curve λ(SOC): $/MWh of stored energy at 5 state-of-charge knots, strictly decreasing
Executed by the offer rule: discharge down to the SOC where λ = η_d (p − c_wear), charge up to where λ = p / η_c, within power and energy limits; cleared against the hour's RT price
Settled: gross revenue, rainflow wear cost, net revenue ($) and cycles; no error bar on the curve (the exam's intervals are on revenue, from a weekly block bootstrap)
models.network: v1.3: the day-ahead backbone curve (asinh of value / price scale at the 5 knots) plus an MLP residual, 140 → 128 → 128 → 5 (SiLU), 35,205 weights; each knot kept at least 0.01 below the one before (a strictly decreasing curve). v1.0/v1.1: MLP 135 → 128 → 128 → 5, 34,565 weights, top knot and 4 softplus steps. Trained by direct policy search: the battery physics (offer execution, limits, losses, linear wear) runs inside the loss in torch, maximising revenue + value of energy left − value at the start over 14-21-day windows, each divided by its own 2 h perfect-foresight value.
models.noise: Simulated real-time noise (Student-t, AR(1), scaled by net-load ramps) and real EIA-930 day-ahead demand-forecast errors laid on the simulated day-ahead; scenario randomisation of demand, renewables, storage, gas price, retirements and scarcity parameters

approach.physics_inputs: The battery's own wear cost (temperature-dependent linear proxy from the rainflow model) and duration; prices scaled by a causal 7-day median
approach.physics_anchor: v1.3: the network outputs a residual on the classical day-ahead backbone (the rolling optimiser's plan as a value curve). The curve feeds a physics executor: an offer rule with round-trip losses, power and energy limits, and rainflow wear; the battery physics sits inside the training loss

exam.summary: Share of perfect-hindsight revenue net of wear (each node-year and battery's net revenue divided by an annual LP on the same RT prices, then averaged), on real prices, run once per version with the released network. Every strategy settles at the hourly RT price with rainflow wear at the BA's temperature. DA optimiser = a rolling LP that re-plans at 14:00 with day-ahead prices as the forecast; spread rule and threshold rule are GridData's baselines (the threshold uses the node's dev-period RT quartiles). Revenue intervals come from a weekly block bootstrap (2,000 draws). The rows below are v1.3.1's: v1.3's network with the causal wear plan (default since 27 Nov 2026), from a dated supplementary re-score of all 48 node-years (training/rescore_causal.py; the network and every choice were fixed before it, and v1.3 as examined was re-run on the same rows: within $0.02/kW-yr of its exam). v1.3's own exam was run once after its release choice was committed; each note keeps v1.3's number, v1.0's first look and v1.1's second look (v1.1 re-scored on the same run: identical).

wins: 4 h ERCOT batteries: 0.786 vs 0.742 for the rolling day-ahead optimiser (v1.3.1; v1.3 0.785; beats it in 30 of 36 node-years; 2023 +$12.9/kW-yr, CI [+3.9, +24.7]; 2024 +$4.9, CI [+3.1, +6.6]).
Beats GridData's daily-spread rule (ERCOT 0.671 vs 0.561 of perfect hindsight) in 82 % of ERCOT node-year-battery cases, and the threshold rule in every case.
Cycles less: about 222 (ERCOT) and 215 (CAISO) cycles a year vs 301 and 282 for the optimiser; its worst month at the median node was −$0.07/kW (any node: −$0.09/kW, CAISO ZP26 December).
Trained without a single real price path: real dev years only calibrated the simulator and gated rungs; GridSim's RT scarcity was fitted on train-input-year prices.
losses: Loses to the classical rolling day-ahead optimiser on both pooled rows in every version: v1.3.1 ERCOT 0.671 vs 0.685, CAISO 0.593 vs 0.681 (v1.3 0.671 / 0.594, v1.0 0.667 / 0.642, v1.1 0.679 / 0.614).

v1.3 is worse than v1.1 on the exam (ERCOT 0.671 vs 0.679, CAISO 0.594 vs 0.614) although it was better on the real dev years (0.660 vs 0.638) and on the new frozen set (0.772 vs 0.735). The dev gain came from 2021 alone (Uri; 0.48-0.50 vs 0.37-0.38); on dev 2019 (0.77-0.78 vs 0.81-0.82) and CAISO 2023 (0.73 / 0.81 vs 0.78 / 0.84) it was already worse, as it is on the exam. The pooled dev gate let the Uri year decide.
1 h batteries lose clearly: ERCOT 0.548 vs 0.629 (7 of 36 node-years won); CAISO 0.483 vs 0.641, every node-year.
CAISO 4 h, a thin win for v1.0 (0.730 vs 0.723), is a loss for v1.1 (0.719) and v1.3 (0.718).

The simulator fix did not make the frozen set agree with dev in general: over 10 fixed policies the rank correlation fell from 0.67 (v4) to 0.43 (v6). On twins of dev 2019 the rolling DA optimiser captures 55-56 % vs 79 % real: physics 1.2 under-rates following the DA plan, where 1.1 over-rated it (90 %).
limits: Energy arbitrage only: hourly settlement (mean of the 15-min RT), no ancillary services, no 5-min prices, price taker; copper-plate simulator (no congestion, nodal differences untrained).

The CAISO-like family is hand-set from 5 dev months (Aug-Dec 2023) and is more volatile than real CAISO. GridSim's RT scarcity (physics 1.2) has no CAISO fit (no CAISO prices before Aug 2023), so CAISO paths have none of it.
Calibration hit grid edges again in v1.3 (σ 3,500 MW, the low end; cold f_max 0.55, the high end); dev-2019 twins carry $57/kW-yr of 2 h perfect-foresight value vs $103 real.
Wear parameters are assumptions from the literature; calendar ageing is not charged.

Exam leak in v1.0, fixed in v1.1: GridSim physics 1.0 took its coal, CC, CT and gas-steam outage shares from Texas RE's 2024/2025 reports (exam-period data). On the ERCOT 2019 fleet they took 14.8 GW of 74.1 GW of thermal capacity out on average, vs 10.8 GW with the pre-2023 rates of physics 1.1. v1.0's scarcity calibration absorbed most of the difference (ORDC μ −4,000 MW; on physics 1.1 the fit moves to μ 0 MW). For v1.1 the calibration, banks and frozen set were rebuilt and every rung retrained and re-decided.
The forced-outage rates of physics 1.1 and 1.2 are PJM class averages (demand-period EFORd), not ERCOT's own pre-2023 rates.
The exams have been seen: v1.3's exam was run once after its release choice was committed, and the dev-chosen v1.3 lost ground on it.
No error bar on the value curve itself; the exam's intervals are on revenue (weekly block bootstrap), so the recipe's coverage step does not apply.

Information boundary (audit, 25 Nov 2026): v1.3's day-ahead planner took its wear cost from realized temperatures for the coming hours, a perfect temperature forecast. v1.3.1 (27 Nov 2026) takes each hour's temperature from 48 h earlier, known when any plan covering that hour is made (plans run up to 33 h ahead); 48 h persistence is a crude temperature forecast, and the wear term is small, so the re-score moved each node-year-battery by -$0.26 to +$0.21/kW-year and the pooled shares by at most 0.05 points. v1.3's own exam used the realized form (run_policy(..., c_lin_plan=None) reproduces it). At the first hour of a path the price history clipped to that hour's own RT price; fixed 27 Nov 2026 (at most $0.02/kW-year on the exam).
help: CAISO OASIS serves only about 3 years (data from 2023-08): an archive of CAISO hub and DLAP prices for 2018-2022 would give the CAISO family real dev years, a GridSim RT scarcity fit for CAISO, and a longer exam.
Pre-2023 ERCOT forced-outage rates by technology (NERC GADS or Texas RE): GridSim physics 1.1 and 1.2 use PJM 2017-2021 class averages and one ERCOT-wide planned-outage factor from 2017.
ERCOT and CAISO ancillary-service clearing prices, and ERCOT resource-node prices in West Texas, to add ancillary services and a congestion basis.
Historical ERCOT day-ahead wind and solar forecasts (the RT scarcity process can only use the demand-forecast miss from EIA-930).
next: Fix what the dev twin test still shows: the rolling DA optimiser captures 55-56 % on 1.2 twins of dev 2019 vs 79 % real. Real unforecast spikes put 86 % of their value in the day's 3 dearest DA hours (2019), the simulator 57 %; and the simulated DA carries a scarcity premium in those hours that real RT often undercuts by more. Calibrate the size and placement until the twin captures of the LP, the backbone and the network all match real dev.
A dev gate that one year cannot carry (for example: no dev year worse by more than 0.01), decided before the next ladder: v1.3 passed the pooled gate on 2021 (Uri) alone and lost ground on the exam.
A 1 h specialist or a 15-minute execution head: every version loses to the day-ahead optimiser on 1 h batteries and in CAISO.
R9 (the hybrid on all 165 path-years) had the best dev score of any rung (0.685) but missed the margin on the frozen set by 0.004: a frozen set that agrees with dev would settle it.
Nodal basis: a West Texas congestion model; a real CAISO import and hydro supply curve; ancillary services.
Upstream to GridSim behind flags: the ORDC adder, the cold-outage curve, the gas-turbine ambient derate, the day-ahead price generator and the single-LP perfect-foresight baseline.
An issue-time day-ahead temperature forecast for the planner's wear cost instead of 48 h persistence (v1.3.1); the re-score says the wear term barely moves revenue, so this is low priority.

physics.summary: Battery: 1 MW grid side, usable energy = P × duration (5-95 % of nameplate), 85 % round trip (√ each way), wear by rainflow cycle counting (ASTM E1049) on a Wöhler depth curve (depth^1.3 / 6,000 per cycle) with LiFePO4 temperature and C-rate dependence (Wang et al. 2011) in an HVAC container, at $130/kWh nameplate. Prices: the shared GridSim fleet dispatch (physics 1.2 from BatteryPilot v1.3: 1.1 plus gridsim.market's real-time scarcity; 1.1 for v1.1) for the real ERCOT and CISO fleets of 2018, 2020 and 2022, wrapped by BatteryPilot's price simulator (training/pricesim.py) with a merit stack, scarcity and day-ahead prices.
checks: GridData's perfect-foresight, daily-spread and threshold baselines reproduced on 89 dev days at two hubs to 1e-13 $ (one spread day differs by $1.65 at HB_WEST: a price tie) (training/checks/battery_checks.json)
Rainflow counting matches the rainflow package exactly on 200 random series; executor energy balance 1.1e-16 MWh; rainflow wear of a summer-2019 PF schedule $2,414 vs the linear proxy $2,416

Uri 2021 (dev), v1.1: 158 and 150 simulated hours above $1,000 for two outage draws vs 153 real; 89-90 % of the real ones covered (training/checks/calibration_v1_1.json). v1.0: 180 and 166, 92-95 % (training/checks/calibration.json)
CAISO-like family vs real Aug-Dec 2023 (dev): hourly medians $18-25 midday and $59-61 evening vs real $21-25 and $66-72 (checked with physics 1.0; not re-checked on 1.1)

Day-ahead foresight on dev (training/checks/predictability_*.json): the DA price covers 31 % of the RT value of hours above $300 in real 2019 (13 % in 2021 without Uri); simulated twins 69-72 % (80 / 71 %) with physics 1.1, 60 % (14-37 %) with physics 1.2

Twin test with physics 1.2 (v1.1 network, training/checks/twin_r2_v4_p1_2.json): on twins of dev 2019 BatteryPilot captures 76-85 % (real 82 %, was 94 % on 1.1 twins), the backbone alone 64-78 % (real 67 %), but the rolling DA optimiser only 55-56 % (real 79 %, was 90 % on 1.1 twins): the simulator now under-rates following the DA plan

Does the frozen set rank policies like dev? (training/checks/agreement_v1_3*.json) Over each ladder's own rungs: v6 Spearman 0.77 with the same top two (R9, R11) as dev; v4 0.68 with a different best. Over 10 fixed policies (the v1.1 and v1.2-attempt networks, backbone, LP): v4 0.67, v6 0.43: worse

Twin test, v1.1: the policy captures 94 % of perfect foresight on simulated twins of dev 2019 but 82 % on real 2019; 2021 (with Uri) twins 71-75 % vs real 38 % (training/checks/twin_r2_v4.json). v1.0: 91-94 % vs 80 %; 64-68 % vs 38 % (training/checks/twin_r4_v3.json)

audit.label: Critical pre-hour leakage
audit.finding: Future temperature moves offers through planned wear (`$1.19/MWh`) and hour-0 history clipping leaks hour-0 RT price (`$3.02/MWh`); causal wear replay preserved rankings across three shipped node-years. Second pass verified zero dead rows, Torch↔NumPy parity (`<= 1.17e-6` on all three node-years), PyTorch seeding, and `9/9` rungs.

resolutions.finding: Day-ahead wear planner reads realized future temperatures
resolutions.text: Opt-in fix, re-score queued. `causal_wear(bat, T)` takes each hour's temperature from 48 h earlier; plans run up to 33 h ahead, so every plan reads only temperatures known when it is made (a first 24 h version still read up to 9 h ahead; Codex, PR #23). `run_policy(..., c_lin_plan=...)` uses it. Default stays as released, so the card's exam numbers remain what v1.3 does.

models.name: PlantDetective
models.tagline: A power unit's technology, heat rate, minimum load, ramps and starts from its output.
models.question: What is this power unit, and how flexibly does it run, from its hourly output?
models.summary: PlantDetective reads a fossil power unit's hourly output (MW) and infers its technology (coal steam, gas combined cycle, gas turbine, gas steam), full- and part-load heat rate, minimum stable load, ramps, minimum up and down times, starts per year and their hot/warm/cold shares, capacity factor and an operating-flexibility class, each with a 68% and 95% range. Prices and EIA-860/923 facts are optional inputs. It learned only from 1,829 simulated units (GridSim systems plus a self-commitment dynamic programme and a CAMPD measurement emulator) and was examined once on 395 real Texas CAMPD units. v1.1 predicts starts per year, minimum up time, median run and minimum down time as learned corrections to the statistic counted in the window itself; it was retrained on the simulated bank rebuilt with GridSim physics 1.1 and examined once more on the same 395 units.
models.reads: Hourly unit output in MW (gross, at least 30 days; NaN = missing) with UTC timestamps; optionally the hourly electricity price ($/MWh) and gas price ($/MMBtu), and EIA-860/923 facts (prime mover, CHP flag, nameplate, minimum load, cold-start time, online year, annual heat rate). Several years are read window by window and pooled.
returns: Technology probabilities: coal steam, gas combined cycle, gas turbine, gas steam
Full-load and part-load heat rate (MMBtu/MWh, CAMPD gross basis; part load = max(min stable load, 40%)) and the heat-rate curve
Minimum stable load (fraction of capacity), ramp up and down (99th percentile hourly change while running)
Starts per year and hot (< 8 h off) / warm (8-48 h) / cold (>= 48 h) shares; minimum up, median run and minimum down time (h)
Capacity factor and an operating-flexibility class (baseload, load-following, cycling, peaking; a rule on the estimates)
Every estimate with 68% and 95% ranges, widened by dev-fitted factors
v1.1: starts per year, minimum up, median run and minimum down time are the window's own counted statistic plus the network's correction (where the window has one)
models.network: Ensemble of 3 MLPs (171 inputs: 170 window features + a net-output flag -> 256 -> 256 -> 128 -> 4 technology logits + 13 means + 13 log sigma; leaky ReLU), 440,797 weights; Gaussian NLL + cross-entropy; variance = mean member variance + spread of member means; windows pooled by summed log-probabilities and precision-weighted means. v1.1: the means of starts per year, minimum up, median run and minimum down time are the counted statistic of the window plus the network output (count skips), in the transformed target space

physics.summary: Two layers of unit physics on the shared grid platform (shared/grid). GridSim generates power systems and dispatches them with a unit-level MILP driven by real EIA-930 demand, wind and solar shapes and Henry Hub gas of the train-input years. Each simulated unit then commits itself against a price background with an exact dynamic programme: on/off and time in state, 7 output levels, a convex fuel curve, hot/warm/cold start costs, minimum up and down times, ramp and start-up/shut-down limits, forced and planned outages. A measurement emulator turns the schedule into a CAMPD-like hourly record and an EIA-923-like annual heat rate.

Dev twin test, 40 dev units in 2019 and 2021 against their simulated twins: pattern mismatch 0.211 with bank v1, 0.128 with bank v2 (training/twin_v1.json, twin_v2.json)
GridSim's own physics checks are in shared/grid/checks/

models.name: DemandCast
models.tagline: Tomorrow's hourly electricity demand, wind and solar for a US grid, with error bars.
models.question: Tomorrow's hourly demand, wind and solar for a US grid?
models.summary: DemandCast forecasts the next day's 24 hourly values of electricity demand, wind output and solar output for 8 US balancing authorities (ERCOT, CAISO, PJM, MISO, SPP, ISO-NE, NYISO, BPA), each with a 95% band. The forecast is issued at 10:00 local standard time the day before, like a grid operator's own. Three small networks correct a building-stock heat-transfer model of demand and wind- and solar-farm physics on the real fleets, reading the last week of metered output against the physics. They learned only from 180,000 simulated region-days. v1.2 (27 Nov 2026) repairs inputs the simulator never varied (twilight solar, missing demand hours, 2 h solar offsets): solar is now 10.6% off against 19.1% for persistence (v1.1: 16.1%), but demand got worse. On 2023-2025 with the weather that actually happened (an upper bound) demand is 2.49% off against 3.41% for the grids' own forecasts (v1.1 2.38%); with real archived forecast weather 2024-2025 it is 3.14% against 3.59%, but 2.98% against 2.70% without CAISO and SPP, whose published forecasts are flawed.
models.reads: Weather for the target day and the past week (population-weighted temperature, humidity, irradiance; hub-height wind, temperature, pressure and humidity at the wind points; irradiance at the solar points), the calendar (DST-aware hour, weekday / Saturday / Sunday-holiday), the grid's dev-fitted building-stock parameters and real EIA-860 wind and solar fleet, and the last 168 h of metered EIA-930 demand, wind and solar before issue
returns: Hourly demand (MW) for the 24 hours of the next day, with a log-scale sigma (widened × 1.34 on dev) and a 95% band

Hourly wind and solar output as a capacity factor of the fleet online at issue (MW = CF × fleet MW), with sigma (wind × 1.00, solar × 1.12 on dev) and a 95% band; solar is 0 at night and is moved onto the reported clock (the reporting offset, -2 to +2 h, read at issue)
models.network: Three MLPs (two hidden layers of 512, SiLU), inputs standardised: demand 329 inputs / 456k parameters, wind 164 / 372k, solar 156 / 368k; Gaussian negative log-likelihood, AdamW, one-cycle LR, 40 epochs; numpy equals torch to 3e-7. v1.1 adds no learned parameters: before the solar network, a two-term least-squares fit of the 168 h reported-minus-physics error on the physics diurnal profile and its slope reads the reporting offset (-1, 0 or +1 h, counted from each grid's dev-year value); the history is put back on the physics clock and the forecast is moved by the offset. v1.2 (rung r10, 27 Nov 2026): the same three architectures retrained on 180,000 region-days of simulator v5 (base features, 40 epochs); offsets read up to ±2 h; the reported solar of the last 24 h is set to 0 at hours the physics calls dark before the network reads it; count-like inputs (flags, missing-hour fractions) have a standardisation floor of 0.05; standardised inputs are clipped at |z| 8
models.noise: Real residuals of building-model fits to each grid's demand in the training-input years 2018, 2020 and 2022 (whole days, local-hour aligned); wind and solar weather-error widths sized to the dev-year physics mismatch

approach.real_backdrop: Real 2018, 2020 and 2022 weather of the 8 grids (perturbed) and their real EIA-860 wind and solar fleets; demand noise is real residuals of building-model fits in those years
approach.physics_inputs: Building-stock demand components (base, lighting, heating, cooling, rooftop PV) for tomorrow and the past week; wind and solar fleet physics with its spread at ±10% wind and ±20% irradiance
approach.physics_anchor: Demand: predicts log(demand / building-stock physics); wind and solar: a correction added to the physics capacity factor

Wind: 19.3% against 22.7% for the physics alone and 43.5% for persistence; with real forecast weather 2024-2025 26.9% against 39.0% and 42.9%.

losses: v1.2 is worse than v1.1 on demand: 2.49% vs 2.38% with actual weather (v1.1.1 2.32%), 3.14% vs 3.05% with forecast weather 2024-2025. The dev gate showed it (dev demand 2.05% vs 1.98%, +3%), but the gate pools demand, wind and solar, and solar's dev gain (13.1% vs 15.7%) carried the rung.
With real forecast weather (2024) it loses to ERCOT, SPP, ISO-NE and BPA's own forecasts (ERCOT 3.38% vs 2.05%).

Second look with real forecast weather, 2024-2025: 3.14% vs 3.59% pooled, but without CAISO and SPP (flawed published forecasts) 2.98% vs the grids' 2.70%; behind ERCOT (3.56% vs 2.26%), ISO-NE (4.26% vs 2.65%) and BPA (2.43% vs 1.96%).
ERCOT (2.41% vs 2.40%), ISO-NE (3.32% vs 2.56%) and BPA (2.14% vs 2.00%) lose even with actual weather; ISO-NE's Jan 2025 cold snap 4.49% vs 1.27%.
Texas heat, Aug 2023: 2.08% vs ERCOT's 1.59%, with the peak 4% too high. Above 35 °C (1,211 h) 2.94% vs the grids' 2.55%.
Solar in SPP (27.0%) and BPA (20.8%) is still far worse than in the other grids, and CAISO beats persistence by only 0.2 points.
limits: The headline uses actual weather and is an upper bound. With real forecast weather DemandCast wins in 4 of 8 grids in 2024 (released) and 5 of 8 over 2024-2025 (second look); the pooled win rests on CAISO and SPP. The archive holds no humidity or radiation forecasts before 2024, so 2023 cannot be graded with forecast weather.

The pooled dev gate let solar decide: r10 passed with dev errors -4.8% (solar -16%, wind -1%, demand +3%), and the exam shows the same split. From 27 Nov 2026 the ladder uses a per-output dev gate (each output no more than 2% worse), an exam-informed rule change; it was not applied back to v1.2. Its first rung, r11 (v1.1.1's demand network with v1.2's wind and solar), passed that gate (dev demand 1.98% vs 2.05%) but was rejected on the frozen set (0.3973 vs 0.4054): val_v5's simulated history gaps favour v1.2's demand network, the real dev years do not.

Solar timestamps: v1.2 reads whole-hour offsets (-2 to +2 h) from the week before issue, counted from each grid's dev-year value. A change is picked up only once the week before issue shows it, and CAISO's dev-year error profile sits about half an hour off (r_hat 0.46), so some CAISO days near that boundary flip. On val_v5 the reader gets 80% of 2 h offsets right (32 of 40 at +2, 55 of 80 at -2), and a misread offset costs solar error.
Bands are too narrow on real data: demand 64% / 89% inside the 68% / 95% bands (CAISO 49% / 76%, ISO-NE 55% / 83%).
Wind is limited by 50 km reanalysis in complex terrain (BPA 50%, CAISO 32%); the network trims the physics error by about 15%.

It needs the last week of metered output: physics alone is about 5% off (load growth since 2019-21). Building parameters are effective (several fits sit on bounds), so the heating / cooling split is indicative.
Over-predicts heat-wave peaks by about 4%.

Inputs the simulator never varied (audit, 25 Nov 2026), repaired in v1.2: reported solar at hours the physics calls dark is now set to 0 before the network reads it (training and inference), simulator v5 adds twilight output, -2 to +2 h offsets and 1-48 h gaps in the demand history, count-like inputs have a standardisation floor of 0.05, and inputs are clipped at |z| 8 (from v1.1.1). In v1.1 the twilight input pinned two BPAT exam days at the 1.2 cap and missing demand hours reached |z| 286; on the 201 actual-weather exam rows with missing history hours demand error was 5.96% (v1.1) and 2.58% with the clip (v1.1.1).

The archive holds humidity, radiation and wind forecasts only from 2024 (temperature from 2022), so 2023 cannot be graded with forecast weather and the dev years 2019 and 2021 have no real forecast errors. Half-hour solar offsets (CAISO's dev reference sits at 0.46 h), and higher-resolution weather for wind in complex terrain (BPA, CAISO).

Upstream to GridSim: the building-stock demand model (1.7-3.0% cross-year on dev, replacing GridSim's demand regression) and the tabulated farm curve with fleet grouping; to GridData: flags for EIA-930 solar timestamp changes and negative night solar, and an archived forecast-weather table.

physics.summary: Demand is a building-stock thermal model (training/buildings.py): conductance × the stock-averaged hinge of a Normal thermostat spread around an envelope-lagged sol-air temperature (fast and slow RC response, internal and window gains, night setback), latent cooling load, resistance / heat-pump / non-electric heating and air conditioning with COPs that fall with outdoor temperature, occupancy schedules from the calendar, daylight lighting, a water-heating season term and rooftop PV (pvlib). Wind and solar are GridSim's farm physics on every EIA-860 farm with its real online dates: moist-air density, IEC density-equivalent speed, the pitch-regulated farm curve from specific power, losses, and pvlib with tracking and clipping per weather point.
checks: Envelope RC lag vs an ODE solver 3.2e-7 K; step response vs closed form 3.6e-15 K (training/checks/physics.json)
Stock-averaged thermostat hinge vs a 1e6-draw Monte Carlo 0.0035 K; degree-day limit exact (1,080,000 vs 1,080,000 MWh)
Specific humidity vs PsychroLib (ASHRAE formulas) 0.2% (T >= 0 °C); heat-pump COP 3.26 at 8.3 °C and 1.94 at -8.3 °C, AC COP 3.5 at 35 °C (typical rating points)
Tabulated wind farm curve vs GridSim's farm_curve: mean 0.0005 CF (max 0.038 away from the 25 m/s cut-out); GridSim wind and solar vs ERCOT EIA-930 (phase 1): hourly r 0.90 and 0.97-0.98
Dev calibration (2019, 2021): building model fitted per grid, in-sample 2.2-3.5% MAPE; twin test re-simulated each grid's dev year with the full simulator (training/checks/twin_r8_wide.json)

models.name: WakeNet
models.tagline: Who is stealing whose wind across a real farm — read as a directed graph.
models.question: How much power is each wind turbine losing to its neighbours' wakes?
models.summary: From a wind farm's turbine coordinates, hub heights, rotor power and thrust curves, mechanical yaw orientations, online flags, and the upstream wind measured on its unwaked front row, WakeNet predicts every downstream turbine's waked power ratio, power loss (kW and %), rotor-effective wind speed and farm-wide wake loss, each with a 68% error bar. It learned only from 24,000 procedural 5-to-16-turbine simulations laid into real unwaked turbulence from Sep 2017 – Dec 2018. It was examined on real 10-minute SCADA from two UK wind farms, one never used for anything else: 24,035 snapshots in 2019–2021, then 35,592 snapshots from 2021–2024 that no version had seen. It beats textbook FLORIS everywhere, but the same physics tuned on one year of the farm's own data (no network) does as well or better on 17 of 18 rows of a second, never-seen exam.
models.reads: Turbine coordinates (East, North, ground elevation in m), hub heights (m), rotor diameter and nominal P(U)/Ct(U) curves, each unit's online flag and mechanical nacelle yaw offset (deg), and upstream freestream wind speed (m/s), wind direction (deg), turbulence intensity, 10-min wind-direction standard deviation (deg), air density (kg/m3) and front-row mean power (kW) measured on the geometrically unwaked front row. Downstream wind speeds, vanes and power meters are never read.
returns: Per-turbine waked power ratio P_i / P_front and wake loss (%) ± 68% bar
Per-turbine active power (kW) ± 68% bar and rotor-effective wind speed (m/s)
Farm-wide wake loss (%) and total waked output (MW) ± 68% bar
models.network: EdgeWakeGNN — directed 3-layer edge-conditioned graph neural network (hidden 96, 245,767 parameters) with additive sigmoid-gated wake superposition over upstream-to-downstream edges (dx/D, dy/D, dz/D, dimensionless meandering number σ_θ·dx/D, pairwise deficit, yaw), predicting a residual correction to the steady 3-D Gaussian wake anchor; trained with β-NLL (β = 0.5) + Huber loss on 24,000 v3 farms
models.noise: 47,610 real unwaked front-row rotor readings from Kelmarsh Sep 2017 – Dec 2018 (10.1% spatial turbulent power spread, 4.7% spatial wind spread, 4.9° nacelle yaw-tracking jitter, and empirical UK inflow tuples; 2016 excluded due to a ~1,680 kW commissioning export cap)

approach.real_backdrop: 47,610 unwaked front-row rotor readings and inflow tuples from Kelmarsh Sep 2017 – Dec 2018
approach.physics_inputs: Wind-rotated pairwise displacements (dx/D, dy/D, dz/D), dimensionless meandering number σ_θ·dx/D, analytical pairwise deficit and overlap, and finite-difference directional sensitivity
approach.physics_anchor: Predicts a residual power-ratio correction on top of a 3-D Bastankhah–Porté-Agel Gaussian wake and Crespo–Hernández turbulence solve

exam.summary: Mean absolute error in each waked turbine's power (as a share of the unwaked front row's power) and in farm-wide wake loss, on exam 2: years no version has seen. Every row gives WakeNet minus the best baseline with a 95% interval from a bootstrap over days; win or loss only when the interval excludes zero. Each note also gives the re-scored exam 1 result.

wins: Beats textbook NREL FLORIS and Jensen on every row of both exams and both farms: exam 2 Kelmarsh waked turbines 10.96% against 11.77% (FLORIS) and 11.92% (Jensen, k = 0.075); unseen Penmanshiel 19.78% against 21.75% and 21.77%.
Directly behind another turbine it beats even the dev-tuned physics, on both exams: Kelmarsh 2022-24 13.15% against 13.32%, −0.17 points [−0.26, −0.07]; exam 1 −0.13 [−0.23, −0.04].

Separating meso-scale wind-direction meandering (~0.25 × nacelle-vane σ_θ) from blade-passage vane flutter, plus 3-D hill speedup, cut Kelmarsh dev waked MAE from 10.12% to 9.48% (smearing wakes by the full vane spread made it 11.24% and was rejected).
losses: The network adds nothing over its own physics once that physics is tuned on dev. FLORIS with the three settings from 2019 dev beats WakeNet on 13 of 18 exam-2 rows and ties 4 (exam 1: 17 of 18). The gains over textbook FLORIS came from the dev tuning, not from the graph network. Anchoring the network on the tuned physics (r9) gained only +0.002 in simulation and was rejected.

On the unseen Penmanshiel ridge it loses to constant guesses: directly behind another turbine (25.12% against 20.60% for the dev-mean wake loss), inside 2 or more wakes, below 10 m/s, and on the highest quarter of turbines (22.64% against 19.33% for assuming no wake). Ridge-top speed-up offsets the wakes there.
limits: Error bars still too narrow on the unseen ridge farm: v1.0.1's per-wind-speed factors (fitted on dev) lift 68% coverage on Kelmarsh 2022-24 turbines from 64% to 70%, but Penmanshiel 2021-23 only from 42% to 49%, because terrain, not wind speed, drives the misses there. Both exams were seen before this change.
Below-rated active wake regime only (freestream 5.0–12.0 m/s); above rated wind speed pitch control caps all turbines at rated power and wakes cause near-zero power loss.
10-minute nacelle SCADA carries no atmospheric stability (Obukhov length / heat-flux) measurement, so convective daytime mixing and stable nocturnal wakes share one turbulence-conditioned curve.
No digital elevation map or forestry roughness map around the farm perimeter is read — terrain enters only through the elevations at the turbine towers themselves.

Demo summary (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): the demo's summary scored only the six turbines shown per snapshot (24 of 31 waked readings), where WakeNet led tuned physics 14.04 to 14.29; over all 31, as the exam scores, it is 14.90 to 14.43. The summary now uses all 31; the exam was already right.
next: Give the simulator physics the anchor does not have, so the network has something real to learn. The dev twin test found the network's corrections uncorrelated with real residuals (r = −0.04); those residuals follow wind speed and turbulence. Tuning FLORIS settings captures little of it (thrust ×0.90: 9.31 → 9.25%), so candidates are wake recovery that depends on turbulence and thrust beyond the Gaussian model, and turbine-to-turbine power-curve scatter.

A cleaner exam metric for the next fresh exam (Kelmarsh 2025 when published): per-turbine 10-minute power is dominated by ~10% turbulent scatter, so every model sits near a 9% floor. Bin-averaged wake deficit by wind direction, the industry's standard check, would show model differences the noise hides. Fix it before that exam is opened.
Read surrounding 30 m DEM terrain slopes and forest-canopy roughness upwind of each sector (Jackson–Hunt / WAsP linearised flow over real topography) to close Penmanshiel's hilltop bias.
Terrain-relief-conditioned or Mondrian conformal σ widening so error bars widen on steep (>30 m relief) sites and later years.
Active yaw-steering controller rung (WakePilot) trained through the differentiable wake graph and checked against dedicated field yaw-offset campaigns.

physics.summary: Sequential 3-D upwind-to-downwind wake propagation on a 3×3 rotor grid: Bastankhah & Porté-Agel (2014, 2016) near- and far-wake anisotropic Gaussian velocity deficit and yaw skew deflection, Crespo & Hernández (1996) wake-added turbulence weighted by rotor overlap, sum-of-squares deficit superposition, power-law vertical wind shear across mixed tower heights, and two real-farm effects calibrated on 2019 dev twins: meso-scale wind-direction meandering separated from rotor-induced nacelle-vane flutter, and 3-D hill exposure speedup.
checks: Bastankhah–Porté-Agel 3-D Gaussian single-wake grid (3D–15D × −1.5D..+1.5D) vs NREL FLORIS 4.7: max relative power diff 1.58e-15 (training/physics_check.json)
Jensen top-hat + Jiménez yaw deflection (−20°..+20°) vs NREL FLORIS 4.7: max relative power diff 2.91e-16
3-turbine Gaussian yaw-steering sweep (−25°..+25°) + Crespo–Hernández TI + SOSFS vs NREL FLORIS 4.7: max relative power diff 1.88e-15 (optimal yaw +25°, +12.36% gain)
14-turbine Penmanshiel layout × 72 wind directions (1,008 turbine states) vs NREL FLORIS 4.7: correlation 1.000000, max relative power diff 7.37e-15
Exact +37.5° compass rotational equivariance and parked-turbine removal equivalence: < 1e-12 kW

models.name: LoadCast
models.tagline: Hourly energy per building meter from weather, calendar and metadata, with 90 % bands
models.question: A building's hourly energy per meter for next year
models.summary: LoadCast forecasts a non-residential building's hourly energy on one meter (electricity, chilled water, steam, hot water or gas) for any span of hours, from weather, the local calendar and what is known about the building, with a 90 % band for every hour. Cold mode reads metadata only (use, floor area, which meters exist, climate); warm mode also reads 2 weeks, 8 weeks or a year of the meter's own history and corrects a time-of-week-and-temperature (TOWT) model fitted on it. It learned only from 1,600 BuildingSim buildings simulated under the real 2016-17 weather of the 19 BDG2 sites, with real dev-meter residuals added as noise. It was examined once on 1,502 real BDG2 exam building-meters, forecasting local 2017 from 2016.
models.reads: Hourly UTC weather (T_out °C, dewpoint °C, GHI W/m², wind m/s) over the forecast window, the history window and 7 days before each; time zone and latitude (holidays for the US, Canada, UK and Ireland); use type (10 classes), floor area (m²), optional year built, the meter type and which meters the building has, optional HVAC class and operating hours; optionally the meter's own hourly kWh history (warm mode).
returns: Hourly mean load (kW) on the chosen meter for any span of hours

A 90 % band (lo90, hi90) and sigma for every hour, widened by one dev-fitted factor per mode, history length and meter type (×1.0 to ×7.75; ×30, the cap, for 2-week chilled water and gas); raw bands with calibrated=False
models.network: Two MLPs, cold (64 inputs) and warm (83 inputs): 3 hidden layers of 192 SiLU units, dropout 0.1, Gaussian head (mean, log sigma); 177,604 parameters (cold 86,978, warm 90,626). Inputs per hour: 38 metadata, 10 weather and 16 calendar features; warm adds 19 history features (TOWT and change-point predictions from the history, time-of-week profile, history level and shape statistics). Cold predicts kW / (A × I_ref), warm kW / history mean. Loss: weighted MSE on the mean (weight 1 / ybar², floored) + 0.1 × Gaussian NLL for sigma; AdamW, cosine schedule, 30 epochs of fresh random hours, per-row metadata jitter (log area ±0.1, year ±6, climate ±0.5 K / ±8 %).
models.noise: Real noise from 85 BDG2 dev building-meters with good data in both years: the hourly residual of an in-sample regression (TOWT + 24 h mean temperature + dewpoint + solar), divided by the year mean — occupancy, campus breaks, events, meter quirks. One residual series is added to each simulated meter on the same local calendar dates, with a real 2017/2016 level change (whole year or a step), occasional quantisation and the real gap pattern. The bank holds the dev buildings' 2017 residuals too.

approach.real_backdrop: Real hourly residuals of 85 BDG2 dev building-meters, added to every simulated meter on the same calendar dates with real level changes and gaps; the simulated buildings run on the 19 BDG2 sites' real 2016-17 weather

exam.summary: Every BDG2 exam building-meter, forecast for local 2017 with the actual 2017 weather from 2016. Taken once after R3 was chosen; re-scored on 17 Nov 2026 with the released weights (seen: it reproduces to 5e-6, and nothing was chosen from it). Each row is a meter type and a history length; daily and monthly rows score daily and monthly totals. Baselines on the same meters: TOWT and a G14 change-point model fitted on 2016 (BuildingData), LoadCast's own ridge TOWT on the same history, the BuildingSim twin calibrated on the 52 dev buildings and run from each exam building's metadata, and two dev-fitted guesses. Median CV(RMSE) (ASHRAE Guideline 14), all with p = 0 (BuildingData's n − p converted). Verdict from a 95 % paired bootstrap interval over building-meters (2,000 resamples) on LoadCast minus the best baseline: 6 wins, 16 ties, 18 losses. v1.0.1 (27 Nov 2026) adds the electricity meter to a meter list that lacks one; re-scored on the seen exam it changes 19 chilled-water, steam and gas building-meters (15 buildings), moves the chilled-water and steam medians 0.1-3.3 points down and changes no verdict (still 6, 16, 18).
