wins: With 2 or 8 weeks of history it beats TOWT fitted on the same weeks on electricity (30.1 vs 36.5 % and 23.8 vs 26.2 %, 856 meters), and with 8 weeks on chilled water (62.6 vs 68.1 %) and hot water (86.5 vs 106.8 %); the intervals exclude zero.
Daily totals with a year of history, electricity: 14.1 % against 14.5 % for its own TOWT anchor and 17.1 % for the change-point model (interval −0.9 to −0.1 points).
Its error bars: the 90 % band covers 88-92 % of hours with a year of history on electricity, chilled water, steam and hot water, and 81-90 % with no history on every meter type but gas (74 %).
losses: A year of history is a tie on electricity (18.8 vs 19.1 % for the change-point model, interval −0.8 to +0.1) and chilled water (42.9 vs 42.4 %), and a loss on steam (45.5 vs 39.4 % for TOWT) and hot water (94.5 vs 80.5 % for its own ridge TOWT anchor). The v1.0 card called the electricity row a win.

With no history it loses to the BuildingSim twin calibrated on dev on electricity (59.3 vs 52.4 %) and chilled water (104.1 vs 85.8 %), and ties it on steam, hot water and gas. The v1.0 card called steam, hot water and gas wins against the median guess; the calibrated physics alone is better than or as good as the network on every meter type.
Monthly totals with a year of history lose on chilled water, steam, hot water and gas to the change-point model (e.g. steam 29.2 vs 20.0 %); electricity is a tie (9.5 vs 9.3 %).
Two weeks of December history cannot forecast summer chilled water: CV 87.3 %, no better than the calibrated twin with no history (85.8 %); the dev widening for that case hit its ×30 cap.
Not a nowcaster: yesterday's real reading (18.6 % on electricity) is as good as any 2016-based forecast.
limits: Non-residential campus buildings at BDG2's 19 sites, trained under their 2016-17 weather; other climates, years and residential buildings are extrapolation.
BuildingSim is single zone and its campus district energy runs about 3× low; 52 dev buildings' a, b calibration closes only part of that gap, empirically rather than physically.
The CV²-weighted loss pulls unknown magnitudes low; R4 tried a median-aimed weight and failed both tests.

The dev set is small: 5 hot water and 2 gas meters. The noise bank holds the dev buildings' 2017 residuals, but that leak is too small to measure: retraining the R3 recipe with only 2016 residuals moved the dev score by −0.1 points (95 % CI −2.7 to +2.7) and the seen exam by −0.9, against 1.8 (dev) and 2.7 (exam) points between two training seeds. The released R3 dev score (49.2) is 2.8-4.6 points better than two retrains of its own recipe (52.0, 53.8) while its exam score (52.8) sits between theirs (51.2, 53.8). R3 scores 3.6 points better on dev than on the exam; the retrains score 0.0 and 0.9 points worse. Picking the best rung on a noisy dev gate, not the residual leak, made the released dev number optimistic, by about 4 points.
Short-history modes were trained on year-end histories; 2-week and 8-week bands are unusable for chilled water and gas when the history is winter.
BDG2 timestamps were mixed (local DST vs standard) and are fixed to UTC; Peacock's weather does not match its stated location; four sites were located by temperature matching.

Buildings without an electricity meter (audit, 25 Nov 2026): every training building had one (has_electricity: mean 1, sd 0.001). A meter list without it puts that input at z = -1000; on two packaged buildings cold forecasts rose 24-50x in every hour. 58 of the 1,584 exam buildings list no electricity meter; 19 of their meters (15 buildings) are exam building-meters and were scored that way. v1.0.1 (27 Nov 2026) adds the meter by default (assume_electricity=True). On those 19, median cold CV(RMSE) fell from 597 % to 114 % and warm (a year) from 51 % to 35 % (cold better on 18 of 19, warm on 15; 13 cold forecasts stay above 100 %, as cold steam and chilled water do across the exam). The network still cannot say 'this building has no electricity meter'.
help: An EnergyPlus binary for a true reference engine: there is no PyPI wheel with an engine and GitHub was blocked in the build sandbox, so BESTEST ranges and ResStock/ComStock twins stand in.
The official ASHRAE Standard 140 (BESTEST) result tables: BuildingSim's ranges were transcribed from the literature.
A residential exam: large open smart-meter sets (IDEAL homes, Low Carbon London) are open but were skipped for size.
More campus thermal meters with plant metadata (which plant serves which building, seasonal shutdowns): the dev set has 5 hot water and 2 gas meters.
next: Twin anchor with a median-aimed loss: round 2 tried the twin anchor (r8) and a median-aimed magnitude head (r7) separately and kept neither; r8's CV²-weighted loss pulled the twin's level down again (dev no-history CV 78 % against 65 % for the twin alone), r7 fixed the level (dev 71 %) without the twin. The combination is the next rung; at inference it needs the twin as an input, not BuildingSim inside the numpy module.
Twin physics the residuals point at: a stronger weekday / weekend swing for campus electricity than the 24-7 calibration gives, and a sharper winter peak for heating meters.
A heating-meter physics rung: seasonal plant shutdowns, steam distribution losses, plants serving several buildings.
Warm mode trained on 4-12 week histories from every season, falling back to cold when the history is out of season.

The dev gate compares 3-seed means with the released R3's single selected seed (49.2; its own recipe retrained averages 53.3), so no rung of round 2 could pass it without a 3-point real gain; rebase the gate on the control's mean before the next round (a rule change, to be logged as one).

Upstream to BuildingSim behind flags: the US/CA/UK/IE holiday calendars, the BDG2-style spec maker, campus defaults (24/7 in 22 of 52, outdoor air ×2.5, VAV minimum flow), a per-meter district scale and base load, and a bounded-memory mode for long bank runs.

A representation that can say 'no electricity meter' (simulated buildings whose meter list lacks one). Not run on 27 Nov 2026: the frozen set v2_val has no such building, so the ratchet cannot score the change, and a 3-seed rung costs about 4 hours; it needs a frozen set with such meter lists first (a rule change for the owner).

physics.summary: The shared BuildingSim simulator (ML Ratchet building platform, Phase 1): an ISO 13790 5R1C single-zone heat balance with multinode walls, solar gains (pvlib), infiltration, ventilation and moisture; DX, heat-pump, chiller (DOE-2 EIR), boiler and district plants; VAV and unitary air sides; domestic hot water; driven by real weather. LoadCast's wrappers (training/lcsim.py, no edit to the shared package) add country holiday calendars, a BDG2-style spec maker (the meters a building has decide its plant), operating knobs and a per-meter calibration y = a·sim + b·A fitted on the dev buildings.
checks: BuildingSim Phase 1: steady conduction vs closed form to 1.8e-9; RC step response within 0.0035 K; degree-day ratio 0.999996; ISO 13786 wall amplitude −1.6 %, lag −0.01 h; every energy ledger closes to 1e-8
BESTEST: 29 of 34 values inside the published ranges, all 20 annual heating and cooling values in (ranges transcribed from the literature, not the official ASHRAE 140 tables)

models.name: BuildingDetective
models.tagline: What kind of building is this, from its meters and the weather?
models.question: From meters and weather: floor area, systems, envelope, use *(no real row beats dev-fitted baselines)*
models.summary: BuildingDetective reads a building's meters (electricity, on-site fuel, district heat, district chilled water) and the outdoor weather at one of three resolutions: a year of hourly data, 12 monthly bills, or one annual total per fuel. It returns floor area, year built, envelope conductance UA (W/K and W/m²K), thermal time constant, heating and cooling balance points, heating and cooling energy per kelvin, non-HVAC share, weekday operating hours and weekend ratio, each with a 1-sigma bar, and probabilities for primary use (12 classes), heating system (heat pump, resistance, fuel, district, none) and cooling system (none, DX, chiller, district). It learned only from 12,000 BuildingSim buildings on real 2016-17 weather with emulated meter faults, and was examined once on 1,428 real BDG2 buildings, 7,401 RECS homes, 2,558 CBECS buildings and 24 HUE homes.
models.disclaimer: Research model, not an energy audit. On real buildings it wins no exam row against the strongest classical baselines fitted on the same dev data: 21 losses and 7 ties (re-scored 17 Nov 2026 with 95 % intervals). It beats the simple meter rules for the heating system, but a logistic model fitted on the dev surveys does better; it loses on primary use (11 % right against 40 % for the majority class), has no skill on year built, and envelope UA and time constant have no real truth at all.
models.reads: Hourly: up to a year (30 days minimum) of hourly mean kW per meter (elec, fuel, dheat, dcool; NaN for missing hours, hour-beginning), outdoor temperature (°C), global horizontal irradiance (W/m²), the local time of each hour and the latitude. Monthly: 12 monthly mean kW per meter plus monthly mean temperature and heating/cooling degree days per day (base 18.33 °C). Annual: kWh per year per fuel plus annual heating and cooling degree days (base 18.33 °C).
returns: Floor area (m²) and year built, each with a 1-sigma bar widened on real dev buildings (hourly area ×3.0, monthly ×1.54, annual ×1.08)

Envelope UA (W/K and W/m²K), thermal time constant (h), heating and cooling balance points (°C), site heating and cooling energy per kelvin (W/K), non-HVAC share of site energy: 1-sigma bars widened on the simulated twins of the 52 BDG2 dev buildings (no real truth exists)
Weekday operating hours (h/day) and weekend/weekday ratio, commercial only (no real hourly truth)
Probabilities: primary use (12 classes, dev-fitted temperature 10 for hourly and monthly, 7.4 annual, which flattens them on purpose), heating system (5 classes) and cooling system (4 classes)
models.network: Three MLPs, one per input resolution, each 2 × 256 GELU with a Gaussian head (mean and log-sigma) for 12 regression targets (missing labels masked) and three softmax heads; trained with heteroscedastic NLL plus cross-entropy on simulations only. Hourly: 1,199 engineered features (daily load in 19 temperature bins for weekdays and weekends, the 168-hour week profile, cold- and hot-day profiles, a PRISM 5-parameter change-point fit, correlations with exponentially smoothed temperature at 6 time constants, hourly lag correlations, robust statistics), 0.38 M parameters (384,557). Monthly: 112 features, 106,285 parameters. Annual: 12 features, 80,685 parameters.
models.noise: Synthetic meter faults modelled on the BDG2 quirks BuildingData documents (gaps, zero runs, spikes, level shifts, clock offsets, Gator-style daily-spread readings, shared loads, scale errors, AR(1) and day-level multiplicative noise; features.quirk_hourly / quirk_monthly / quirk_annual). No real meter residuals are added; the simulated buildings run in real hourly weather.

approach.real_backdrop: Real hourly 2016-17 weather of 18 BDG2 sites (and TMYx typical years) that every simulated building runs in
approach.physics_inputs: A PRISM 5-parameter change-point fit (base load, heating and cooling slopes, balance points), degree days and daily-temperature bins computed from the meters and the weather

exam.short: 1,428 BDG2 buildings, 7,401 RECS homes, 2,558 CBECS buildings, 24 HUE homes
exam.summary: Real truth only where it exists: floor area, use, year built and which meters exist for BDG2 (2017 meters), survey answers for RECS and CBECS (annual totals), the heating type of HUE homes. Baselines marked TRUE are given the true use type, which the Detective is not. Envelope UA, time constant and balance points have no real truth; their rows are simulator-only (held-out BuildingSim buildings, or EnergyPlus ResStock/ComStock meters graded against a BuildingSim twin) and are info. The real rows were re-scored on 17 Nov 2026 with the released weights (the exam is seen: nothing was chosen from it) against fair baselines fitted on dev only (the 52 BDG2, 1,848 RECS and 661 CBECS dev units the simulator was tuned on): dev-fitted lines and logistic models on the same 12 annual numbers the network gets, a dev site prior, a dev week-profile centroid, and a PRISM change-point reading for HUE. Verdict: 95 % bootstrap interval on Detective minus the best baseline (2,000 resamples of buildings, homes or respondents, seed 20261117): win if it excludes zero on the good side, loss on the bad side, tie if it spans zero. The best baseline is sometimes given the TRUE use or type; the note then gives the interval against the best one that is not. Simulator rows were not re-run (they need the 60-shard bank).

wins: No real exam row is a win against the strongest dev-fitted baseline (re-scored 17 Nov 2026, 95 % intervals): 21 losses, 7 ties.

Against the simple rules v1.0 used it does win: heating system from annual totals, RECS 87.3 % against 85.3 % for 'any fuel used → fuel' (+2.0 points [+1.2, +2.8]) and CBECS 74.7 % against 68.6 % (+6.1 [+4.6, +7.6]); floor area from monthly or annual BDG2 input against electricity ÷ dev EUI of the TRUE use (−4.4 [−8.5, −0.4] and −5.9 [−9.3, −2.5] points); meters and chillers well above chance (AUC 0.70-0.77).
In simulation it reads the envelope: UA within 0.10 log10 against 0.85 for PRISM, balance points within 2.1-2.2 K against 4.9-6.5 K.
losses: A dev-fitted model on the same 12 annual numbers beats it almost everywhere: RECS heating 91.9 % vs 87.3 %, CBECS heating 79.2 % vs 74.7 %, CBECS use 28.4 % vs 16.5 %, CBECS chiller AUC 0.80 vs 0.77, RECS heat pump vs resistance AUC 0.63 vs 0.40, RECS area 29.6 % vs 33.6 %, CBECS hours 37 h vs 44 h. All these intervals exclude zero.

BDG2 floor area: a two-parameter line fitted on the 52 dev buildings (log10 A = 0.73 log10 kWh − 0.49, no use given) reaches 40.9 % against the Detective's 45.6-49.7 % on the same 1,364 buildings; v1.0's three 'ties' are losses.
Which meters a campus building has: the share of dev buildings at the same site with that meter gives AUC 0.83 against the Detective's 0.75 (chilled water) and 0.70 (steam / hot water).

Primary use does not transfer: 11 % right on BDG2 against 40 % for always guessing education and 31 % for the nearest dev week-profile centroid (simulated: 88 %); 16 % on CBECS against 21 % for the majority class.
Year built has no real skill: BDG2 28 yr (hourly) against 25 yr for the dev median; RECS 22.1 vs 21.8 yr for a dev-fitted line; CBECS 27.0 vs 26.0 yr.
Heat pump vs resistance fails on real homes: RECS AUC 0.40, worse than chance, against 0.94 in simulation. HUE (24 homes) cannot separate anything: every interval spans zero.
limits: UA, time constant and balance points have no real truth. Against EnergyPlus ResStock homes the hourly UA error is 0.29 log10 with a +0.25 bias, worse than the sample median (0.23).

Dev twin test (17 Nov 2026): the network's corrections to the dev-calibrated rules point the right way (correlation with what reality needed 0.50-0.60 for RECS area and heating fuel, 0.43 for CBECS hours, 0.1-0.3 for BDG2 area) but are biased and too large: on CBECS dev the hours correction has median +37 h and raises the error from 27 to 45 h; on BDG2 dev the hourly area correction (median −0.13 log10) makes the error worse than the rule's.

Real BDG2 load shapes still differ from simulated ones: hourly floor area needed error bars 3× wider than the network's own, and hourly input reads area no better than one annual total. Real electricity is less weather-sensitive than the twins (PRISM r² 0.07 vs 0.24).
Single thermal zone, first-order part load, ideal thermostat within the hour; campus plants are a flat distribution factor plus base load (W2, W3).

The real dev gate is small (52 BDG2 buildings plus the survey dev respondents) and noisy; it drifted from 0.331 to 0.306 over the kept rungs. It also lets a much worse headline output pass: rung r10 (17 Nov 2026) raised BDG2 dev hourly floor-area error from 50.8 % to 69.0 % (worse than the dev median's 64.3 %) and still passed, because area is one of twelve terms.

Physics 1.1 + 1.2 + 1.4 (rung r10, 17 Nov 2026; not released) did not shrink the dev twin-test bias: the area correction to electricity ÷ dev EUI flipped from −0.13 to +0.10 log10 (hourly; needed 0), its correlation with what was needed fell from 0.12 to 0.03, and CBECS hours stayed at +37 h. Dev-fitted baselines still beat the networks on dev (5-fold CV).
Use probabilities are flattened on purpose (dev-fitted temperature 10): on real buildings they are close to uninformative.

When every day of the record lies on one side of the best change-point balance point (a home heated all year, three winter months only), the PRISM fit is degenerate and the release's reading depends on floating-point tie-breaking: numpy and the site's JS port can pick different, equally good fits. The monthly 12-point fit has such ties often: re-run here (numpy 2.5), 157 of 1,428 BDG2 buildings get different monthly features and the monthly area error moves from 49.4 % to 49.6 %.

The balance points do not follow the weather the way physics says: with the meters unchanged, shifting the outdoor temperature by ±4 K should move them by ±4 K, but the hourly network moves Lamb_education_Bert's heating balance point by about ±1 K (11.3 / 12.4 / 13.4 °C) and the HUE home's not at all (17.2 / 17.1 / 16.3 °C); the monthly network follows more (5.8 / 10.1 / 13.0 °C). Four exam units, checked in the live instrument on 17 Nov 2026.

The simulator rows were not re-run: the training bank is not kept and the ResStock/ComStock samples (data/proc/stock, about 1.2 GB) are not unpacked here. Numpy-vs-torch parity of the shipped weights cannot be checked (no checkpoints shipped).

Record length (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): training saw partial records as a full year of weather with the meters masked, so the two record-span inputs never moved; a shorter date axis put them at |z| ~ 90 (HUE_2 at 330 days read 295.6 m² healthcare instead of 99.5 m² residential). read_hourly now holds them at one year and warns (330 d: 95.1 m², 180 d: 76.0, 90 d: 88.3, all residential). The BDG2 and HEAPO exams used full-year axes, so they are unchanged.

District meters: two zero-fraction inputs reach |z| > 8 on real BDG2 district meters and alone moved floor area 45-99 % on two packaged buildings. Which reading is closer to the truth is not established; the reader warns and nothing is clipped.
help: Real thermostat logs (ecobee Donate Your Data, by application) would give a real exam for time constants and setpoint behaviour; none exists today.
UK heat-pump field trials (RHPP, Electrification of Heat) need UK Data Service registration; they would test the heat-pump signature that fails on RECS and HUE.
An EnergyPlus binary for a true reference engine (no PyPI wheel with an engine; GitHub was blocked in the build sandbox) and the official ASHRAE 140 tables for BESTEST.
Any public building set with measured envelope UA or a co-heating test next to its meters: UA and the time constant have no real truth anywhere in the exam.
A fresh real exam: every set here has now been seen (v1.0 once, the 17 Nov 2026 re-score). A new BDG2-like release, or a utility's metered buildings with floor area and systems, would give one.
next: Add a per-output dev gate on the headline real outputs (BDG2, RECS and CBECS floor area; RECS and CBECS heating type), each against its dev-fitted baseline, written down before the next rung.

Anchor on the dev-fitted baselines: predict the correction to the dev-fitted line or logistic model instead of the raw output, so the network has to add something real to win (the twin test shows its corrections point the right way but overshoot).

Physics v3 from the remaining twin gaps: real electricity is much less weather-sensitive than the twins (PRISM r² 0.07 vs 0.24); add a calibrated mix of meters serving unconditioned space or process load.
Heat-pump realism: backup strips, defrost, sizing and ResStock-like controls fitted on RECS and HUE dev, or WPuQ heat-pump homes as a dev set (done when RECS dev heat pump vs resistance AUC > 0.7).
Domain-adversarial or twin-consistency training on unlabelled real BDG2 2016 meters, plus a dev-fitted population prior for the use classes.
Upstream to BuildingSim behind flags: W1 intensity factors, W2 campus factors, W3 base-load shares, and common.clean_labels (base_share undefined when metered site energy is ~0).

District meters (audit follow-up, 27 Nov 2026): rung r11 (simulated district plants switched off for a season or an outage) brought the two zero-fraction inputs from 387 sd to 6 sd on dev but tied r10 on the frozen set (0.8287 vs 0.8301) and was rejected; clipping the two inputs in v1.0 gave dev area 43.5 % vs 50.8 % but only +0.007 on the frozen set. Next: a frozen set whose district meters include zero runs, so the ratchet can score this, then both again.

physics.summary: BuildingSim, the collection's building simulator (shared building platform, Phase 1): an ISO 13790 5R1C single-zone heat balance with Perez solar gains, LBL infiltration, ventilation and moisture, and 13 HVAC systems built from capacity, COP and EIR curves with part load, defrost, fans, pumps and district plants. Labels come from the simulator itself: UA is the 5R1C network conductance (labels()['UA_network_W_K']), tau, balance points, end-use shares, schedules and system classes. Three wrappers calibrated on dev only (training/wrappers.py, upstream candidates for BuildingSim) set use-type intensities (W1), campus district service (W2) and always-on base loads found by the dev twin test (W3, physics v2).
checks: BuildingSim Phase 1 (shared building platform checks): steady conduction to 1.8e-9, RC step within 0.0035 K, degree-day ratio 0.999996, ISO 13786 wall amplitude −1.6 % and lag −0.01 h, every energy ledger closes to 1e-8
BESTEST (ASHRAE 140): 29 of 34 values inside the published ranges, all 20 annual heating and cooling values in (ranges transcribed from the literature)
ResStock twins (126 homes): site energy median 1.10× (IQR 0.98-1.26), daily r 0.92; ComStock twins (45): 0.86× (aggregate 0.97), daily r 0.89

Dev twin test (52 BDG2 dev buildings vs simulated twins from their metadata, medians): district-heat heating slope real 0.81 vs twin 4.38 before W3 and 1.00 after; chilled-water night/day real 0.69 vs 0.31 before and 0.63 after; electricity night/day real 0.77 vs 0.66 before and 0.74 after (training/twintest.json)

The release's JS feature port (training/detective.js) matched Python to 2e-7 on real and simulated buildings; the site's live instrument matches the Python release to 1e-6 on 60 control settings of the 12 example units

ladders.name: BuildingDetective v1.0, hourly network
ladders.objective: Skill on the frozen simulated validation set (bank shards 900-904: 1,000 BuildingSim buildings; hourly and annual read two meter-quirk draws per building (2,000), monthly one (1,000)): the mean of 12 regression R² (clipped at 0) and 3 class balanced accuracies rescaled so chance = 0
ladders.rule: Keep a rung if its frozen-set skill beats the incumbent of the same network by more than 0.01 AND the real dev composite (all three networks together, the candidate in place of its incumbent) is no more than 0.02 below the composite of the last kept rung of any network. A physics change rebuilds the frozen set from the same shards and re-scores the incumbents.

models.name: FaultFinder
models.tagline: Is this air handler faulty today, and which fault is it, from one day of trend log?
models.question: From one day of an air handler's trend log: P(fault) and which fault
models.summary: FaultFinder reads one local day of an air handler's (AHU) or rooftop unit's (RTU) building-automation trend log (outdoor, return, mixed, supply and zone air temperatures, the supply-air setpoint, damper and valve commands, fan speed, power and status, occupancy; 1- to 15-min samples, any subset) and returns P(fault), a probability over 18 fault classes, a severity for the top class and the day's extra HVAC energy. It learned only from BuildingSim simulations: 38,987 simulated days of random RTU and VAV buildings in 17 US climates, with real sensor noise and quirks from 20 real dev days. It was examined once on 217 real lab and building days from four sources (Iowa Energy Resource Station, LBNL FLEXLAB, ORNL's rooftop unit and Drexel's Nesbitt Hall), and re-scored on 17 Nov 2026 against rules tuned on the same dev days, with 95 % intervals. v1.1 (17 Nov 2026) can also compare the day with the same unit's last 1-3 logged days: v1.0's network plus 47 reference input rows, trained on simulated days with v1.0's weights frozen. Without reference days it gives v1.0's log-odds. On real days with a reference it shifts the log-odds up by about 0.1 to 0.7, which raised false alarms on the (seen) exam.
models.disclaimer: Research model: it flags days for a person to look at and does not replace commissioning. At P = 0.5 it raises a false alarm on a third of healthy air-handler days, and v1.1 raises false alarms on days with a reference (seen exam: AHU 33 → 56 %). Its fault diagnosis is no better than naming the commonest fault.
models.reads: One local day of an AHU or RTU trend log, 1- to 15-min samples, binned to 96 × 15 min: T_oa, T_ra, T_ma, T_sa, T_sa_sp (or T_sa_sp_cool / T_sa_sp_heat), T_zone (°C); damper_oa, valve_cc, valve_hc, fan_sa_speed (0..1, controller commands as logged); comp1_status / comp2_status for RTUs (0/1); fan_sa_power_kW or a fan current (any unit, scaled by its own daily 95th percentile); fan_sa_status, occ (0/1). Any subset; missing channels are flagged to the network. Temperatures below −45 or above 70 °C, and flatlined temperature sensors, count as missing. Optional (v1.1): the same unit's earlier days within 7 days, in the same format; the last 3 are used and their fault status is not needed.
returns: P(fault) for the day, calibrated by one temperature (T = 4.2, v1.0 4.3) fitted on 20 real dev days with their reference days; ranking is unaffected, but values are squashed toward 0.5 (157 of 217 exam days fall in 0.4-0.6)
Diagnosis: a probability over 18 fault classes given a fault (top-1 18 %, top-3 50 % on 66 real faulty days, seen; v1.0 20 % / 48 %)
A severity parameter for the top class and the day's extra HVAC energy fraction (simulation-trained only; the energy output is not useful on real data: Spearman 0.23)
models.network: 1-D CNN over 96 × 15-min bins. Input (v1.1): 82 rows = today's 35 feature rows (6 temperatures, 5 physical differences MA−RA, SA−MA, SA−SP, OA−RA, zone−RA, the estimated outdoor-air fraction, 7 actuator and state signals, time of day, 14 availability masks), the per-bin median of the same 35 rows over the unit's 1-3 reference days, today minus that median for the 11 temperature and physics rows, and the reference count / 3 (all 47 zero without references). Convolutions 64-64-128-128 (kernels 5, 5, 5, 3; two max-pools), mean + max pooling, dense 128, heads for 19 class logits, 19 severity parameters and 1 energy-waste fraction. 175,143 parameters after BatchNorm folding: v1.0's 160,103, frozen, plus 15,040 first-layer weights for the reference rows (r8). One calibration temperature T = 4.2 on the detection log-odds and the diagnosis logits, fitted on the 20 dev days with their reference days (widen-only, T >= 1).
models.noise: A real-noise model fitted on the real fault-free dev days only: each channel's 15-min residual around a 75-min running mean while the fan runs (residual library, random circular shift and gain 0.5-1.5), static sensor offsets, sensor drift toward a return/outdoor blend when the fan stops, logger gaps, flatlined sensors and each exam source's set of logged points. Twenty unlabelled Korean office AHUs set the start/stop irregularity and the tail of supply-air tracking error.

approach.real_backdrop: Real BMS noise from the 20 dev days' fault-free trend logs (15-min residual library, static offsets, fan-off drift, gaps and each source's logged points), added to every simulated day
approach.physics_inputs: Mixing-box and coil physics as feature rows: MA−RA, SA−MA, SA−setpoint, OA−RA, zone−RA, and the outdoor-air fraction (MA−RA)/(OA−RA) from the mixed-air energy balance

split.exam: Every other gradable run: 217 real or experimental unit-days, 200 AHU days (91 faulty) and 17 RTU days (12 faulty), from Iowa ERS (101), LBNL FLEXLAB (23), ORNL RTU (17) and Nesbitt Hall (76). Run once, after the ladder was closed.

exam.short: 217 real lab and building days (Iowa ERS, FLEXLAB, ORNL, Nesbitt Hall), seen
exam.summary: Detection (P(fault)) and diagnosis on 217 real days. v1.0 took the exam once; the 17 Nov 2026 integrity pass re-scored it from the released weights (FaultFinder's numbers reproduce to 6e-8), so every row is labelled seen and nothing was chosen from it. Baselines: the APAR rule set (12 rules, after Schein et al., 2006) for AHUs and a one-line rule (fan on while unoccupied) for the RTU, with textbook tolerances and a dev threshold as in v1.0, the same rules with tolerances tuned on the 20 dev days (a 54-setting grid), and a mixing-box residual detector fitted on the dev days. Every graded row gives FaultFinder minus the best baseline on that row with a 95 % bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples, seed 20261117) over unit-days, and over facility-days as a check; win or loss only when the unit-day interval excludes zero, and a row the majority guess wins is a loss. The recall-at-fixed-false-alarm rows set thresholds on the exam's own healthy days and are report-only. The rows below are v1.1, re-scored after its release decision (seen): each exam day gets as references the same unit's exam days from the previous 7 days (most recent 3, chosen by date; labels not read); 153 of 217 days have one. v1.0's values are in each note and in MODEL_CARD.md. Nothing in the release was chosen from these rows.

wins: Catching faults at P = 0.5 (seen, v1.1): 86 % of faulty AHU days against 52 % for the APAR rules with dev-tuned tolerances (+34 points, 95 % CI [+22, +46]); at Nesbitt Hall, a real occupied building, 88 % against 62 % for a dev-fitted mixing-box residual (+27, [+10, +44]). The price is the false alarms below.

Ranking: FLEXLAB AUC 0.97 against 0.74 (+0.23, CI [+0.02, +0.48], 23 days). AHU AUC 0.78 against 0.69 for the dev-tuned rules (+0.09, CI [−0.00, +0.17]) and Nesbitt 0.79 against 0.71 (+0.08, CI [−0.03, +0.20]) are ahead but not established.
losses: False alarms: at P = 0.5 v1.1 flags 56 % of healthy AHU days (v1.0 33 %; Iowa ERS 67 %, Nesbitt 44 %) against 2 % for the textbook-tolerance rules (+54 points, CI [+44, +64]). On real days with a reference the reference rows add about +0.1 to +0.7 to the log-odds, healthy days included (ERS healthy +0.71 on average).

Balanced accuracy is no better than rules tuned on the same 20 dev days: AHU 0.65 against 0.68 (CI [−0.11, +0.06]), all units 0.64 against 0.69 (CI [−0.13, +0.03]); Iowa ERS 0.55, a loss (−0.14, CI [−0.26, −0.02]). v1.0: AHU 0.70, ERS 0.65.

At Nesbitt Hall the textbook rules were a weak baseline (AUC 0.54): a mixing-box residual fitted on the dev days reaches 0.71 and the dev-tuned rules stay at 0.54; most of v1.0's Nesbitt margin was against the weak one.
Rooftop unit (17 days): AUC 0.72, the same as the one-line rule 'fan on while unoccupied' (v1.0 0.65); balanced accuracy 0.53, a tie with the rules (v1.0 0.47, a loss to the majority guess).
Diagnosis: top-1 18 % against 21 % for always naming the commonest fault, top-3 50 % against 55 % for the three commonest. Ties by the interval rule: no evidence of skill beyond the commonest class.
At strict false-alarm rates the rules catch more on the point values: 32 % against 29 % at 2 %, 41 % against 30 % at 5 % (AHU, report-only thresholds; the intervals span zero).
limits: Diagnosis on real data is about as good as guessing the commonest fault. Use the top three as a checklist, not an answer; outdoor-air damper stuck is top-1 on 1 of 14 days (v1.0 0).

v1.1 raises false alarms on days with a reference (seen exam: AHU 33 → 56 %, Iowa ERS 27 → 67 %). The reference rows were trained on simulated days only; on real days they add a near-constant +0.1 to +0.7 to the log-odds, a sim-to-real offset. The dev gate could not see it: only 2 of the 20 dev days have a reference. Leave the reference days out to get v1.0's behaviour.

Probabilities are squashed toward 0.5 by a temperature fitted on 20 days (T = 4.2; v1.0 4.3): 157 of 217 exam days fall in 0.4-0.6, and two of the four false alarms on the dev days sit at P = 0.501. v1.0's uncalibrated Brier score was lower (0.204 vs 0.216); for v1.1 the calibrated one is (0.220 vs 0.225); both intervals span zero. A two-parameter (Platt) map fitted on the dev days (r7b, not kept) cut dev false alarms from 4 to 1 of 11 leave-one-out but also cut detections from 6 to 4 of 9, and its leave-one-out Brier score was worse (0.258 vs 0.246).

History is short: v1.1 compares a day with at most the unit's last 3 days within a week, and only on simulated evidence. That most false alarms are unit habits is a hypothesis, not a measurement: on the 11 healthy dev days the nearest day in feature space was the same unit's for 4 of 10, and subtracting the unit's other healthy days' log-odds raised dev false alarms from 3 to 4 of 8. A multi-day rung (r7_context, 17 Nov 2026) was tried and not kept: on simulated days with a reference it scored 0.563 against 0.537 with the reference removed, but its 3-seed mean skill on frozen v5 was 0.558 against v1.0's 0.561, and only 2 of the 20 dev days have an earlier same-unit day within 7 days. r8 (v1.1) kept v1.0 frozen and added only the reference rows: frozen v5 skill 0.572 against 0.561.
Single-zone simulator with ideal controls and no exhaust damper, return fan, duct model, chiller-off or chilled-water sensor faults: 13 of the exam's 27 fault types cannot be diagnosed at all.

Small exam: 217 days from five facilities. The 95 % interval on AHU AUC minus the best baseline is about ±0.09, on the RTU ±0.4. The fixed-false-alarm recall rows set their thresholds on the exam's own healthy days and are report-only.
The energy-waste output is not validated (Spearman 0.23 on 46 paired ERS days; v1.0 0.19).

Reader guardrails (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): the flatline check ran over the whole file before the day was cut, so another day in the same file could flip an alarm (0.513 to 0.500). The day is now cut first; the exam passed one-day frames, so it is unchanged. read_day refuses an empty day (it returned 0.45) and reference days that are not earlier than the day read (self-reference moved ornl_rtu by -0.089), and warns when supply-air temperature covers under 75 % of the day (6 h prefixes dropped three full-day alarms below 0.5).
help: LBNL's full fault-detection datasets sit behind a name-and-e-mail form at faultdetection.lbl.gov. They would add a second real RTU exam and more field data; the owner can fill in the form.
More real, labelled field data from occupied buildings (Nesbitt Hall is the only one): the exam has 217 days from five facilities.
An EnergyPlus binary for a true reference engine (no PyPI wheel with an engine; GitHub was blocked in the build sandbox) and the official ASHRAE 140 tables for BESTEST.
next: A dev-side fix for the reference offset: calibrate the shift the reference rows add (for example one dev-fitted offset on the reference-row contribution) on dev days that have references, once the dev split has more same-unit runs (2 of 20 days have one now). Not done in v1.1.

Simulate the missing air-side and plant faults in BuildingSim (exhaust and return-fan dampers, return fan, duct leak, chiller off, chilled-water sensors) so 13 more exam fault types become diagnosable.

Calibration with its own rule and a larger dev set: on 20 days a Platt map (r7b) and the single temperature cannot be told apart (leave-one-out Brier 0.258 vs 0.246), and the Platt threshold trades 3 false alarms for 2 detections.

physics.summary: BuildingSim, the collection's building simulator (shared building platform, Phase 1): a 5R1C zone heat balance with solar gains, wind and stack infiltration and moisture, and air handlers built from fan laws, a mixing box, cooling and heating coils, chillers and boilers and DX curves from DOE reference data. Twenty fault types are injected into the plant and logged as a BMS-style trend. A FaultFinder wrapper (training/simbank.py, noise.py) makes the log look like a real BMS: commands rather than actuator positions, an installed damper characteristic, larger static sensor offsets and operator start/stop jitter.
checks: RC step response within 0.003 K of the closed form; steady conduction to 2e-9 relative error; energy ledger closes to 1e-8 (BuildingSim checks)
31 of 36 BESTEST (ASHRAE 140) results inside the 1995 reference ranges (the transcribed ranges; the official ASHRAE 140 tables are still wanted)
Psychrometrics within 0.02 K (p95) of CoolProp; PMV within 0.003 of pythermalcomfort
26 of 26 BuildingSim fault signatures move the trend in the expected direction

Numpy inference matches torch to 3.8e-6 for v1.1 (faultfinder_weights.npz.check.json; v1.0 9.5e-7); without reference days v1.1 matches v1.0's logits to 1.9e-6. The lab page's JS port (v1.0) matches numpy to 5e-6 on all 217 exam days (top class agrees on 217 of 217)

models.name: ThermoPilot
models.tagline: A thermostat MPC that pre-heats and pre-cools against real tariffs.
models.question: Which setpoints keep a building comfortable for the lowest bill? *(graded in simulation)*
models.summary: ThermoPilot is a causal thermostat / heat-pump controller for homes and small commercial buildings. Every hour it picks a heating and a cooling setpoint from a menu of 36 pairs (off, the comfort-band edge, or pre-heat / pre-cool by up to 3 K) to minimise the bill plus a penalty of $3 per kelvin-hour outside the occupant's comfort band (per 150 m² of floor). Since v1.1 the default controller is classical, with no learned parameters: a 24 h dynamic programme ("card MPC") on a 12-number linear map of the house carried by its building card, behind a rule-based 6 h comfort shield. It replaced the v1.0 network (an MLP that imitated a perfect-foresight teacher in BuildingSim), which stays in the package as mode='network': on the rebuilt simulated val set the card MPC scores 0.700 skill against the network's 0.561, and a residual network on top of it (rung R8) did not beat it. On simulated twins of real exam units (seen re-score, 17 Nov 2026) v1.1 beats v1.0 on every set, beats the classical MPC on small commercial buildings with demand charges, and still loses to the classical MPC on homes.
models.disclaimer: Graded in simulation. There are no real thermostat logs (ecobee's Donate Your Data needs an application), so every exam number is BuildingSim with real weather, real tariffs and twin buildings, not a measured saving. v1.1's house map is fitted to the twin's own nominal BuildingSim model, so it plans on a near-copy of the house the simulator starts from (the simulated house is a perturbed copy); a real thermostat would have to identify those 12 numbers from its own data, which was not tested. On 37 real WPuQ heat-pump homes the simulator overstates the heating slope 2.7× and puts heat-pump load at night.
models.reads: Each hour: the indoor air temperature (°C), the HVAC's own heat output (W) and the meter's electricity (kW) last hour, a 24 h forecast of outdoor temperature (°C) and solar (W/m²), 24 h of energy prices ($/kWh), demand-charge windows, rates and the running monthly peak, the occupant's comfort band for the next 24 h, the expected other electricity load, and a building card: heating type, heat-pump / furnace / AC capacity and COP tables vs outdoor temperature, fan power, and (v1.1) a 12-number linear house map (air and mass temperature one hour ahead as linear functions of the mass temperature, HVAC heat, outdoor temperature, solar and the other load). The v1.0 network also reads the last 3 hours of indoor temperature and the card's UA (W/K), thermal capacitance (J/K) and floor area.
returns: A heating and a cooling setpoint (°C; ±100 means that side is off) for the hour, after a comfort shield that never lets the zone fall behind the band of the next 6 h (recovery 1 K/h heating, 0.5 K/h cooling)
v1.1 also returns the card MPC's expected cost ($) of each of the 36 setpoint pairs over the next 24 h
No uncertainty: the controller is deterministic; exam intervals are 95 % bootstrap intervals over units
models.network: v1.1 (default) has no network: a backward dynamic programme over the house's mass temperature (0.25 K grid, 24 h horizon, replanned every hour, 36 setpoint pairs; cost = energy + gas + demand-charge increments over the running monthly peak + λ × K h outside the band) on the card's 12-number linear house map, with a dead-beat observer of the mass temperature from the measured air temperature, then the 6 h comfort shield. v1.0 (mode='network'): MLP 298 → 384 → 384 → 36 (276,516 parameters) on 34 state / tariff / building-card features plus 11 × 24 h forecast rows, trained on soft targets from a perfect-foresight teacher's action values plus expected regret (behaviour cloning, then 3 DAgger rounds); argmax over the 36 pairs, then the same shield
models.noise: Forecast error on outdoor temperature that grows with lead time; a perturbed 'true' house (envelope ±12 %, air leakage ±25 %, mass class, internal loads) that the controller never sees exactly; real weather years and real tariffs

approach.real_backdrop: Real weather years (BDG2 2016 site weather, TMYx cities) and real tariffs (URDB, ERCOT real-time prices) drive every simulated episode; v1.1 was chosen on the frozen simulated val set and the RECS / BDG2 dev gate
approach.physics_inputs: A building card from the physics model: a 12-number linear house map least-squares fitted to the nominal twin's hourly ISO 13790 5R1C maps, and heat-pump / furnace / AC capacity and COP tables on the 24 h temperature forecast
approach.physics_anchor: v1.1 is the physics: a dynamic programme on the card's house map, behind a comfort shield built on recovery rates (1 K/h heating, 0.5 K/h cooling); the v1.0 network, kept as an option, was trained to imitate a dynamic programme with the true house and weather

exam.short: 166 simulated twin episodes, real weather and tariffs (seen; HUE not scored for v1.1)
exam.summary: All seen: v1.0 took these sets once at release, and on 17 Nov 2026 v1.1 and v1.0 were scored again after v1.1 was chosen on val and dev; nothing was chosen from them. The RECS list was frozen again with stable twins (same respondents, 39 of 48 homes got a different twin), so both versions were re-scored there; BDG2 and WPuQ are as frozen. Twins of real exam units (perturbed true house, noisy forecasts) under their real weather and real tariffs, against a fixed thermostat, the occupant's own setback schedule, standard setback, two pre-cool rules, the in-band pre-cool rule tuned on dev (4 h, 3 K), a classical MPC with the same nominal house and the same noisy forecast (it also reads the true wind and indoor humidity), and a perfect-foresight bound. Bill = energy + demand + gas for the month (fixed charges left out), summed over episodes. Skill = share of the perfect-foresight saving on cost + comfort (0 = fixed thermostat, 1 = perfect foresight). Every row gives v1.1 minus the best baseline with a 95 % bootstrap interval over units (homes / buildings; 2,000 resamples, seed 20261117); win or loss only when the interval excludes zero. On bill rows a baseline counts only if it keeps comfort within the ratchet's test (K h ≤ fixed + 1). Each note gives v1.0 (the network, mode='network') on the same episodes and v1.1 minus v1.0 with its interval. HUE was not run (NASA POWER irradiance not fetched): v1.0's point values are kept in one info row.

wins: v1.1 beats v1.0 on every exam set, bill and skill, with intervals above zero: bill +0.43 points (RECS), +2.20 (BDG2), +2.81 (WPuQ); skill +0.42, +0.31, +0.44 (seen).
On small commercial buildings with demand charges (BDG2) it beats the classical MPC: bill 4.97 % vs 2.69 %, +2.28 points [+1.46, +3.08]; skill 0.757 vs 0.452, with no time outside the band.
Comfort: 0.42 K h per RECS home-month (fixed thermostat 0.74, setback 2.52, classical MPC 0.56; tie with the MPC [−0.32, +0.03]); 0.00 on BDG2 and WPuQ.
No learned parameters and no weights: it runs from the building card alone, in numpy, in about 4 s per simulated month.
losses: The classical MPC (BuildingSim's own hourly 5R1C maps of the nominal house, the true wind and indoor humidity) still beats it on homes: RECS bill −0.93 points [−1.30, −0.58], skill −0.12 [−0.20, −0.01]; WPuQ bill −1.22 [−1.32, −1.11], skill −0.16 [−0.18, −0.15].
On homes its bill saving ties the occupant's own setback schedule (RECS +0.49 points [−0.28, +1.36]; WPuQ +0.37 [−0.36, +1.30]); it keeps much better comfort than setback (0.42 vs 2.52 K h on RECS).
Without the comfort shield the card MPC leaves the band often (0.91 K h per dev episode; dev skill 0.572 vs 0.720 with the shield): it does not anticipate the band tightening after a setback.
A learned residual on top of it (R8) made it worse on val (0.667 vs 0.700, 3 seeds): the network moved the setpoints in 97 % of hours where the teacher departs from the card MPC in 6 %.
limits: Graded in simulation: there are no real thermostat logs (ecobee Donate Your Data needs an application; Pecan Street is paid). Every exam number is BuildingSim with real weather, real tariffs and twin buildings, and every exam set is seen.

The card's 12-number house map is fitted to the twin's own nominal BuildingSim maps over the month being controlled. In the simulator the true house is a perturbed copy, so there is model error, but a real thermostat would have to identify the map from its own logs; that was not built or tested.
v1.1 was chosen on numbers seen as a reference row in R8's run (the same frozen val and dev sets); the rule was applied without changes, but the candidate was proposed after seeing them.

WPuQ reality check (37 real heat-pump homes, report only, v1.0): generic twins overstate the heating slope 2.7× (median; IQR 1.4–5.4) and peak at night while real heat pumps run flat (hourly-profile r = 0.21). Time-shifting savings are the least certain part.

The exam's classical MPC reads the true future wind for infiltration (with the wind at its monthly mean its dev skill dropped 0.815 → 0.787 on the old dev set) and the indoor humidity; the card MPC reads neither.
Hourly ideal thermostat: one zone, no short-cycling or minimum run times, no humidity control; on/off counts are hourly.
Twins come from survey characteristics plus a ResStock match, not audits. HUE and WPuQ use stand-in US tariffs. HUE was not scored for v1.1.
Perfect foresight is a practical bound (a DP on a 0.25 K grid with the 36-pair menu, plus rules), not a proven optimum.
The comfort weight (λ = $3 per K h per 150 m²) is an input; the v1.0 network was trained at one λ and sees it only through log(λ / (mean price × size)).

Since 17 Nov 2026 the twin builder ranks tied ResStock matches by bldg_id (training/tp/twins.py), so RECS twins rebuild on any machine; v1.0's own RECS twins (sandbox tie order) cannot be rebuilt, so v1.0's release-day RECS numbers are not comparable with these.

UK heat-pump field trials (RHPP, Electrification of Heat): UK Data Service registration; they would test the heat-pump load shape the WPuQ check found wrong.
Pecan Street Dataport (paid): US homes with circuit-level HVAC data.
EnergyPlus as a reference engine: no PyPI wheel with an engine and GitHub was blocked in the build sandbox; install it outside and compare BuildingSim's zone response.

Evaluation card (audit, 25 Nov 2026): the exam fitted each house's card on the episode's own weather, including realized wind beyond the 24 h forecast (+6 m/s from hour 48 changed 19 of 72 first commands, by up to 2 °C). On four 30-day BuildingSim episodes a prior-month card moved v1.1's monthly cost by -$1.02 to +$0.23 (<= 0.21 %), with no comfort violations and every ranking kept. BuildingSim's weather cache keyed only on temperature and could reuse another run's wind; fixed 27 Nov 2026 (all columns are hashed). Re-scored 27 Nov 2026 with cards fitted on the month before each episode (166 episodes): every exam row moved by at most 0.04 bill points or 0.009 skill, no verdict changed (RECS skill −0.009 [−0.016, −0.003] is the one difference whose interval excludes zero); per episode the monthly cost J moved by up to 1.2 % (RECS), 0.7 % (BDG2), 0.2 % (WPuQ), in both directions. The exam rows now carry these numbers.

physics.summary: BuildingSim v1 (shared/building, BuildingData + BuildingSim): ISO 13790 5R1C zone with Perez solar, LBL infiltration and EnergyPlus-derived heat-pump (capacity and COP vs outdoor temperature, defrost, backup strips), DX, furnace and boiler curves with part load, run at 1 h steps through the step API with exact state rollback. Bills from real URDB tariffs (TOU, demand charges) and ERCOT real-time prices, gas at 2025 EIA averages. The teacher is a dynamic program over the mass temperature (0.25 K grid, 24 h horizon, hourly replanning) with the true house, the true weather and the true state; on demand tariffs it re-simulates the month with a monthly peak target (two-pass). The classical MPC and the teacher use BuildingSim's own one-step 5R1C maps. v1.1's card MPC uses the same dynamic programme on the card's 12-number linear house map instead (no wind, no indoor humidity), fitted to the nominal twin's hourly maps; on three dev episodes the map reproduces them to 0.08-0.19 K RMS.
checks: BuildingSim (platform checks, checks/*.json): steady conduction to 1.8e-9, RC step within 0.0035 K, ISO 13786 wall amplitude −1.6 %; BESTEST 29 of 34 values in the published ranges; ResStock twins (126 homes) site energy median 1.10×, daily r 0.92
Numba DP sweep == numpy DP loop exactly (max difference 0)

v1.1: the numpy card MPC in thermopilot_core.py reproduces the training-side runs exactly (closed-loop J to the cent on dev); the numpy demo replays its closed-loop setpoints in 744 / 744 hours on each of 3 exam episodes; the browser port matches Python to 8.5e-15 on 40 parity cases (20 per mode)
v1.0 network: numpy inference == torch to 0 (float32); the JS port == Python on 2,232 / 2,232 demo hours

Reality check (report only): on 37 WPuQ heat-pump homes, generic twins' heating slope is a median 2.7× the real one (IQR 1.4–5.4); real January profiles are flat while twins peak at night (profile r = 0.21)

models.name: StormNet
models.tagline: Three hours ahead, from the solar wind to the ring current.
models.question: How low will Dst fall in the next three hours?
models.summary: StormNet reads 36 completed hours of solar wind and the last hourly Dst and forecasts the lowest Dst of the next three hours. On 76,507 real forecasts across solar minimum and maximum, including the May 2024 superstorm, it beats persistence by a wide margin (storm-strength targets 10.7 against 14.2 nT at solar maximum) but only ties ring-current physics tuned on the same dev storms (10.7 against 10.6 nT), and loses on the most extreme hours and on quiet false alarms. Its 68% bars, now widened by how deep the storm already is, cover 60% of storm-strength targets.
models.reads: 36 hourly values of GSM Bz (nT), bulk speed (km/s) and dynamic pressure (nPa), plus the last completed hourly Dst (nT).
returns: Lowest hourly Dst in the following three complete hours (nT) and its nominal 68% half-width (nT)
models.network: Two recurrent physical states plus a simulation-trained nonlinear residual and log-error scale. 15 causal features, 48 fixed random tanh units, 128 fitted output coefficients, 926 stored scalars including normalization. Standalone NumPy inference.
models.noise: Actual unlabelled training-era wind supplies joint Bz, speed, pressure and measurement gaps. Synthetic autoregressive disturbance and parameter variation supply index scatter. Real Dst is used for dev calibration, gates and evaluation, and as the last observed scalar at inference.

approach.physics_inputs: Southward motional electric field, square-root pressure, rolling wind means and fast/slow current estimates
approach.physics_anchor: Dev-tuned two-state forecast conditioned on the last completed Dst

Retrospective Earth-arrival-aligned wind and the last completed historical Dst. Real telemetry latency and index revisions matter in operational use; 2022–2025 Dst in OMNI is Kyoto's provisional or quicklook index.

The two-state fit reaches the lower pressure-coefficient bound. Simulated dev minima are typically 8–14 nT deeper than their real twins. Re-running the physics with the actual next three hours of wind barely helps (dev 4.36 → 4.21 nT), so the remaining error is the physics and the index's hourly noise, not the unknown wind.

Freshness (audit, 25 Nov 2026): a one-hour-stale Dst raised gallery MAE from 8.97 to 11.21 nT (extremes 39.12 to 46.85 nT). The calibration file's bin labels now match the code: Dst < -50, -50 to < -30, >= -30 nT.

models.name: FlowCast
models.tagline: Daily streamflow for rivers without a gauge, from weather and basin attributes
models.question: Daily flow of a river with no gauge
models.summary: FlowCast predicts daily streamflow (mm/day and m³/s) with 5-95 % quantiles for a basin that has no gauge, from basin-average ERA5-Land weather and 11 static attributes. It is a 64-unit LSTM (24,710 weights) trained only on 12,000 WaterSim simulations of random basins driven by real ERA5-Land forcing from non-exam years; it never reads streamflow from the basin it predicts. Graded once on 619 real CAMELS-US exam rivers (WY1990-99) and 603 of them again on WY2016-23, it does not beat classical ungauged regionalisation: median NSE 0.341 against 0.372 (and 0.378 against 0.433 on the recent exam). It ties or beats it in arid, regulated and large basins and loses in snowy and humid ones. An optional gauged nowcast mode, fine-tuned to also read the river's own observed flow up to 1-7 days earlier, beats persistence at every lead but not NOAA's National Water Model.
models.disclaimer: Every score here uses ERA5-Land forcing (through Caravan), which under-catches mountain and Pacific Northwest precipitation and drifts about 6 % between decades; that caps every method on the page, and published Daymet/NLDAS-driven LSTM scores (NSE about 0.69-0.76) are not comparable. Research model: not for flood warning.
models.reads: Basin-average daily forcing (Caravan / ERA5-Land conventions, UTC days): P (mm/d), PET (mm/d, FAO-56 Penman-Monteith), T_mean, T_min, T_max (°C), SRAD (W/m², net shortwave), vp (Pa), wind (m/s), from 365 days before the first predicted day to one day after the last; 11 static attributes: area (km²), mean/min/max elevation (m), slope (m/km or degrees), forest fraction, soil porosity, soil conductivity (cm/h or mm/h), carbonate fraction, reservoir storage / mean annual flow, irrigated fraction, urban fraction. Seven climate indices are computed from the forcing of the window itself. Nowcast mode also reads the observed daily flow (mm/day) up to `lead` days before each day.
returns: Daily mean flow Q (mm/day; Q_m3s in m³/s when the area is given), trained with an NSE-type loss
5 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 95 % quantiles (pinball loss), widened about the median by dev-fitted factors: 50 % band × 1.00, 90 % band × 1.08 (raw quantiles in the nowcast mode)
models.network: One LSTM layer, 64 units, over 11 daily weather features (P/10, log1p P, PET, three temperatures, net shortwave, vapour pressure, wind, day-of-year sine and cosine) plus 18 static features repeated at every step (11 attributes and 7 climate indices computed from the window's forcing: mean P and PET, aridity, snow share of P, high- and low-precipitation day frequencies, mean T). A linear head gives the mean (softplus) and five monotone quantiles (cumulative softplus), all in units of the basin's mean precipitation. 24,710 weights (25,478 for the nowcast copy, which adds three inputs: the observed flow `lead` days earlier, an availability flag and lead/7). Loss: NSE-type on the mean, scaled per sample by the Fu runoff ratio of the forcing (an input-only quantity; r0b), plus pinball loss on the quantiles. 3,000 steps × 32 windows of 730 days (365 scored), Adam lr 2e-3, dropout 0.1, CPU. Inference runs 365-day blocks, each with its own 365-day warm-up.
models.noise: WaterSim's forcing-error model on the network's input (precipitation bias and daily lognormal scatter cv 0.25, snow undercatch, temperature error) and gauge-like error on the target (AR(1) rating error, revisions, low-flow error). No real recordings are laid into the training signals: the forcing itself is real ERA5-Land from non-exam windows of CAMELS basins (exam basins' free-window forcing included, as the platform brief allows).

approach.real_backdrop: Real ERA5-Land daily forcing of CAMELS basins from non-exam windows (1951-1988, 1999-2015) drives every simulated basin
approach.physics_inputs: Seven climate indices computed from the forcing (mean P and PET, aridity, snow share, high/low-precipitation frequencies, mean temperature), and the output is expressed in units of the basin's mean precipitation

wins: Arid basins: level with regionalisation (median NSE 0.21 against 0.20 for U-dev, 174 basins), where flow is a small residual of rain minus evaporation; large basins (0.23 vs 0.22, 48; recent 0.34 vs 0.32). Regulated basins lead on the main exam (0.30 vs 0.25, 37) but trail on the recent one (0.38 vs 0.46). Breakdowns, not graded.

The gauged nowcast beats persistence at every lead on both exams: at 65-66 % of basins at 1 day and 85-90 % at 3 and 7 days (exact binomial intervals all above 61 %); median NSE 0.569 / 0.474 / 0.426 against 0.475 / −0.19 / −0.47 (1990s).
Its 90 % band is not too narrow: it holds 97 % of exam days at the median basin.
losses: It does not beat classical ungauged regionalisation: median NSE 0.341 against 0.372 (U-dev) and 0.385 (U-k12) on WY1990-99, 0.378 against 0.433 and 0.443 on WY2016-23; FlowCast is better at only 34 % of basins (95 % CI 30-38 %), and the paired bootstrap of the 1990s median gap to U-dev is −0.031 (95 % CI −0.056 to −0.014). U-dev borrows GR4J parameters calibrated on real dev gauges, information the network gets only through the simulator.
Snowy and humid basins: −0.16 and −0.12 NSE against U-dev (0.40 vs 0.56, 0.49 vs 0.62).

Flood peaks run 46 % low (median absolute error 60 % against 42-47 % for the gauged and operational baselines): the mean of a parameter-uncertain prediction is smooth. Flashier physics fixed peaks on dev but cost NSE (rungs r2, r4).
KGE and high- and low-flow volume: worse than both regionalisations (KGE 0.367 vs 0.433 and 0.462; FHV −31 % vs −27 and −21 %; FLV +59 % vs +34 and +37 %).
Bands too wide: the 90 % band is about 2.9 × the mean flow wide at the median basin.
The nowcast does not beat NOAA's National Water Model except at one day ahead in the 1990s, where it is level (0.569 vs 0.550); KGE at one day is below persistence's (0.635 vs 0.738).
limits: Weather data: ERA5-Land (Caravan conventions, net shortwave) under-catches mountain and Pacific Northwest precipitation (50 of the 671 CAMELS-US basins have a validation-period runoff ratio above 1; WaterData DATA.md gotcha 2) and drifts about 6 % between decades. This caps every method on the exam; published Daymet/NLDAS-forced LSTMs (median NSE about 0.69-0.76 on CAMELS) are not comparable.

The p1 water-yield correction is a regional regression fitted on the 52 dev basins that also gate the rungs (4 coefficients, partly in-sample). It over-predicts some wet Pacific Northwest basins: South Prairie Creek, WA, in the demo, at 1.76 × the observed volume (regionalisation also fails there: decade NSE −0.44).
CONUS-like attribute ranges and a daily step only; no hourly flows. WaterSim has no glacier melt (Caravan's glacier_frac is ignored).
Not a forecast: it simulates flow from observed weather. The nowcast is a hindcast too (observed weather on the target days).
The climate statics are computed from the forcing of the window being predicted, so a prediction for a short or unusual window carries that window's climate (exam-period forcing, never flow).

Rung decisions near ±0.01 on the frozen set are noise-level: a 300-basin subset and the full 800 disagreed on r5. A paired bootstrap over the 800 frozen basins (added on import) gives r1b's gain over r0b on p1 as +0.030 (95 % CI +0.001 to +0.052).

Reproducibility (audit, 25 Nov 2026): training seeded only NumPy's batch sampler, so the same config gave different initial weights; torch is seeded and resume restores both generators since 27 Nov 2026 (historical rungs were trained unseeded). The nowcast API now refuses lead 0, which would feed each day's own observed flow to its forecast; the exam used leads 1, 3 and 7.
help: Per-basin NWM v3.0 hourly flow and the WaterData baseline simulations, to extend the paired comparisons beyond median scores (both exams and the flood peaks were re-scored with paired intervals on 18 Nov 2026 from Caravan and NWIS).
Daymet or NLDAS daily forcing for the CAMELS basins in Caravan's format, to separate method skill from ERA5-Land bias.
next: A snow rung driven by twins on the 10 snowy dev basins: the full dev snow shift (TT −0.66 °C, SFCF +0.11, CFMAX) and an elevation-dependent ERA5-Land temperature bias. Snow is the largest exam gap (−0.16 against U-dev).
Per-basin water yield learned from attributes with uncertainty, instead of the regional regression; or ERA5-Land snow water equivalent and soil-moisture states as inputs.
Peaks without losing NSE: a separate high-flow head, the q75/q90 annual maximum as the peak estimate, or the flashier physics with a larger network.
Capacity: 128 units with longer training, or an ensemble of seeds, judged on larger frozen sets (decisions near ±0.01 are noise).
Narrower bands: a calibration that can also narrow (a rule change) or a log-space quantile head.
Re-run every exam with Daymet or NLDAS forcing to separate method skill from ERA5-Land bias; out-of-domain exams on CAMELS-GB, -CL, -BR and -AUS (attributes already in shared/water).

physics.summary: WaterSim, the shared water platform's simulator (shared/water/watersim): four lumped rainfall-runoff models (HBV, GR4J, SAC-SMA, VIC-lite), degree-day or energy-balance snow on elevation bands, unit-hydrograph or Muskingum-Cunge routing, reservoirs and irrigation, driven by real ERA5-Land forcing. FlowCast wraps it, without editing it, in five versioned physics files (training/phys/p0-p4.json); the released rung uses p1, which adds a dev-measured water-yield correction: a simulated basin's true precipitation is ERA5-Land × m with log m = −0.088 + 0.058 elev_km + 0.153 snow share + 0.397 log(P/3 mm) + N(0, 0.146), while the network still reads ERA5-Land.
checks: WaterSim GR4J vs airGR 1.7.9 (CRAN, compiled in an isolated R), help example L0123001: max |ΔQ| 1.0e-7 mm (airGR's single-precision output); NSE 1990-99 0.79882 vs the published 0.7988 (shared/water/checks/reference_models.json)
WaterSim HBV vs TUWmodel 1.1-1, lumped Vils 1976-2008: snow, soil moisture, ET, rain and melt identical to ≤ 1e-12 mm; runoff NSE 0.9990 (no routing), 0.9998 (MAXBAS 10)
Water balance, 121 runs over every model × snow × routing and real dev basins: worst closure 1.4e-15 relative, worst daily residual 8.3e-12 mm (balance.json)

Twin test (r1b, 52 dev basins, twin.py): median NSE of the same prediction against the real record 0.425, against each basin's calibrated twin 0.595, against its prior twin 0.380; flashiness ratio (prediction / target) 0.79 real vs 0.75 calibrated twin: the network reads real and calibrated twin alike. Mixing in the next UTC day gained nothing (no time-zone offset). For r0 the flashiness ratio was 0.54 real vs 0.51 twin, which led to the loss fix and to p2
numpy release == torch to 1.7e-7 relative on 4 dev basins × 2 years (export_check.json); the site instrument (TypeScript, float16 weights) == numpy on the same weights to 5.3e-8 on 54 cases

ladders.name: FlowCast v1.0, ungauged (WaterSim physics versions p0-p4, 18 Nov 2026)
ladders.objective: Median daily NSE of the mean prediction against the gauge-like target over 800 frozen simulated basins of the rung's physics version (two fixed 365-day scored windows per basin; training/src/train.py sim_eval). One frozen set per physics version: p0 (WaterSim as shipped), p1 (water yield), p2 (flashier runoff), p3 (forcing error), p4 (p3 + p2).
ladders.rule: Keep if the sim median NSE on the frozen set of the rung's physics version beats the incumbent's on that same set by more than 0.01 AND the dev median NSE (52 real dev basins, WY2001-14, ungauged) is at least 95 % of the incumbent's.

rungs.change: Baseline: WaterSim generator as shipped (p0): both attribute priors 50/50, 4 runoff models × 2 snow routines, 25 % Muskingum-Cunge, real ERA5-Land forcing from free windows, default forcing and gauge noise; NSE* loss scaled by the target's own std (Kratzert et al. 2019); LSTM 64, 3,000 steps
rungs.why: First rung. Dev NSE 0.390, KGE 0.319, FHV −51 %: the network ran low (twin test: flashiness ratio 0.54 real, 0.51 calibrated twin).

rungs.change: p1 physics: dev-measured water-yield correction (true P = ERA5-Land × m, log m = −0.088 + 0.058 elev_km + 0.153 frac_snow + 0.397 log(P/3) + N(0, 0.146)), old loss
rungs.why: Sim 0.332 vs r0's 0.397 on p1 (needs > 0.407) and dev 0.331 vs 0.390 (needs ≥ 0.370): both tests failed. It exposed the loss bias fixed in r0b.

rungs.change: Loss fix: per-sample loss scale from inputs only (the Fu runoff ratio of the forcing's aridity) instead of the target's own std, which down-weighted wet, flashy draws and biased the sim-trained ungauged network low
rungs.why: Sim 0.476 vs 0.441 on p0; dev NSE 0.436 vs 0.390, KGE 0.32 → 0.44, FHV −51 → −27 %. Share of dev basins with NSE < 0 rose from 7.7 % to 15.4 %.

rungs.change: p1 water-yield physics (as r1) with r0b's input-only loss scale
rungs.why: Sim 0.425 vs r0b's 0.395 on p1; dev 0.425 vs 0.436 (−2.5 %, inside the 5 % gate). Share of dev basins with NSE < 0 fell from 15.4 % to 11.5 %. Released as v1.0.

rungs.change: p2 flashier runoff: the full dev-calibrated median parameter shift (shrink 1.0, WaterSim ships 0.5) for the four runoff models; simulated Richards-Baker flashiness 0.62× → 1.00× of observed on dev
rungs.why: Sim 0.463 vs r1b's 0.446 on p2 passed; dev NSE 0.380 vs 0.425 (−10.5 %) failed, although dev KGE rose to 0.490, FHV to −16 % and peak error fell 49 → 42 %.

rungs.change: p3 larger forcing error for the network input: daily P cv 0.4 (was 0.25), bias sd 0.10 (was 0.08), up to 30 % of each day's rain moved to a neighbouring day (calib_noise.py: default noise left a calibrated twin at NSE 0.88 vs its clean run; reality allows 0.56; p3 gives 0.72)
rungs.why: Sim 0.326 vs r1b's 0.335 on p3 failed; dev 0.406 vs 0.425 (−4.4 %) passed.

rungs.change: p4 = p3 forcing error + p2 flashier runoff (flashiness retried with realistic forcing error)
rungs.why: Sim 0.404 vs r1b's 0.380 on p4 passed; dev NSE 0.378 vs 0.425 (−11 %) failed; dev KGE 0.490, FHV −23 %, peak error 45 %.

rungs.change: Longer training: r1b fine-tuned for 5,000 more steps (lr 1e-3, cosine, seed 5), same p1 physics
rungs.why: Sim 0.419 vs r1b's 0.425 on p1 failed (paired bootstrap −0.006, 95 % CI −0.019 to +0.015: noise); dev 0.434 passed. A 300-basin validation during training had said +0.02.

rungs.change: Error bars: one widen-only factor per band, about the median, fitted on the dev predictions of r1b (calib_sigma.py, results/sigma_r1b.json): the smallest factor at which pooled dev coverage reaches the nominal level
rungs.why: 50 % band × 1.00 (dev coverage 0.502 raw), 90 % band × 1.08 (0.863 → 0.953). No effect on the mean. r0's factors were 1.08 and 1.08.

ladders.name: FlowCast nowcast mode (gauged, optional, 18 Nov 2026)
ladders.objective: None logged. n1 is a single fine-tune of r1b (2,500 steps, lr 1e-3, seed 11, p1 bank) with three extra inputs: the gauge-like flow `lead` days earlier (log scale, in units of mean precipitation), an availability flag (gaps simulated in 30 % of training windows) and lead/7; one network serves leads 1-7.
ladders.rule: No frozen-set comparison and no dev gate were applied: there was no incumbent nowcast. Its only real-data check before the exam was the dev score against persistence at leads 1, 3 and 7 (results/nowcast_summary.json, dev).

rungs.change: r1b fine-tuned 2,500 steps with the observed flow up to `lead` (1-7) days earlier, an availability flag and lead/7 as inputs (configs/n1.json)
rungs.why: Released as the optional gauged nowcast weights (flowcast_nowcast_weights.npz). Dev: beats persistence at every lead.

audit.label: MINOR HYGIENE
audit.finding: Forward pass, Torch↔NumPy parity (`2.7e-7`/`3.9e-7`), static scaling (`max |z| <= 2.01` on shipped examples), and feature alignment all pass. Two minor issues found: (1) `train.py` seeds NumPy only, not PyTorch weight init/dropout, and resume resets RNG; (2) `flowcast.py` nowcast API silently accepts `lead=0` (same-day leakage; exam scripts cleanly use `1, 3, 7`).
audit.fixedNow: Nowcast refuses lead 0; torch seeded, resume restores RNG

resolutions.finding: Training seeds NumPy only; resume resets the generators
resolutions.text: Fixed for future runs: `torch.manual_seed(seed)` before the network is built; resume files store and restore both generator states. Historical rungs stay as trained.

resolutions.finding: Nowcast API accepts lead = 0
resolutions.text: Fixed: `predict` raises unless 1 ≤ lead ≤ 7 when `qobs` is given.

models.name: SnowSense
models.tagline: Daily snow water equivalent at a snow pillow, from the station's own weather
models.question: Daily snow at a mountain station, from its gauge and thermometer
models.summary: SnowSense estimates daily snow water equivalent (SWE) at a SNOTEL snow-pillow station from that station's own daily precipitation and air temperature, with 68 % and 90 % bands, plus each winter's peak SWE, peak date and melt-out date. It never reads a snow measurement. It learned only from WaterSim snow simulations (degree-day and energy balance) driven by real dev-station weather up to 2010. On 621 SNOTEL exam stations (water years 2011-2025) it scores median NSE 0.888, clearly above WaterSim's energy balance with default parameters (0.853). But the same energy balance with parameters tuned on the dev stations, run on the exam after import, scores 0.895: a tie on NSE, RMSE and melt-out timing, and a loss on peak SWE. The network adds nothing over tuned physics on the median, though it fails less often and is better below 1,500 m. A degree-day model calibrated on ten years of each station's own snow is better still (0.925).
models.reads: Daily precipitation P (mm, the gauge total for the local day), T_mean, T_min and T_max (deg C) from the station itself, plus its latitude and elevation. Each water year is read from 1 August of the previous year to 1 October (427 days). Gaps are allowed: missing P counts as 0, missing T is interpolated, and both are flagged to the network. Never any SWE or snow depth.
returns: Daily SWE median (mm, end of day) with 68 % and 90 % bands (exam coverage of snow days 78 % and 96 %)
Per water year: peak SWE (mm) with 68 % / 90 % intervals (exam coverage 76 % / 93 %)
Per water year: peak date, and melt-out date (first day after the peak below 5 mm) with 68 % / 90 % intervals (exam coverage 86 % / 95 %)
models.network: Input layer 10 -> 64 (tanh), a 2-layer GRU with 64 hidden units, and a head 64 -> 5 giving five monotone quantiles (5, 16, 50, 84, 95 %) of z = sqrt(SWE)/10, trained with a pinball loss on the water-year days; 50,949 parameters. Input channels per day: log1p(P)/2, T_mean/10, T_min/10, T_max/10, sin and cos of day of year, P-gap and T-gap flags, (elevation - 2200)/800, (latitude - 43)/8. Released rung R6: 48,000 simulated station-winters (two physics-p4 banks), fine-tuned R1 -> R6, AdamW one-cycle, batch 128, one CPU thread. numpy-only inference, about 0.05 s per station-year.
models.noise: Real weather, not synthetic: the simulated snowpacks are driven by the dev stations' own recorded P and T. From rung R2 on, the snowpack feels a 'true' weather that differs from the gauge record the network reads: wet-day P x lognormal(sd 0.25), 15 % of wet days slip part of their total to the next or previous day, temperature error AR(1) 0.6 deg C plus a station bias N(0, 0.5) deg C, and injected data gaps in the network input (P set to 0, T interpolated, both flagged).

approach.real_backdrop: Real daily precipitation and temperature records of the dev SNOTEL stations (water years up to 2010) drive every simulated snowpack, shifted to other climates

data.role: physics (simulator and the uncalibrated exam baselines)

split.dev: WaterData's frozen SNOTEL split (shared/water/data/proc/splits.json, seed 20261118): 39 dev stations, drawn per state, systematically by elevation, only where the HUC8 holds no exam CAMELS gauge. Training weather: dev stations up to WY2010, six of them (1059_CO, 461_UT, 510_MT, 560_WY, 573_NV, 647_OR) held out for the frozen simulated sets. Parameter prior: dev SWE up to WY2010. Dev gate, widen factors and twin test: the 38 dev stations with at least 5 complete water years in 2011-2025.
split.exam: The 621 of 772 exam stations that WaterData scored (at least 5 complete calibration and scoring years), water years 2011-2025, end-of-day SWE against the pillow's next-morning reading (WaterData's protocol). Scored once, after the ratchet had chosen the release on simulated and dev data only.

exam.summary: Medians over 621 exam stations of each station's 2011-2025 scores, re-scored on 18 Nov 2026 on the rebuilt SNOTEL series (the released weights reproduce the shipped exam exactly). Baselines: WaterSim's two snow routines with default parameters and with dev-tuned parameters (medians of the dev-station calibrations, frozen before scoring; added on import, seen exam), all reading only the weather like SnowSense; a climatology and a degree-day calibrated per station, both reading the station's own 2001-2010 SWE. Intervals: paired bootstrap over stations (10,000 resamples, seed 20261118) of the difference in medians; win or loss only where the 95 % interval excludes zero.
