Beats the degree-day routine tuned on dev (NSE 0.888 against 0.864, interval +0.012 to +0.037) and climatology built from each station's own 2001-2010 snow (0.701), without reading any snow.

Fails less often than the dev-tuned energy balance: NSE below 0.5 at 8.4 % of stations against 10.5 % (interval -3.9 to -0.3 points); below 1,500 m its median NSE is 0.787 against 0.704 (interval +0.041 to +0.159).
Its error bars hold on the exam: the 68 % bars cover 78 % of snow days, 76 % of peaks and 86 % of melt-out dates.
losses: Ties WaterSim's energy balance with dev-tuned parameters (added on import, seen exam): median NSE 0.888 against 0.895 (-0.007, interval -0.018 to +0.001), RMSE 51.7 against 49.7 mm, melt-out error 8.3 against 8.6 days; the tuned physics has the higher NSE at 55 % of stations. The network adds nothing over tuned physics on the median, as with WakeNet and StormNet.
Loses to the dev-tuned energy balance on peak SWE: error 17.5 against 16.2 % (interval +0.3 to +2.0 points), bias -9.0 against -4.3 %.

Loses to a degree-day model calibrated on ten years of each station's own SWE on every measure: NSE 0.888 against 0.925 (interval -0.050 to -0.026), ahead at only 34 % of stations; peak error 17.5 against 12.5 %; melt-out 8.3 against 6.1 days.
limits: The dev-tuned physics baselines were added on import and run once on an exam that had already been seen; their parameters (training/devtuned_params.json) were frozen before scoring and come from dev data only. The degree-day set uses the prior's means, because per-station medians were not shipped.

Weather data: SnowSense reads the station's own gauge and thermometer, not ERA5-Land, so the ERA5-Land under-catch and decade drift that cap FlowCast and BasinDetective do not apply here; but gauge under-catch of windblown snow does, and is the likely cause of the -9 % peak bias. Gridded forcing (ERA5-Land, PRISM, Daymet) is untested, and SNOTEL temperature sensors changed network-wide in the 2000s (Oyler et al. 2015).
Low and warm stations are weakest: median NSE 0.787 below 1,500 m and 0.776 in the Southwest (rain-on-snow, thin intermittent packs).
Every water year starts on 1 August with no snow knowledge; perennial snow is outside the training data (simulated windows with snow on 1 August were dropped).
The dev prior was fitted on dev SWE up to WY2010 and the dev gate uses the same stations in WY2011-2025, so the gate is partly in-sample. The exam was untouched until the release.

'WaterSim defaults' means WaterSim's default and attribute-transfer parameters as the exam path resolves them for a station given only latitude and elevation (energy balance CANOPY 0.535; degree-day TT -0.33 C, CFMAX 3.77, SFCF 1.054), not the bare parameter-table defaults.

Partial water years (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): predict() returned nothing before day 200 of the water year and then estimates through 30 September, 165 days past the last input. A year the record ends inside now needs 30 days, stops at the last input and reports the peak so far (melt-out is left empty). Completed years and the exam (which uses training/common.station_windows) are unchanged. Temperature gaps are filled from both sides: at the end of a live record that holds the last reading; across a gap in a past record it is smoothing, which moved station NSE by at most 0.0003 on the three packaged stations.
help: The SNOTEL daily series (data/proc/snotel) are not in the repository; rebuild them with `mlratchet data water` to re-run training/rescore_exam.py.
next: Give the network something the tuned physics lacks: the dev-tuned energy balance already matches it, so a rung should start from that anchor (e.g. a physics_anchor on the tuned EB, or snow processes it misses: wind drift, under-catch by exposure), shown failing on dev first.
Peak under-catch: a wind- or exposure-dependent snowfall-correction (SFCF) prior, or a drift term.
Rain-on-snow and thin packs below 1,500 m: sub-daily melt-refreeze, or rain energy in the degree-day routine.
A gridded ERA5-Land band mode so SnowSense can feed FlowCast (the SnowSense -> FlowCast test was not done).
An initial-snow input for stations that keep snow through summer; checks across the SNOTEL temperature-sensor change; more Alaska stations.

physics.summary: Point snowpack mass and energy balance. WaterSim's two snow routines run snow-only at the station (one band, no runoff model): the HBV-light degree-day routine (rain/snow partition over TT +- TTI/2, snowfall correction, melt CFMAX (T - TT), refreeze, liquid water holding) and a daily single-layer energy balance after Walter et al. (2005) and the Utah Energy Balance model (net shortwave with an ageing albedo, Brutsaert long-wave with a cloud correction, bulk-transfer sensible and latent heat with a stability reduction, ground and rain heat, cold content, refreeze, sublimation). Radiation comes from the daily temperature range (Hargreaves-Samani).
checks: Degree-day routine against a 5-day hand calculation: 0.0 mm; identical to TUWmodel 1.1-1 to <= 1e-12 mm (shared/water/checks/analytic.json, reference_models.json)
Energy-balance terms exact against hand arithmetic; mass closes to 6e-15 mm (shared/water/checks/analytic.json)

Against SNOTEL pillows at 33 dev stations, WY2011-2025 (shared/water/checks/snotel.json): degree-day NSE 0.700 with default parameters and 0.892 calibrated per station; energy balance 0.824 default and 0.930 calibrated

Twin test, 38 dev stations, WY2011-2025 (training/twin_r6.json): each station's calibrated energy-balance twin scores NSE 0.917 against its pillow; the released network reads the twin at 0.914 and the pillow at 0.888

ladders.name: SnowSense v1.0 (WaterSim snow, 18 Nov 2026)
ladders.objective: Median per-series NSE of daily SWE (water-year days) on the frozen simulated validation set: 1,600 windows simulated from the weather of six held-out dev stations, one set per physics version (val_p1..val_p4)
ladders.rule: Keep if the rung beats the incumbent by more than 0.01 median NSE on the newest frozen set (val_p4) AND (1 - NSE_dev) <= 1.05 (1 - NSE_dev of the incumbent), dev NSE being the median over 38 dev stations, WY2011-2025.

rungs.change: Baseline (physics p1): WaterSim degree-day and energy balance 50/50, parameters uniform over WaterSim's ranges, the network reads the forcing that drives the physics (no measurement error); Gaussian head
rungs.why: First rung.

rungs.change: Physics p2: gauge error between what the snowpack feels and what the network reads (wet-day P x lognormal 0.25, one-day timing slips, T AR(1) 0.6 C + station bias 0.5 C) and injected data gaps; fine-tuned from R1
Physics p3: parameter prior fitted on the dev stations (both routines calibrated on each dev station's own SWE up to WY2010 with wider bounds; multivariate normal x1.3); fine-tuned from R2
rungs.why: val_p4 0.810 > 0.769 + 0.01; dev 0.880 vs 0.805 passes. Twin test: R1 had read the twins at 0.80 but real at 0.73 with peaks 21 % below the twin; the prior, not the network, was the gap (twin_r1 not shipped).

rungs.change: Quantile head: five quantiles of sqrt(SWE) with a pinball loss instead of a Gaussian, so the many snow-free days stop dragging the median melt-out late (same p3 bank; fine-tuned from R3)
rungs.why: val_p4 0.822 > 0.810 + 0.01; dev 0.882 vs 0.880 passes. R3 had melted out 10 days after its twins (twin_r3 not shipped).

rungs.change: Physics p4: the dev prior used as fitted (inflation 1.3 -> 1.0), because R4's dev bands were too wide (68 % bands held 84 % of snow days, 93 % of melt-outs) and its peaks 11 % low; new frozen set val_p4; fine-tuned from R4
rungs.why: val_p4 0.831 not > 0.822 + 0.01 (dev 0.887 would have passed). On val_p3 it would have been kept (0.793 vs 0.778).

rungs.change: More simulated data: a second p4 bank with a new seed (48,000 windows in all), 6 more epochs, initialised from the rejected R5's weights
rungs.why: val_p4 0.839 > 0.822 + 0.01 over the incumbent R4; dev 0.888 vs 0.882 passes. Released as v1.0. Rule note: initialised from R5, which the ratchet had rejected; on val_p3 it would have fallen short (0.785 vs 0.778).

audit.label: Daily inference and partial-year defects
audit.finding: Future gap filling moved an earlier SWE estimate by 2.14 mm on an actual gap. On all three stations, 199 days returned no data and 200 days returned 165 daily estimates beyond the last input.
audit.fixedNow: Partial water years stop at the last input; torch seeded

resolutions.finding: Partial water year: empty before day 200, then 165 dates past the last input
resolutions.text: Fixed: a year the record ends inside needs 30 observed days, its daily output stops at the last input, and its annual row gives the peak so far with no melt-out and an `observed_through` date. Completed years follow the old path exactly.

resolutions.finding: Temperature gaps interpolated from both sides
resolutions.text: In live use the record ends today and `interpolate` holds the last reading, so nothing ahead is read. Across a gap inside a past record, using both sides is smoothing for a retrospective estimate, which is what the completed-year exam scores.

resolutions.finding: Trainer seeds NumPy only
resolutions.text: Fixed for future runs (`torch.manual_seed(SEED)`).

models.name: BasinDetective
models.tagline: How a river's flow changes in a decade it has not seen, from its own gauge record
models.question: A river's flow in an unseen decade, from its own record
models.summary: BasinDetective reads a river basin's daily precipitation, temperature and potential evaporation and its gauged streamflow for about nine years, plus the weather of another decade. It says how six flow signatures change in that other decade (mean flow, runoff ratio, baseflow index, low flow Q5, high flow Q95, half-flow date), whether a reservoir holding more than 10 % of the annual flow sits upstream, and four hidden properties (slow-store time constant, groundwater share, soil capacity, precipitation multiplier), each with an error bar. It was trained only on 20,000 WaterSim basins driven by real ERA5-Land weather from non-exam years, and examined once on 619 real CAMELS-US basins, predicting 1989-99 from 1999-2008. v1.1 (27 Nov 2026) is the same recipe with a symmetric prior on the decadal precipitation drift; the ratchet promoted it and its one exam gave: level with calibrated GR4J on mean flow (rho 0.77 vs 0.79), Q5, Q95, BFI and half-flow date, a loss on runoff ratio (0.44 vs 0.50), median errors worse than v1.0's on five of six changes, and bars that are too wide; regulation detection did not transfer.
models.disclaimer: Research model. On the change between decades it is level with a per-basin calibrated GR4J model on five of six signatures and behind it on mean flow; its reservoir detector is at chance on real basins (AUC 0.49), and its four hidden properties have no real truth (graded on simulated twins only).
models.reads: Daily basin-average precipitation P (mm/day), mean temperature T_mean (°C) and potential evaporation PET (mm/day) for a gauged period of about 9 water years (trained on 9), the gauged streamflow Q (mm/day over the basin; NaN = missing) on the same days, and P, T_mean and PET for the target period (trained on 10 water years). Exam inputs: 1999-10..2008-09 forcing and Caravan Q, and 1989-10..1999-09 forcing.
returns: Change from the gauged to the target decade of six signatures, each mean ± 1 sigma: log ratio of mean flow, runoff ratio, baseflow index (Lyne-Hollick), log ratio of Q5, log ratio of Q95, half-flow date (days); plus the implied target-decade level with its 68 % range
p_regulated: probability that upstream reservoir storage exceeds 10 % of the mean annual flow (temperature 1.3, fitted on dev), and log10(storage / annual flow) ± sigma (sigma not calibrated)
Four hidden properties ± sigma, no real truth: slow-store recession time constant (days), groundwater share of flow, soil water capacity (mm), true / forcing precipitation in the gauged decade
Error bars are widened by one dev-fitted factor per output (×1.00-1.73; Detective.sig_scale); divide by it for the raw ensemble sigma
models.network: Five MLPs (seeds), each 150 inputs → 2 × 256 GELU (dropout 0.1) → 23 outputs (means and log sigmas of 11 Gaussian targets, one logit for regulation); 110,359 weights each, 551,795 in all. Inputs: 150 engineered features of both decades' climate and their differences, gauged signatures, flow-duration curve, monthly regime, recession, baseflow filters, rain-flow lag correlations, autocorrelation and seasonal damping; robust-standardised (median / IQR of the bank), clipped to ±6. Gaussian NLL + binary cross-entropy, AdamW, one-cycle schedule, 60 epochs on 20,000 basins (banks v3 + v4). Ensemble: mean of means; variance = mean member variance + spread of means; × dev widen factor.
models.noise: Not real recordings: the gauge noise is a model fitted to real dev records. Dev twins showed real USGS daily values are smoother than WaterSim's default gauge noise (more flat days, fewer rising days); v2 fits an AR(1) multiplicative error (rho 0.999, cv 0.02) plus rounding to 3 significant figures in cfs (0.01 cfs floor) to the dev records' day-to-day features. Forcing error (precipitation multiplier, daily, annual and decadal error, snow undercatch, temperature offset) is laid between the TRUE forcing the simulator runs on and the SEEN forcing the network reads.

approach.real_backdrop: Real ERA5-Land daily forcing of CAMELS basins from the free window 1951-1988 drives 75 % of the simulated basins
approach.physics_inputs: Classical hydrological signatures and filters of the gauged record (Lyne-Hollick and Eckhardt baseflow, recession constants, flow-duration curve, half-flow date) and the climate shift between decades (precipitation, PET, aridity, snow fraction)

exam.summary: 619 CAMELS-US exam basins, gauged protocol: the network reads 1999-2008 forcing and flow and 1989-99 forcing and predicts the change of six signatures; truth is each basin's own 1989-99 record. v1.0 was run once (training/exam.json); v1.1 (rung R6s, promoted 27 Nov 2026) was run once on the same basins with the same code (training/exam_v11.py; training/exam_v11.json, exam_v11_per_basin.csv, exam_v11_rescore.json). The rows below are v1.1's, each note giving v1.0's value and verdict. The fairest classical baseline is GR4J+snow calibrated per basin on the same 1999-2008 flow (WaterData), scored as its model-implied change; also GR4J's simulated 1989-99 minus the observed 1999-2008 value, Budyko-Fu with w fitted on 1999-2008, and no change. No NWM, regionalisation or dev-tuned baseline exists for the change task (NWM was not fetched). Intervals: seen re-score of 18 Nov 2026 (training/rescore.py), which reproduces exam.json; paired bootstrap over the 619 basins (10,000 resamples, seed 20261118) of the model minus each baseline, per-basin values in training/exam_per_basin.csv, summary in training/exam_rescore.json. Verdict: loss if any baseline is better with an interval excluding 0, win only if every baseline is beaten that way, else tie. The unpaired Fisher-z / Zou intervals of the import stay in each note as a cross-check. Result: on the six changes, a loss on mean flow (to GR4J model-implied, -0.036 [-0.063, -0.008]) and five ties; all six median-error rows tie; levels: wins on mean flow, runoff ratio, Q5 and Q95, ties on BFI and half-flow date; regulation at chance on all three HydroATLAS truths; against USGS peak codes 5/6 (11 positives) above chance, AUC 0.711 [0.543, 0.863], but level with the classical scores.

rows.note: v1.1 (27 Nov 2026); v1.0: 0.22, 0.11, 0.24, -0.06, 0.24, 0.90. Where the forcing misses precipitation, every method fails on the volume changes.

wins: Needs no per-basin calibration and stays level with a GR4J model calibrated on each basin's own 1999-2008 flow on five of six changes (paired intervals include 0), and gives an error bar with every answer. v1.1 closed the mean-flow gap from a loss (-0.036 [-0.063, -0.008]) to a tie (-0.025 [-0.051, +0.001]).

Beats 'no change' in median error, paired intervals excluding 0, on mean flow (0.092 vs 0.184), runoff ratio (0.032 vs 0.038), Q95 (0.117 vs 0.204) and half-flow date (6.1 vs 8.3 days); beats calibrated GR4J's median error on Q5 (0.120 vs 0.163).

Direction: with the symmetric prior the forward-plus-reverse sum of predicted mean-flow change on 51 paired dev basins is -0.040 (median; v1.0 -0.149), and identical forcing in both periods no longer gives a decline on all four packaged basins (v1.1: -0.039 to +0.086; v1.0: -0.130 to -0.002).

Levels of the 1989-99 signatures: wins against both the basin's own 1999-2008 value and GR4J on mean flow, runoff ratio, Q5 and Q95 (paired intervals, but by only +0.004 to +0.007 Spearman: practically equal, since the own record alone scores 0.97-0.98); far ahead of GR4J on BFI (0.979 vs 0.787) and Q5 (0.975 vs 0.778).
Error bars are never too narrow on the changes: 95 % bars cover 95-99 % of exam basins.
losses: Runoff-ratio change (v1.1): rho 0.439 against 0.499 for calibrated GR4J's model-implied change, paired difference -0.059 [-0.111, -0.008]: a loss (v1.0 was level, 0.453). Mean-flow change, median error 0.092 against 0.077 for Budyko-Fu: a loss (v1.0 0.083, level). v1.1 predicts a median mean-flow change of +0.197 where the exam's is +0.173 (v1.0 +0.133): the symmetric prior removed a downward pull and overshot.

Median errors of v1.1 are worse than v1.0's on five of six changes (mean flow 0.083 → 0.092, runoff ratio 0.030 → 0.032, BFI 0.0185 → 0.0198, Q95 0.108 → 0.117, half-flow date 5.97 → 6.07 days); only Q5 improved (0.126 → 0.120). Its rank correlations improved on five of six.

Regulation does not transfer: v1.1 AUC 0.483 [0.392, 0.574] against HydroATLAS storage > 10 % (37 positives), indistinguishable from chance (0.5), against 0.91 on simulated basins (val-v4s); 100 false alarms for 5 hits at p > 0.5 (v1.0: 0.485, 92 for 5). Storage > 50 % (0.52) and any reservoir (0.44) are at chance too. Against USGS peak codes 5/6 (11 positives) it is above chance, AUC 0.693 (v1.0 0.711), but not better than GR4J misfit or seasonal damping.
On BFI and Q5 changes its median error is no better than 'no change' (v1.1 0.0198 vs 0.0181; 0.120 vs 0.129; paired intervals include 0).

The 68 % bars are too wide: 73-88 % of exam truths fall inside (v1.1; v1.0 73-83 %). The widen-only factors were fitted on the 1980s dev window, which drifted more than the exam decade; v1.1's factors are larger on mean flow (1.39 vs 1.15) and runoff ratio (1.20 vs 1.05).
Where ERA5-Land undercatches (gauged runoff ratio > 1, 42 basins), mean-flow change rho 0.19 (GR4J 0.21; v1.0 0.22).
On the BFI and half-flow-date levels it adds nothing measurable over its own record (BFI) or GR4J (half-flow date).
limits: Weather data caps every method: the forcing is ERA5-Land, which under-catches mountain and Pacific Northwest precipitation (50 of the 671 CAMELS-US basins have a 1989-99 runoff ratio above 1, 44 in 1999-2008; 42 of the 619 exam basins in the gauged decade) and drifts about 6 % between decades (more precipitation in the 1980s). Literature numbers from Daymet- or NLDAS-forced LSTMs (NSE about 0.69-0.76) are not comparable.

Gauged mode only: it needs about nine water years of the basin's own daily flow. Trained on 9 gauged and 10 target water years of CAMELS-US / ERA5-Land; other regions, record lengths and forcing products are extrapolation.
The decadal drift (v3) was measured on dev twins for 1980-89 vs 1999-2008 and scaled linearly to the 9.5-year exam separation; it is one number for all regions.

Simulated reservoirs follow generic operating policies; CAMELS-US basins are chosen to be minimally impacted, and HydroATLAS upstream volumes can be wrong where a pour point snaps to a larger river. The log-storage sigma is not calibrated.

Hidden properties have no real truth in this data package; 'slow store' means a different store in each model structure (HBV lower box, GR4J routing store linearised, SAC-SMA lower primary, VIC-lite ARNO baseflow), and the precipitation-multiplier twins all have m = 1.

Rule notes: dev data were used both to fit physics and to gate rungs (the decadal-drift mean was fitted on the dev basins and gated on the same dev basins: partly in-sample). models.name: ReservoirPilot
models.tagline: A daily dam release policy learned in a simulator, graded on 244 real US reservoirs
models.question: Today's release from one dam, from what its operator knows
models.summary: ReservoirPilot picks each day's release for one reservoir from what an operator knows that day: storage, capacity, today's inflow, recent inflow, the demand calendar, the safe channel capacity Qmax and the calibration-period inflow normal. It never sees future inflow. A 5,314-weight network learned it only in simulation, by back-propagating WaterData's cost J through the reservoir mass balance on WaterSim inflows with simulated historical operators. It was graded once on WaterData's frozen exam. On 27 Nov 2026 every arm was re-scored on the causal version of that task (capacity from the dam's metadata and the calibration half only; the numbers below): on 244 real ResOpsUS dams its median J is 0.0154 (90 % interval 0.0099-0.0203), against 0.0289 for a classical flood-pool and hedging rule tuned on the same simulator, 0.109 for SOP and 0.183 for the real operators; it beats the tuned rule on 62 % of dams (95 % interval 56-68 %). Perfect-foresight DP, a bound, reaches 0.0061. The caveat belongs beside the headline: J charges nothing for stored water, so the pilot keeps a median 38 % of capacity full where SOP keeps 59 %.
models.disclaimer: Research benchmark, not an operating tool. J, WaterData's cost, charges for shortage against a calibrated demand and for releases above a safe channel capacity, and nothing else: not for stored water, evaporation, environmental flows, hydropower value or dam safety. The policy exploits that: it holds reservoirs lower than SOP does.
models.reads: Daily, for one reservoir: storage S (hm³), capacity (hm³), today's inflow I (m³/s, as recorded, which for ResOpsUS is usually back-calculated from storage changes), and the task WaterData builds from the calibration half of the record: the demand calendar D(doy) (median release by day of year, 31-day smoothed), Qmax (99th-percentile release) and the inflow climatology by day of year. Fifteen features: S/cap, asinh(I/Qmax), 5-, 20- and 60-day inflow means, D and the next-30-day mean demand over Qmax, log capacity in days of Qmax, headroom, SOP spill pressure, storage in days of demand, the next 30- and 90-day inflow normal and two expected-overflow terms. Never future inflow, future storage or the observed release.
returns: Today's release (m³/s), applied through WaterData's mass balance: capped by the water stored, anything above capacity spills and counts as release
The two decisions behind it: h, the share of demand released (h < 1 hedges, rationing now to keep water for later), and e, an extra release toward 1.25 × (Qmax − D) that makes flood space
No error bars: it is a policy, scored by WaterData's cost J = mean daily (shortage / demand)² + 10 (excess over Qmax / Qmax)²
models.network: MLP 15 → 64 → 64 → 2, tanh, 5,314 weights (plus 30 feature-scaling numbers). Two sigmoid outputs h and e give the requested release R = h·D + 1.25·e·max(Qmax − D, 0); output biases start near SOP (4.5, −5.5). Trained by direct policy optimisation: torch back-propagation through WaterData's mass balance and cost over 270- to 1,000-day windows, then a 365-day SOP tail so leftover storage is valued by what it does next; loss mean log(J + 0.03); Adam, gradient clip 1, cosine learning rate, 96 windows per batch; checkpoints chosen on the simulated selection set. numpy inference, about 0.15 s per 10-year dam.
models.noise: Simulated, with ranges set on real dams: back-calculated inflow noise I_obs = I + (e_t − e_t−1)/K, e ~ N(0, σ·cap), which gives negative-inflow days as in ResOpsUS (dev and aux dams: median 2 % of days, up to 35 %); an upstream regulating reservoir on 30 % of tasks and gross data spikes on 10 %; a non-stationary scored decade (× exp(N(0, 0.3))); and the simulated operator's AR(1) release noise, which shapes demand and Qmax as real operators' records do.

approach.real_backdrop: Half the simulated inflows are WaterSim basins driven by real ERA5-Land forcing of CAMELS donor basins in non-exam years (via Caravan); the other half use the stochastic weather generator
approach.physics_inputs: Mass-balance features: headroom (cap − S), SOP spill pressure (S + I·K − D·K − cap), storage in days of demand, and expected overflow from the calibration-half inflow normal over the next 30 and 90 days
approach.physics_anchor: SOP: the head R = h·D + 1.25·e·(Qmax − D)+ starts at release-the-demand (h ≈ 1, e ≈ 0), and every release passes through WaterData's mass balance, which caps it by the water stored and spills above capacity; training differentiates J through that balance

split.exam: The other 250 core dams (at least 10 years of simultaneous storage, inflow and release, known capacity); 244 have a scorable second half. Per dam: the first half of the record from 1980 calibrates demand, Qmax, capacity (with GRanD) and the climatologies; the second half (longest gap-free block, at most 10 years) is scored from the observed start storage with the observed inflow. Causal version (re-score of 27 Nov 2026, the numbers on this card): the record is split before gaps are interpolated, the split day is in the scored half only, and the scored half no longer raises capacity (37 of the 244 dams change capacity, 169 change Qmax slightly, 3 change start day). exam.short: 244 real ResOpsUS dams + 15 CDEC reservoirs, once
exam.summary: WaterData's frozen reservoir exam, run once after the ratchet was closed (training/final_exam.py, training/exam_results.json). Medians over dams of the cost J and of each of its components. Baselines on the same dams and decades: the classical flood-pool and hedging rule grid-tuned on the simulator (on g4, rung c2: the fairest baseline; and on g1, rung c1), WaterData's storage-target rule curve, the real operators' record, SOP and the perfect-foresight DP bound. Intervals: the 90 % bootstrap interval of the median J as shipped (dams resampled); the exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95 % interval of the paired win fractions (ties count against the pilot). Per-dam scores of the re-score are in training/rescore_per_dam.csv, the intervals in training/rescore_exam.json. J charges nothing for storage: the storage rows sit right after the headline. On 18 Nov 2026 the release was re-scored on the rebuilt data (a reproduction: every shipped median reproduces) and two things were added, both on the already-seen exam: the same classical rule tuned on the 15 dev dams (dev-tuned rule), and paired bootstrap intervals over dams (10,000 resamples, seed 20261118) of the difference in median between the pilot and each baseline; a verdict is win or loss only if that 95 % interval excludes zero. The Clopper-Pearson intervals stay as a cross-check. On 27 Nov 2026 every arm (the pilot, both sim-tuned rules, the dev-tuned rule, WaterData's four baselines) was re-scored once more on the causal version of the task (owner-approved; a dated supplementary exam on a seen exam, nothing chosen): training/rescore_exam_causal.json, training/rescore_per_dam_causal.csv. The rows below are that re-score; the exam-definition values are in the NOTEBOOK beside them. CDEC is unchanged (its task was already causal).

baselines.name: Dev-tuned rule (added on import, seen exam)

rows.note: Causal task. Paired bootstrap (95 %, 20 dams): g4 rule −0.0140 (−0.0299 to +0.0019), level; dev-tuned rule −0.0065 (−0.0207 to +0.0059), level; SOP −0.046 (−0.101 to −0.017). DP 0.0033. Small groups (medians only): navigation (7 dams) pilot 0.125, g4 rule 0.148, SOP 0.155; recreation (4) 0.030, 0.034, 0.690 (exam definition 0.017, 0.020, 0.691: grand_1595's capacity is 154 hm³ instead of 262, and its pilot J 0.060 instead of 0.033); other (3) 0.052, 0.072, 0.056.

wins: The best causal policy on WaterData's reservoir exam: median J 0.0154 on 244 real dams against 0.0289 for the classical flood-pool and hedging rule tuned on the same simulator, 0.109 for SOP and 0.183 for the real operators; it beats the tuned rule on 62 % of dams (95 % interval 56-68 %), SOP on 85 % (80-89 %) and the record on 95 % (91-97 %). Causal task, every arm re-scored 27 Nov 2026 (the exam definition gave 0.0154 against 0.0285); the paired bootstrap of the median difference excludes zero against every causal baseline, including the same rule tuned on the 15 real dev dams (0.0322; −0.0168, −0.0260 to −0.0112).
It holds on the 151 dams whose records close the mass balance (0.0162 vs 0.0304 for the tuned rule) and on flood-control, irrigation, hydropower and supply dams alike.
Floods: its worst release above Qmax is a median 4 % of Qmax, against 97 % for SOP and 27 % for the real operators.
Trained only in simulation: no real reservoir record was a training sample; the exam was opened once, after the ratchet closed.
losses: It buys part of its J with stored water, which J does not charge for: median storage 38 % of capacity against SOP's 59 % and DP's 68 %. It ends at least 20 % of capacity lower than it started on 34 % of dams (SOP 21 %; confirmed by both re-scores); on the 15 CDEC reservoirs the median end − start is −0.10 of capacity. The dev-tuned rule keeps 62 % on average and ends that low on only 18 % of dams, at J 0.0322.

It loses to SOP on 35 of 244 dams (14 %; 37 under the exam definition), mostly irrigation or supply reservoirs (23 of 35), large (median 1.85 years of inflow against 0.79 for all exam dams), 89 % of them in a scored decade drier than the calibration one (74 % of all dams).
It rations often: release below demand on a median 67 % of days, and its shortage ratio (6.6 %) is worse than SOP's (1.0 %) and the tuned rule's (3.8 %).
It exceeds Qmax on more days a year than any comparator (2.9 against 2.2 for SOP and 0 for the tuned rule), by small amounts.

On the 15 CDEC reservoirs (WY2021-2025) it only ties the tuned rules: median difference −0.016 against the sim-tuned rule (95 % −0.039 to +0.0005) and −0.010 against the dev-tuned rule (−0.026 to +0.002).
Perfect-foresight DP is still 2.5 × lower (0.0061): the pilot has no inflow forecast.
limits: J is the whole objective. It ignores stored water, evaporation, minimum environmental flows, hydropower head, water-quality and dam-safety rules; a policy tuned to J is not a policy to operate a dam with.
Single reservoir, daily step: no cascades, no evaporation (the benchmark ignores it), no minimum flow, demand a fixed calendar from the calibration half.
The calibration half sets demand, Qmax and the inflow normal; when the scored decade is drier, the policy keeps releasing for a normal that no longer comes (its known failure on large supply dams).
ResOpsUS inflow is mostly back-calculated from storage changes: 189 of the 678 ResOpsUS dams have negative inflows somewhere, and 93 of the 244 exam dams fail the mass-balance check.

Weather data: the simulated training inflows are driven by ERA5-Land, which under-catches mountain and Pacific Northwest precipitation (50 CAMELS basins have a runoff ratio above 1) and drifts about 6 % between decades; this caps every Watershed method. The exam runs on recorded ResOpsUS inflow, so it enters ReservoirPilot only through the training inflows. Literature streamflow numbers (Daymet- or NLDAS-forced LSTMs, NSE about 0.69-0.76) are not comparable.

Rule notes: aux-dam statistics (6 complete dams, inflow ratios on 29) set the generator's ranges; the climatology features use each exam dam's calibration-half inflow, as WaterData's rule curve does; the dev dams both set generator ranges and gate rungs (partly in-sample); two void training runs (missing optimiser step) were removed and logged. The dev-tuned rule was tuned (on dev only) and scored after the exam had been seen.

Capacity (audit, 25 Nov 2026): v1.0's exam (and make_task) took capacity as the larger of the metadata value and the highest storage observed, including the scored window, so a later observation could raise the capacity an earlier release sees; the loader also interpolated gaps before splitting and put the split day in both halves. Since v1.0.1 (27 Nov 2026) make_task and pipeline.py use the calibration half only, and every arm was re-scored that way: median J moved by at most 0.0011 (rule curve), the pilot's by 0.00001, and no verdict changed. WaterData's frozen tables in shared/water/data/proc/baselines stay on the exam definition (run_baselines_reservoir.py --causal writes the causal ones). The six packaged demo dams (examples/exam_dams.json) are still the v1.0 tasks: two of them change capacity under the causal task (grand_148 4,414 → 4,367 hm³, grand_470 39.09 → 39.04 hm³).
help: A fresh reservoir exam: every row here is on an exam that has now been seen (the dev-tuned rule was tuned and scored after it was opened). Newer ResOpsUS releases or other agencies' records after 2020 would give an unseen test.
Reservoir evaporation and operating rules (minimum flows, flood-control curves) for the exam dams, to make J closer to a real operator's objective.
next: A storage-aware objective: report and train under J plus a carry-over or head term to price the low-storage behaviour, or condition the policy on an operator-chosen storage floor.
MPC, or an inflow-forecast input (FlowCast's nowcast is a natural partner): DP is still 2.5 × lower, mostly from future-inflow information.
Adaptation to a drier or wetter decade: a 1-3 year inflow moving-average feature that lets demand and the inflow normal drift online, and a wider g4 spread.
Cascades, evaporation, minimum flows and an hourly flood mode.

Upstream to WaterSim: the reservoir task generator (operator-derived demand and Qmax, back-calculated inflow noise, upstream regulation and spikes, the non-stationary decade factor), and the realdata.random_forcing window arithmetic fix (span × 365 days is shorter than DateOffset(years=span), so 20-year draws can end a few days inside the exam period; the guard raises and ReservoirPilot redraws).

physics.summary: Reservoir water balance, WaterData's exam benchmark unchanged: S(t+1) = S(t) + (I − R)·K with K = 0.0864 hm³ per m³/s·day, release capped by the water stored, spill above capacity counted as release, no evaporation. The training inflows come from WaterSim, the Watershed simulator: generated basins run through HBV, GR4J, SAC-SMA or VIC-lite with degree-day or energy-balance snow and channel routing. A simulated historical operator runs each dam's first decade, and the task (demand, Qmax, climatologies, start storage) is then built from that record exactly as WaterData builds it from a real one.
checks: WaterSim (shared/water/checks): GR4J vs airGR 1.7.9 to 1.0e-7 mm (NSE 0.79882 vs the published 0.7988); HBV vs TUWmodel 1.1-1 identical to ≤ 1e-12 mm; water balance closes in 121/121 runs, worst 1.4e-15 relative; replaying observed inflow and release on the 15 dev dams ends within a median 5 % of capacity (reservoir_dev.json)

Task reproduction: WaterData's own functions (doy_curve, cost, simulate, dp) are imported, not copied; dev baselines match WaterData's per-dam table to 1.6e-9 and the exam medians exactly (one historical value differs by 3e-5; status doc, not in a shipped file). Re-checked on import: the shipped baseline medians equal shared/water/data/proc/baselines/reservoir_scores.parquet (SOP 0.108372, rule 0.142997, historical 0.183264, DP 0.006254)

Policy equivalence (training/checks_equiv.json, check_js.json): numpy policy vs WaterData's operating loop 8.3e-17 in J; vs the torch training rollout 1.4e-8 in J; the shipped page's JavaScript vs Python 5.0e-15 (release / Qmax) on 5 dev dams, 1,100 days. The site instrument (TypeScript) vs the Python module: 1.5e-14 on 30 cases, WaterData's DP included

Causal re-score (27 Nov 2026, seen; training/rescore_exam.py with RESERVOIRPILOT_TASK=causal): every arm on the causal task; the re-scored baselines match the table WaterData's run_baselines_reservoir.py --causal wrote (SOP, rule curve, DP exactly on 244 dams; historical on one dam by 1.9e-4); CDEC unchanged

Reproduction re-score (18 Nov 2026, seen; training/rescore_exam.py): on the rebuilt ResOpsUS / CDEC data (build.py --only verify passed, splits sha256 33f88ca0...), the released weights through the shipped exam path reproduce every median, win fraction and bootstrap interval of the shipped exam log to < 1e-5; re-scored baselines match WaterData's shipped per-dam table on 244 dams (SOP and rule curve to 1e-12; historical on one dam by 3.1e-5, DP on one dam by 1.2e-4) and the CDEC table on 15 reservoirs

Generator vs reality: on g4's frozen set SOP and DP have median J 0.105 and 0.0069; on the real exam 0.108 and 0.0063 (known from the brief, not tuned to). The status doc's g4 rule-curve median 0.165 (exam 0.143) is not in a shipped file

Twin test (dev dams, training/twin_r1_dpo_hd_g1_g1.json; weights of rung r3): replacing each dev dam's inflow with its 5-day mean moved the pilot's median J only from 0.0361 to 0.0359 (SOP 0.0964 to 0.0683), so gauge noise was not the main sim-to-real gap; that pointed at non-stationary decades and led to g4

ladders.name: ReservoirPilot v1.0 (WaterSim inflow + simulated operators, 18 Nov 2026)
ladders.objective: S_J = 1 − median J(policy) / median J(SOP) on the frozen simulated set of the current generator version (300 tasks per version, seeds 9000+; WaterData's cost J and mass balance, the whole scored window from the task's start storage). Final generator g4; the g1-g3 columns are re-scores on the earlier frozen sets.
ladders.rule: Keep if S_J on the frozen set beats the incumbent's by more than 0.01 AND the median J on the 15 real dev dams is at most 1.05 × the incumbent's (the first rung: at most SOP's dev median, 0.0964). Checkpoints are chosen on a separate simulated selection set (200 tasks per version, seeds 7000+), never on the frozen set or real data.

models.name: FireCast
models.tagline: Where a wildfire will have burned by tomorrow afternoon, cell by 90 m cell
models.question: Tomorrow's burned area of a wildfire
models.summary: FireCast gives every 90 m cell around a burning wildfire the probability that it has burned by the next afternoon VIIRS overpass, about 24 h later. It reads today's observed fire (FEDS burned area and active fire line, VIIRS S-NPP hot spots at the issue and the night overpass) and gridMET daily weather for today and tomorrow. It is a small U-Net (374k weights) trained only on 1,083 FireSim fires burned on real LANDFIRE landscapes with real HRRR weather and observed through an emulated satellite. Graded once on 3,030 real exam fires (25,105 growth fire-days, 2012-24), it beats every baseline: mean AP 0.323 [0.318, 0.328] and F1 0.239 against 0.252 and 0.184 for the best one, yesterday's growth measured from the active fire line. It wins in every period, region and size class, and on the 48 replay fires it more than doubles the calibrated physics replay (AP 0.351 against 0.165). It loses on total burned-area overlap, where persistence still wins (Dice 0.964 against 0.922), and its probabilities above about 0.35 are over-confident: a 0.9 forecast burned 61 % of the time.
models.disclaimer: Research model. It forecasts the satellite view of a fire (FEDS perimeters from 375 m VIIRS hot spots, 12-hourly), not ground truth, and it has never seen suppression tactics, plume-driven runs or wind-event nights. Not for evacuation, firefighting or any safety decision.
models.reads: One fire-day on a 90 m grid, north up (the release used EPSG:5070 CONUS Albers windows from FireData), covering the burned area plus at least 10 km on each side: the burned area at the issue (afternoon) overpass (boolean grid); optionally the burned area 24 h earlier and the FEDS active fire line; VIIRS S-NPP detections at the issue overpass and the night overpass 12 h earlier (fractional row and column of the pixel centre, pixel size along scan and track in km, FRP in MW); gridMET daily values for the issue day and the next day: wind speed (m/s) and direction (deg, from), minimum relative humidity (%), maximum temperature (°C), VPD (kPa), precipitation (mm), 100-h fuel moisture (%), plus the grid convergence angle; whether this is the fire's first detected day. Optional (mode L): LANDFIRE FBFM40 fuel model, slope (deg), aspect (deg) and canopy cover (%).
returns: P(cell burned by the next afternoon VIIRS overpass), every cell of the grid, calibrated on dev only (p = sigmoid(logit / 1.44 − 1.23), widen-only temperature); reliable up to about 0.35, over-confident above (forecast 0.9 → 61 % burned)
A yes/no map at the dev-fitted threshold 0.10 (it over-predicts the new area about 1.9× at the median exam fire-day)
models.network: U-Net on 90 m patches: stem at 90 m (16 channels), encoder 32-48-64-64 to 1.44 km, decoder with skip connections, BatchNorm folded, 374k weights (373,122 in the weight file). 22 map channels: burned now, yesterday's growth, fire line, two VIIRS FRP rasters (issue and night), distances to the burn, the fire line and the nearest hot spot, the offset from the nearest fire-line cell along and across tomorrow's wind, the 10 km scoring zone, and 11 LANDFIRE channels (fuel groups, slope, uphill vector, canopy cover, a landscape flag; zero in the default exam mode F). 22 scalars (16 gridMET features for today and tomorrow, 6 fire features: area, yesterday's radial growth, flags, hot-spot count, fire-line share) through a 2-layer MLP that adds a per-channel bias (FiLM-style) at every level and to the head. Loss: BCE on unburned cells in the 10 km zone. 128-cell random crops × 12, dihedral augmentation, landscape dropout 0.5, Adam; 1,800 + 1,200 steps for the released rung. CPU only, one thread; a rung takes about 30 min.
models.noise: No real recordings are laid into the training signals. Observation noise comes from firesim.observe (VIIRS detection against FRP, scan-angle footprints, overpass timing, clouds) and the dev-fitted FEDS emulator; the weather the network reads is the HRRR series pushed through a dev-fitted gridMET operator plus its residual noise; landscapes and HRRR weather are real, from dev fires and guard-passed non-exam windows.

approach.real_backdrop: Real LANDFIRE landscapes (dev-fire windows and guard-passed non-exam windows, 70 % of training fires) and real hourly HRRR weather drive every simulated fire
approach.physics_inputs: Distances to the burned area, the active fire line and the VIIRS hot spots; the offset from the nearest fire-line cell projected along and across tomorrow's wind; wind as a spread-toward vector in grid coordinates; optional LANDFIRE fuel groups, slope and uphill vector

exam.summary: Every exam growth fire-day, scored like FireData's baselines: unburned cells within 10 km of the burned area at issue time, AP over the cell ranking and F1 of the yes/no map on the newly burned cells, averaged over growth fire-days, with 95 % bootstrap intervals that resample whole fires (training/results/exam_summary_r2.json). Each method's interval is its own (not a paired interval on the difference: the per-fire-day rows were not shipped); on every row marked win the intervals do not overlap. Baselines (FireData, the same fire-days): persistence (no growth), the climatological median growth, yesterday's growth repeated from the whole perimeter, and yesterday's growth measured from the active fire line (the best); on the 48 replay fires also FireSim run forward with the dev-calibrated replay settings (replay_calibration.json as stored), deterministic and as a 12-member ensemble. The baselines' F1 is at 0.5 on their distance score; FireCast's at its dev-fitted threshold 0.10.

More than doubles the dev-calibrated physics replay of its own simulator on the 48 replay fires: AP 0.351 (the released mode F; 0.355 with LANDFIRE inputs, mode L) against 0.165 for the 12-member ensemble, F1 0.265 (mode L 0.271) against 0.217. Probabilities up to about 0.35, where 99.4 % of the scored exam cells sit, are close to the diagonal (slightly under-confident at 0.10-0.25: a 0.12 forecast burned 13.5 %).
losses: Total burned-area overlap: persistence (draw no growth) wins, median Dice 0.964 against 0.922. At its threshold FireCast over-predicts the new area 1.9× at the median fire-day.
Over-confident above about 0.35: a 0.9 forecast burned 61 % of the time, a 0.97 one 65 %.
Its F1 depends on the dev-fitted threshold 0.10, at the low edge of the searched grid; at 0.5 it is 0.058, below the growth baselines.
Sim AP 0.59 against real dev AP 0.32: the simulated fires are more predictable than real ones.
limits: It forecasts the FEDS/VIIRS picture of a fire (375 m detections, 12-hourly perimeters), not ground truth.
Probabilities above about 0.35 are over-confident; the widen-only calibration (2 numbers) cannot reshape the curve. The yes/no threshold (0.10) sits at the edge of the searched grid (0.10-0.60).

Simulator gaps: no suppression tactics beyond growing containment, no plume-driven runs or wind-event nights (handoff: Riverside 2020 burned 496 km² overnight), no fuel change since the LANDFIRE year, and simulated fires grow on 91 % of half-days against 50 % for real ones. Sim AP 0.59 against real dev AP 0.32.

LANDFIRE (mode L) adds little: +0.004 AP on the 627 replay days, +0.001 on all 713 growth days of the replay fires (the card says +0.002 to +0.004), and on dev mode L scores below mode F (0.308 vs 0.316). It exists for just the 48 replay fires; the shipped weights carry the mode F calibration only (mode L: T 1.57, b −1.20 in training/results/cal_r2_L.json).
Only three trained rungs fit on 2 shared CPU cores; rung decisions within ±0.01 AP are at noise level, and no interval on a rung difference can be computed from the shipped files.

Dev fires fed the physics calibration (FEDS emulator, weather operator, the p1 age factor through the twin test) and also gate every rung and fit the calibration: the gate is partly in-sample. The exam was untouched.

Dead-fuel moisture observations (the NFMD moved into FEMS, which has no public download) and ICS-209 suppression records: the twin tests point at persistence and suppression as the largest physics gaps.
Memory and cores: the p1 twin test stopped at 126 of 470 dev days (1.3-1.45 GB), the p1 bank at 35 of 72 shards, and a 12-member replay ensemble on crops over 500k cells needs more than 1.2 GB.

Exam grids (audit, 25 Nov 2026): the archived grids are cropped to the final perimeter and exclude 45-59 % of the nominal 10 km window on two packaged days. Padding 112 unburned cells outward put no exterior cell above 0.10 and moved AP by +0.005, -0.003 and 0.000 on the three packaged Mode-F days, so the network does not lean on the grid edge there. Mode FL with real exterior fuels and issue-time grids remain untested.

Finish twin p1 with lower memory (stream the dev cache), fit a p2 fire-age factor for days 1-10, then re-score r1 (the best rung on dev).
Wind-event nights and suppression: condition the night slow-down on gridMET night wind and RH, add a suppression-effort prior by region and size, and run the twin test by wind tercile.
A lower threshold grid (0.03-0.10) and a 12 h product (the morning overpass as target).
A bigger bank (finish p1: 35 of 72 shards) and the platform's physics p2 (the diagonal line-leak fix U1 and a persistence module), then re-score every rung.

physics.summary: FireSim, the shared fire platform's simulator (shared/fire/firesim): Rothermel 1972 surface spread with Albini 1976, Scott & Burgan 40 fuel models, Anderson 1983 ellipses, Van Wagner 1977 crown initiation, Nelson 2000 dead-fuel moisture, minimum-travel-time spread, spotting and timed containment lines, with a VIIRS/MODIS/GOES detection emulator (firesim.observe). FireCast wraps it, without editing it, in two versioned physics files (training/phys/p0.json, p1.json; training/src/simbank.py). Each training fire burns 2-8 days on a real LANDFIRE landscape with real hourly HRRR weather, in 12 h segments, with a randomised rate-of-spread factor (lognormal, median 0.35 of the dev-calibrated replay level, sd 0.7), night slow-down, growing containment and spotting. p1 adds a fire-age ROS factor fitted to the p0 dev twin test (×2.6 on the first day down to ×0.55 after day 10).
checks: FireSim vs published BehavePlus/Rothermel tables (GTR-371, GTR-143): 436 of 436 within half the last published digit; vs pyretechnics on 6,720 flat and slope cases: ROS median relative difference 4.9e-5, maximum 5.2e-5 (shared/fire/checks)
Uniform-fuel fires against analytic ellipses (55 cases, 30-90 m, 7 wind directions): mean area ratio 0.981, minimum 0.940 (level_set solver 0.992 / 0.973); grid-orientation bias ≤ 3.4 %

Dev physics replays (40 fires, 470 growth days): next-day F1 on new burn 0.153 uncalibrated, 0.194 dev-calibrated in sample (0.184 leave-one-out); new area over-predicted 4-12× (shared/fire/checks/replay_dev.json)

Twin test p0 (training/results/twin_p0.json; 470 dev fire-days × 3 simulated members from the observed start): median log10(simulated / real new area) +0.16 (quartiles −0.58, +0.82); 34 % of real days fell below all three members. The status doc's by-age split (first day −0.44, days 6-10 +0.33, days > 10 +0.35) is not in the shipped file. It led to p1

Twin test p1, partial (stopped at 126 dev fire-days for memory; twin_compare_p0_p1.json): on the same 126 days the first-day median went from −0.82 to +0.20 and days > 10 from +0.44 to +0.01; days 1-10 now about −0.34
FireData's dev baselines reproduced with this pipeline: fire-line baseline dev AP 0.252 (eval_baselines.json)

numpy release == torch to 2.5e-6 in the logits (status doc; export.py checks three random grids); the published page's JavaScript == numpy to 2.1e-6 with float16 weights; the site instrument (TypeScript, float16 weights, inputs rebuilt in the browser) == firecast.py on the same weights to 3.9e-6 on 35 cases (logits and the 22 scalar inputs; site/public/instruments/firecast/reference.json)

models.name: FireSize
models.tagline: Escape probability and final size of a new US wildfire, from its ignition record
models.question: Will a new fire escape, and how big will it get?
models.summary: FireSize reads a US wildfire ignition record (place, date, cause, reporting agency, discovery hour), a 250 m LANDFIRE summary around the point and gridMET weather on the discovery day and the day before. It returns P(escape to ≥ 100 acres), P(≥ 1,000 acres) and the final-size distribution over 12 FPA-FOD size classes with a median and an 80 % range. It is an ensemble of three small MLPs (83,364 weights) trained only on 8,500 simulated ignitions: FireSim free-burn spread in real 90 m LANDFIRE windows under real gridMET weather, then a containment race whose parameters were fitted on 911 real dev ignitions. Graded once on 655,869 real FPA-FOD exam ignitions (2012-2020), it ranks escapes better than climatology (AUC 0.726 vs 0.688) and fire-danger indices (0.634) but not as well as a gradient-boosting model fitted on real dev labels (0.777). It ranks fires that reach 1,000 acres better than every baseline (AUC 0.815 vs 0.803), and beats the GBM in California, the Northwest and the Rocky Mountain region. Its probabilities are about twice too high and its size point estimate is worse than climatology.
models.disclaimer: Its escape probabilities are about twice too high (mean 0.055 against a real 0.027), so read them as a ranking, not as calibrated chances. Research model: not for dispatch or resource decisions.
models.reads: One ignition (CONUS, 2012-2020 in the exam): 75 inputs that `firesize.make_features` builds from 13 x 13 patches of the 250 m LANDFIRE 2016 grids around the point (FBFM40 fuel model code, canopy cover %, canopy height, slope in degrees; fuel class at the point and class fractions in 1.25 km and 3.25 km boxes, mean CC, CH and slope in the 5 x 5 box, slope at the point), gridMET daily values for the discovery day and the day before (ERC, BI, FM100 %, FM1000 %, wind m/s, RHmin and RHmax %, Tmax and Tmin °C, precipitation mm, VPD kPa), the log1p Rothermel head spread rate (m/min) of the fuels under the afternoon weather (point, 5 x 5 and 13 x 13 means, the point the day before), and the record: NWCG cause class, federal reporting agency (0/1), local discovery hour (sin, cos, missing flag), day of year (sin, cos) and one of 9 GACC-like regions. Missing values are filled with the training medians.
returns: P(escape): the chance the final reported size is ≥ 100 acres, from the widened distribution (T = 1.459). Not calibrated: the exam mean is 0.055 against a real rate of 0.027
P(large): the chance of ≥ 1,000 acres

Final-size distribution over the 12 FPA-FOD size classes (< 0.1 acre to ≥ 20,000 acres), widened by one dev-fitted temperature (T = 1.459), with an 80 % range (the 10 % and 90 % points, interpolated in log size within a class); `temp=1.0` gives the raw distribution
Median final size (acres) from the raw T = 1 distribution (decided on dev before the exam)
models.network: An ensemble of 3 MLPs, 75 → 128 → 128 → 12 with ReLU (27,788 weights each, 83,364 in all), averaged after a softmax. Inputs standardised with the training mean and sd; NaN filled with the training medians. Trained in torch with soft-label cross-entropy weighted by the importance weights, AdamW lr 2e-3, batches of 256, up to 60 epochs with early stopping on held-out windows (patience 8), seeds 0/100/200, one CPU thread, a few minutes per rung. One widen-only temperature T = 1.459 on the logits, fitted on the dev calib half by size-class log-likelihood. numpy inference (firesize.py) matches the page's JavaScript to 4 decimals of P(escape).
models.noise: No real recordings are laid into the training signals. The landscapes (90 m LANDFIRE windows near dev ignitions, exam footprints excluded) and the daily weather (gridMET) are real; the ignition attributes are borrowed from dev records. The randomness is in the simulator: pre-discovery burn time, a ROS multiplier, and 24 draws of the calibrated suppression and reporting model per ignition, which give the soft label.

approach.real_backdrop: Real 90 m LANDFIRE windows near dev ignitions (exam footprints excluded by the platform's guard) and real gridMET daily weather drive every simulated ignition; cause, agency, hour and date are borrowed from real dev ignitions
approach.physics_inputs: The log1p Rothermel head spread rate of the LANDFIRE fuels around the point under the afternoon weather (Simard 1-h moisture at Tmax and RHmin, 10 m wind = 1.45 x the daily mean), from a FireSim behave() lookup table: at the point, 5 x 5 and 13 x 13 means, and the point the day before

split.dev: FireData's frozen FireSize split (shared/fire/data/proc/firesize_split.parquet): a seeded 1.5 % of 2012-2019 CONUS ignitions plus FOD fires inheriting a dev MTBS fire, 8,913 in all. Split again by a seeded hash of the FOD_ID (common.dev_half, seed 20261119) into a calib half (suppression fit, 911 twins, widening) and a gate half (4,429 ignitions, the ratchet's dev gate, never used for calibration)
split.exam: Every other FPA-FOD CONUS ignition of 2012-2020: 655,869, of which 582,986 main (2012-19) and 72,883 recent (all of 2020, a whole season held out). Scored once by exam.py (audit file results/exam.started: one line, per the status doc; not shipped) after the ratchet closed. The 8 demo ignitions are a seeded draw (seed 20261126) of two per size group among exam ignitions with a discovery time, drawn after the exam

exam.summary: One run of exam.py on every exam ignition (training/results/exam.json), against FireData's baselines on the same records: the median / prevalence, climatology by region x cause, a logistic model on ERC + BI + wind, and a gradient-boosting model (GBM) fitted on the real labels of the 8,913 dev ignitions with lat/lon, owner, cause, hour, day of year and two days of gridMET. The GBM is a fair and strong baseline: it learns from real fire outcomes, which FireSize never does, and it reads lat/lon and owner, which FireSize cannot. Escape = final size ≥ 100 acres (2.68 % of exam ignitions), large = ≥ 1,000 acres (0.63 %). Size error is the median |log10| error of the median. The only interval shipped is a bootstrap of the all-exam escape-AUC differences (post_exam.py: 100 resamples of ignitions, seed 20261119, results/post_exam.json); no other row has one. The per-region baselines were re-run after the exam with the platform's own code (post_exam.py) and reproduce its stored all-exam AUCs to every digit. v1.0.1 (27 Nov 2026) clips standardised inputs at 8 sd; the released weights were re-scored once on the exam with the clip (an owner-approved, dated supplementary exam; work/results/v1.0_rescore_2026-11-27_zclip8/, with a no-clip run that reproduces v1.0's exam.json exactly). The model values below are that re-score; v1.0's are in each note where they differ at the shown precision. The bootstrap intervals are v1.0's.

baselines.name: FireSize v1.0 (the released behaviour: pt_SB at z = 1e6)

rows.note: Added 27 Nov 2026 (audit). v1.0 gave all 91 the same output: P(escape) exactly 0 and a 1.73-acre median. With the 8 sd clip (v1.0.1): 80 % range coverage 0.96 (v1.0 0.18), size ρ 0.10 (v1.0 undefined), mean P(escape) 0.085, escape AUC 0.667 on 1 escape (v1.0 0.500), Brier 0.0204 (v1.0 0.0110: predicting 0 was right for 90 of 91). One escape in 91 is too few to grade escapes; the size rows are the readable ones. No interval; no baseline was scored on this stratum. A retrain with simulated slash-blowdown ignitions (r8) was rejected by the ratchet (below margin) and the exam was not opened for it.

rows.metric: 80 % size range: share of exam ignitions whose real size class lies inside it (nominal 80 %)
rows.note: Conservative: the widening (T = 1.459) was fitted on dev to the size-class likelihood and brought dev-gate coverage from 0.835 to 0.899. 2020: 91.7 %. By region 83 % (SE) to 96 % (GB, NE/MW). MTBS-matched big fires: 9.4 %.

wins: Large fires: the best of every method at ranking which ignitions reach 1,000 acres (AUC 0.815 against 0.803 for the GBM fitted on real dev labels, 0.767 for climatology), in both 2012-19 and 2020.
Escape ranking beats climatology (+0.039 AUC, 95 % bootstrap +0.035 to +0.044) and the fire-danger indices (+0.093) without ever training on a real fire outcome.

In California (0.739 vs 0.690), the Northwest (0.776 vs 0.735) and the Rocky Mountain region (0.748 vs 0.703) it ranks escapes better than the GBM fitted on real labels, and better than every other baseline there.
losses: Escape ranking overall: AUC 0.727 against 0.777 for the GBM fitted on dev real labels (−0.050, 95 % −0.053 to −0.047); 0.740 against 0.789 in 2020.
Southeast (AUC 0.566 against 0.704) and Southern Plains (0.715 against 0.808), the two biggest gaps; also behind the GBM in the Northern Rockies, Great Basin, Southwest and Northeast/Midwest.
Calibration: mean P(escape) 0.055 against a real rate of 0.027, so its Brier score (0.0273) is worse than predicting the prevalence (0.0260).
Size point estimate: median |log10 error| 0.642 against 0.505 for climatology and 0.510 for the GBM, with a +0.22 log10 bias; it under-sizes the big MTBS fires by 3.3 log10.
limits: Escape probabilities are about twice too high. The widen-only temperature was fitted to the size-class likelihood, not to escape, and raised the dev-gate Brier score from 0.0274 to 0.0285 before the exam; the release kept it as frozen.

Suppression is an effective race model fitted on dev twins, not a measured one: 10 of its 31 fitted parameters sit at a bound (response 0.1 h, line rates 30 times the handbook values, a federal line-rate term of e^−3, a confine-only share of 0.5, ROS spread 0.3, and five more; ratchet.yaml lists them). No validated suppression data (ICS-209) were used.
The simulator has no spotting, no re-burn after containment and no weather after 96 h; daily gridMET is disaggregated to hours. The largest fires are under-sized as a result.

Southeast and Southern Plains: debris, prescribed and agricultural burning, small parcels and dense fast suppression are not in the simulator. LANDFIRE 2016 fuels are stale for 2017-2020 and scarred by 2012-16 fires.

Landscape inputs are 250 m national grids (a coarse summary by design; the simulator ran on 90 m windows). Labels are FPA-FOD reported sizes, rounded to 0.01, 0.1 or 1 acre in most records; complexes and merged fires are booked to one record.

Twin-test ceiling: the network matches the simulator (AUC 0.906 against the simulated twin's outcome), but the simulator matches reality at 0.671. Better networks will not help much; better physics and suppression would.

Rule notes: FireSize read FPA-FOD records straight from the platform's parquet, filtered by its split (common.fod_records), because firedata has no FPA-FOD accessor. It loads the whole 2012-2020 table, then filters; in the shipped scripts only exam.py and, after the exam, post_exam.py and build_release.py select the exam records, and every other script asks for 'dev'. The dev calib half fitted the suppression model, the importance weights and the temperature; the gate half is out of sample. r7 passed the gate AUC test by 0.0004, and no interval was computed for any rung decision.
CONUS, 2012-2020 only (FPA-FOD has no later records); a 2021 or later ignition is outside both the training weather years and the exam.

Slash-blowdown ignitions (audit, 25 Nov 2026): no simulated ignition landed on LANDFIRE codes 201-204, so the point-fuel input pt_SB has sd 1e-6 and a real one enters at z = 1e6. Escape probability is then exactly 0 and the median 1.73 acres whatever the weather. 91 of the 655,869 exam ignitions were scored that way (exact zeros in exam_preds). probs() warns on inputs beyond 8 sd, and since v1.0.1 (27 Nov 2026) z_clip = 8 clips them by default: on the 91, size error 1.237 → 0.750 log10; pooled escape AUC 0.7266 → 0.7264. The clip also touches 19,246 other exam ignitions (every Great Basin one, whose region input sits at z = 8.1, and 2,846 others with shrub or slash-blowdown fractions, rain, slope or wind beyond 8 sd). A simulated bank with 415 slash-blowdown ignitions (rung r8) did not clear the ratchet's margin (+0.008 sim RPSS against +0.01 needed); on 64 held-out simulated slash-blowdown ignitions it scored RPSS 0.127, the clip on r7 0.254, r7 unclipped −1.668.
help: ICS-209 incident records or another source of validated suppression timing and resources, to replace the effective containment race fitted on dev twins.
Fresh fuels: a LANDFIRE layer for 2017-2020 fires (LF2016 is used throughout) and ignition records after 2020 (FPA-FOD ends in 2020).
next: Escape-aware calibration: keep T = 1 for P(escape) and widen only the size tail, or fit the temperature on the escape term. On the dev twins the unwidened escape rate already matches (0.023 vs 0.026). It is likely, but not computed, that T = 1 would also have given a better exam Brier.
Southeast and Southern Plains physics: burnable agricultural and debris-burn fuel states by season, and a WUI or parcel suppression term fitted on dev twins in those regions.
Containment beyond 96 h with real multi-day gridMET for fires that are not contained, to fix the −3.3 log10 under-sizing of MTBS fires.
Model FPA-FOD's reporting granularity (0.1 and 1 acre point masses) inside the simulator's reporting floor.
More twins per region: the guard skipped 45 % of the escaped dev twins; LANDFIRE windows that pass the guard could recover some.
Widen the suppression-parameter bounds or change the race's form; add owner class and position through the simulator (the GBM gains from them between regions).

Simulated banks that cover the Great Basin (1.5 % of the bank, 2.5 % of exam ignitions) and slash-blowdown fuel at their real shares, judged on a frozen set that contains them; the current frozen set has no slash-blowdown ignition, so the ratchet could not see what r8 was for.

physics.summary: FireSim, the shared fire platform's simulator (shared/fire/firesim): Rothermel/Albini surface fire on the 40 Scott & Burgan fuel models, Van Wagner crown fire, minimum-travel-time spread on the real 90 m LANDFIRE window, Nelson dead fuel moisture from hourly weather disaggregated from gridMET, live moisture from the GSI; no spotting. Fires smaller than one 90 m cell (0.81 ha) are tracked as an analytic sub-cell ellipse, because most FPA-FOD fires are. Each simulated fire burns freely for 96 h; a Fried & Fried (1996) containment race then sets its final size: line building starts after a response time and escalates, and the fire is contained when the line built catches the line needed (a share of the ellipse perimeter). FireSize wraps FireSim without editing it, with two physics versions: v0 as shipped and v1 (agriculture, LANDFIRE 93, burns as GR1; an ignition on a non-burnable cell moves to the nearest burnable cell within 180 m).
checks: FireSim (platform checks, shared/fire/checks): 436 of 436 published BehavePlus / GTR values within half the last digit; agreement with pyretechnics to 5e-5 (6,720 cases); uniform-fuel fires grow as the predicted ellipse (mean area ratio 0.981)

Suppression fit (results/calibration/calib_v1rep2.json): twin size-class NLL 3.60 with literature values, 2.64 fitted; 2-fold held out 2.66 / 2.73 against 3.56 / 3.68 for the literature values. Twin escape rate 0.024 against a real 0.026

Twin test (twin.py, 911 dev twins, results/twin_final.json): the released network predicts the escape of the simulated twin of each real ignition at AUC 0.906, but the calibrated simulator predicts the real outcome at only 0.671. The network reads a real ignition the way the simulator does; the ceiling is the physics and suppression model, not the network. The network's own AUC against the real outcome is 0.734

Rothermel inputs: a lookup table from FireSim's behave() (ros_lut.npz, fuel code x 14 1-h moistures x 12 wind speeds). On import, recomputing the four ROS columns of the 8 demo ignitions from their 13 x 13 fuel patches reproduces the exam features to 1.1e-7

The released weights file is byte-identical to the model the exam ran (sha256 72289217…3902 in results/exam.json); demo.py reproduces the exam's P(escape) for its 8 ignitions to 1e-4. The site instrument (TypeScript, float16 weights) matches numpy on the same weights to 1.1e-14 on 104 cases (8 ignitions x 13 what-ifs, Rothermel inputs included); float16 moves P(escape) by at most 6.4e-6 from the float64 release

ladders.name: FireSize v1.0 (FireSim physics v0/v1 × suppression fits, 19 Nov 2026)
ladders.objective: Ranked probability skill score (RPSS over the 12 FPA-FOD size classes, against the frozen set's own importance-weighted class climatology) of the network's distribution against each simulated ignition's soft label (its reported-size distribution over 24 suppression draws), on the frozen simulated validation ignitions (304 frozen windows). One frozen set per physics × suppression version: v0|lit, v0|v0acc (743 ignitions each), v1|v1acc, v1|v1reg, v1|v1rep, v1|v1rep2 (1,175 each). Decisions use the latest, v1|v1rep2.
ladders.rule: Keep if the sim RPSS on the latest frozen set beats the incumbent's on that same set by more than 0.01 AND the dev-gate escape AUC is at least the incumbent's − 0.01 AND the dev-gate size MAE (log10) is at most 1.05 × the incumbent's. Every rung was re-scored on every frozen set and the decisions re-taken in order on v1|v1rep2.

rungs.change: Baseline: FireSim as shipped (physics v0: LANDFIRE agriculture 93 and urban never burn), literature suppression race (IA arrival about 1 h after discovery, handbook line rates by fuel group, escalation doubling in 4 h); 4,800 simulated ignitions; an ensemble of 3 MLPs (71 → 128 → 128 → 12) without the Rothermel inputs
rungs.why: First rung. On its own frozen set (v0|lit) sim RPSS 0.220; re-scored on v1|v1rep2 −0.256. Dev gate escape AUC 0.697, mean P(escape) 0.066 against a real 0.029. Log: base.

rungs.change: Suppression and reporting parameters fitted on 911 dev twins (v0 physics): response time, line rate, escalation, perimeter share, ROS centre, access and slope terms (calib_v0acc)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS −0.292 vs r0 −0.256 on v1|v1rep2 (needs > −0.246); gate AUC 0.675 vs 0.697 (needs ≥ 0.687): both failed. Gate MAE improved 0.725 → 0.694. Log: sim RPSS -0.036 vs r0; gate AUC fails; below margin.

rungs.change: Physics v1: agriculture (93) burns as GR1, and an ignition on a non-burnable cell moves to the nearest burnable cell within 180 m; suppression recalibrated on the twins (calib_v1acc)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS −0.124 vs r0 −0.256 (+0.131); gate AUC 0.757 vs 0.697; gate MAE 0.744 vs 0.725 (+2.6 %, inside 5 %). Twin NLL v1 3.356 vs v0 3.378. The biggest single physical fix: ignitions on non-burnable cells never grew. Log: sim RPSS +0.131 vs r0.

rungs.change: Regional initial-attack response offsets plus per-fuel-group ROS centres, fitted on the dev twins (calib_v1reg)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS +0.163 vs r2, but gate AUC 0.655 vs 0.757 failed. Twin NLL fell to 2.86: the regional offsets fit dev sizes but soak up variance the landscape and weather should explain. Log: sim RPSS +0.163 vs r2; gate AUC fails.

rungs.change: Regional reporting floors (share of fires booked at ≥ 1 acre) instead of regional response offsets, and an escape term in the dev fit (calib_v1rep)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS +0.337 vs r2, but gate AUC 0.634 vs 0.757 failed. Log: sim RPSS +0.337 vs r2; gate AUC fails.

rungs.change: r2 + physics inputs: log1p Rothermel head ROS of the LANDFIRE fuels around the point under the afternoon weather (point, 5 × 5, 13 × 13, and the point the day before)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS −0.139 vs r2 −0.124 (−0.015): below the margin. Gate AUC 0.760 and AP 0.087 were the best so far. Log: sim RPSS -0.015 vs r2; below margin.

rungs.change: Two-mode initial attack (a share of fires only confined or monitored, at 2 % of the line rate), a federal line-rate term and reporting floors, recalibrated (calib_v1rep2)
rungs.why: Sim RPSS +0.389 vs r2 (0.265 vs −0.124); gate AUC 0.766 vs 0.757; gate MAE 0.618 vs 0.744. Twin NLL 2.64 (literature values 3.60). Log: sim RPSS +0.389 vs r2.

rungs.why: Sim RPSS +0.014 vs r5 passed; gate AUC 0.746 vs 0.766 (needs ≥ 0.756) failed. Log: sim RPSS +0.014 vs r5; gate AUC fails.

rungs.why: Sim RPSS +0.015 vs r5 (0.280 vs 0.265); gate AUC 0.756 vs 0.766 (−0.0096, inside the 0.01 tolerance); gate MAE 0.627 vs 0.618 (+1.4 %). Kept; with the widen-only temperature below it is v1.0. Log: sim RPSS +0.015 vs r5.

The cost was visible on dev before the exam: gate Brier 0.0274 → 0.0285 and gate mean P(escape) 0.025 → 0.054 against a real 0.029. Gate MAE here uses the widened median (0.648); the release's point estimate is the T = 1 median (0.627).

models.name: FireDetective
models.tagline: What drove a wildfire, read from its satellite record
models.question: What drove a wildfire, from its satellite record
models.summary: FireDetective reads a wildfire's first six days (up to 12 half-day steps): the FEDS-style burned-area mask at each VIIRS overpass on a 180 m grid, the VIIRS 375 m fire pixels and their fire radiative power, daily gridMET weather, and LANDFIRE fuels, canopy and terrain. A small 1-D CNN (3 seeds, 189k weights) says what drove the fire, with error bars: the share of the burned area MTBS maps as high severity (through a 2-number map from the simulated crown-fire share, fitted on dev), the daily wind on the fire days read with the wind inputs blanked, and live fuel moisture. It was trained only on about 4,100 FireSim fires on real dev landscapes and real HRRR weather, seen through a simulated satellite, and graded once on 944 real exam fires from 2017-23. In forests its severity rank (rho 0.58) ties FWI and ERC (0.54, 0.53) and its error is the lowest (0.088 vs 0.092); across all fuels Van Wagner's crown-fire potential ranks higher (0.55 vs 0.48, not decisive). Blind wind ranks at rho 0.30 against 0.13 for a Rothermel back-calculation, but its error is worse than the dev median. Live fuel moisture fails (MAE 27.7 vs 21.3 % for a climatology).
models.disclaimer: Research model. On 944 real exam fires it ties the best fire-danger indices at ranking forest burn severity and beats them on its error, ranks fire-day wind better than a Rothermel back-calculation but misses its level (worse than guessing the dev median), and fails on live fuel moisture. Its other outputs (spread-rate factor, spotting, initial attack) are simulator readings with no real truth, and several are not identifiable even in simulation.
models.reads: One fire's first 12 half-day steps (S-NPP night ~01:30 and day ~13:30 overpasses), starting at the first step with burned area: cumulative burned-area masks on a 180 m EPSG:5070 grid (real fires: rasterised FEDS-MTBS perimeters), the VIIRS 375 m detections of each step (grid row and column, FRP in MW), a day/night flag, the gridMET day driving each step's growth (tmmx, rmin, rmax, vs, th, fm100, fm1000, erc, bi, pr, vpd), LANDFIRE FBFM40 fuel, canopy cover, height, base height and bulk density, slope and elevation at 180 m, the day of year and the grid convergence angle (pipeline.py turns these into 12 x 25 sequence and 17 static features).
returns: hs ± hs_sd: share of the burned area MTBS maps as high severity: hs = 0.017 + 0.271 x simulated crown-fire share (fitted on 30 dev fires), 1-sigma through the same map
wind, wind_lo, wind_hi: daily-mean 10 m wind on the fire days (m/s, gridMET definition), inferred with the wind inputs blanked; 68 % range (log-normal)
lfmc ± lfmc_sd: live fuel moisture (% dry mass) the fire behaviour implies; fails on the exam

Simulator readings, no real truth: crown (simulated crown-fire share), ros_adj (spread-rate factor vs uncalibrated Rothermel), m1 (afternoon 1-h dead moisture, %), wind_regime (wind- vs slope-driven share), p_spot, p_ia (spotting, initial-attack line)

Error bars are the 3-seed ensemble's sigma (mean variance + spread of means) times a widen-only dev factor: severity x2.53, wind x1.98, LFMC x1.09, fitted so the 80 % band covers 80 % of dev truths (weights/calib.json); FireDetective.raw() gives the unwidened sigmas
models.network: Three 1-D CNNs (seeds), 62,898 weights each, 188,694 in all. Per member: a 25 → 48 linear step embedding (ReLU), two 3-tap convolutions (48 → 64 → 64, ReLU, time mask), mean and max pooling over the valid steps, a 17 → 32 static branch (ReLU), 160 → 128 → 128 (ReLU), Gaussian heads (mean and log-sigma, clipped to [-5, 3]) for 8 regression targets and 2 logistic heads (spotting, initial attack). Gaussian NLL + BCE, Adam, 60 epochs, one CPU thread, about 4 minutes per seed. Ensemble: mean of means; variance = mean member variance + spread of means.
models.noise: Not real recordings. The weather is real (HRRR drives the simulator, the matching gridMET days are the network's input), the landscapes are real dev LANDFIRE windows, and the satellite view is FireSim's VIIRS emulator plus a FEDS-like perimeter emulator tuned on real dev VIIRS pixels. Wind is blanked in half the training samples (wind-blind mode).

approach.real_backdrop: Real dev-fire LANDFIRE landscapes and real HRRR hourly weather drive the simulated fires; the network reads the matching real gridMET days as its weather
approach.physics_inputs: gridMET fire-danger fields (ERC, BI, 100-h and 1000-h dead fuel moisture) and LANDFIRE fuel groups and canopy fuels, beside the observed growth, shape and FRP

split.dev: FireData's frozen split (shared/fire/data/proc/splits.json): 40 dev fires, CONUS 2017-21; 30 have MTBS severity (16 forest), all 40 gridMET wind, 9 Globe-LFMC samples. Dev is used for the FEDS emulator tuning, the twin tests behind physics v2/v3, the ratchet gate, the severity map and the widen-only factors, and R5's rejected re-weighting: the gate is partly in-sample
split.exam: Exam fires 2017-23 with at least one FEDS growth day: every fire whose dominant fuel group is timber (TU/TL) plus a seeded draw of 250 others (seed 20261119): 944 fires (718 main 2017-21, 226 recent 2022-23). 2024 is excluded because LANDFIRE has no disturbance layer for it yet. Built (inputs and truths) before the ratchet closed, scored once after it (rule note in the exam summary)

exam.summary: 944 exam fires, read from their first six days and graded on measurements the network never saw: MTBS high-severity share (357 forest fires with severity, 531 in all fuels), gridMET wind on the fire days (944, the network reads with the wind inputs blanked) and Globe-LFMC samples (175). Run once with R6 after the dev calibration (training/results/exam.json). Classical rivals: max ERC, BI and FWI over the fire days and Van Wagner crown-fire potential (each through the same kind of 2-number dev map for MAE), a Rothermel wind back-calculation from the observed head spread (dev-mapped for MAE), an LFMC climatology (fuel type x month from dev sites) and dev medians. Intervals at import (21 Nov 2026, training/import_check.py, from shipped numbers only): a paired bootstrap over the shipped per-fire rows (10,000 resamples, seed 20261119) where the rows carry the baseline (crown potential, ERC, back-calculation, dev medians), else Zou's interval from exam.json's own 95 % bootstrap intervals (independent: conservative). Verdict: loss if a baseline is better with an interval excluding 0, win only if every baseline is beaten that way, else tie. Result: severity ranks tie (forests: level with FWI and ERC; all fuels: crown potential ahead, interval just includes 0), severity errors win narrowly, wind ranks win, wind level loses to the dev median, live moisture loses on error and ties on rank. Error bars: the 80 % bands cover 69 % of forest severity truths (too narrow), 77 % across fuels, 83 % of wind and 90 % of LFMC. Rule note: the exam input build (exam.py build), including the truth values stored in the same records, ran before the ratchet closed, while R4 was the incumbent; nothing was predicted, scored or opened before the close (model card, ratchet.yaml). Dev twins fed both the physics calibration and the gate.

The z = 1000 scaling kept the released model off that path. R7f passes the rule's numbers but was held, and the exam was not opened.
