Conformal or heteroscedastic severity bands per fuel group, fitted on more dev fires.
Drop live fuel moisture or replace it with a phenology input.
Validate growth against GOFER hourly perimeters.

physics.summary: FireSim, the shared fire platform's simulator (ML Ratchet Wildfire Phase 1, shared/fire/firesim, not edited): Rothermel 1972 + Albini 1976 surface spread on the Scott & Burgan 40 fuel models with wind adjustment and slope, Van Wagner 1977 crown-fire initiation and Cruz 2005 / Rothermel 1991 crown spread, Albini spotting with stochastic embers, Nelson-type dead fuel moisture, minimum-travel-time spread on 180 m grids, and its VIIRS detection emulator. FireDetective's bank generator (training/simbank.py) wraps it with randomised drivers and three physics versions found by dev twin tests, then sees each fire through a FEDS-like perimeter emulator tuned on real dev VIIRS pixels.
checks: FireSim Phase 1 (shared/fire/checks): 436 of 436 published BehavePlus / Rothermel cases within tolerance (published_examples.json); WAF vs pyretechnics max difference 3e-8 and crown fire-type agreement 1.0 (pyretechnics_crosscheck.json); two-fuel strip arrival time vs the hand solution 3e-9 relative (analytic.json); Van Wagner I0 example 2,476 vs quoted 2,500 kW/m (crown.json)

Twin test (training/twin.py, results/twin_v1.json): each dev fire re-simulated from its first mapped perimeter with its own fuels and weather. Sims grow on 91 % of half-days vs 50 % real, have 3x the VIIRS pixels (log10(1 + pixels) 1.38 vs 0.85), more night FRP (0.86 vs 0.50) and rounder shapes (elongation 0.40 vs 0.70)

numpy == torch: max difference 6e-7 (means), 9e-6 (log-sigma), 9e-8 (probabilities) on 40 dev fires (weights/export_check.json). The site instrument recomputes the features from the raw record and runs the ensemble in TypeScript: equal to feats.py + firedetective.py to 8e-16 on 40 cases (4 fires x 10 what-ifs, float16 weights); float16 weights move the outputs by ≤ 3e-4 relative

Import check (21 Nov 2026, training/import_check.py): the shipped per-fire exam rows re-derive exam.json's headline numbers (differences ≤ 0.003, from the rows' rounding), and the four example fires' raw observations through pipeline.py reproduce their exam rows exactly to the shipped digits

models.name: FirePilot
models.tagline: A learned containment-line planner, graded in a fire simulator on 48 real exam fires
models.question: Where to build containment line in a fire's first 72 h *(graded in simulation)*
models.summary: FirePilot is given a wildfire at its first afternoon satellite detection, one forecast FireSim run from that burned area and a crew budget in metres of line per working hour. It picks one line plan for the next 72 h: a build order (centre-out, or ends-in from anchors), a centre angle and half-width around the fire, and offsets from the fire edge at the centre and the far side. A 6,338-weight value network ranks 301 candidate plans by their predicted share of the no-action growth stopped; it learned only from simulated fires scored in a hidden truth world. Graded once in FireSim on 48 real exam fires (real LANDFIRE fuels and terrain, real HRRR weather, real first FEDS detection), v1.1 (27 Nov 2026: the same network trained on crew starts from 06 to 18 h instead of the afternoon only) stopped 0.469 of the simulated no-action growth at 300 m/h and 0.625 at 1000 m/h (v1.0: 0.474 and 0.644; paired differences include zero), against 0.316 and 0.480 for anchor and flank, the best classical plan, and 0.400 and 0.591 for a 29-simulation forecast search (MPC). It beats anchor and flank on 71 % / 63 % of fires and MPC on 54 % / 42 %. A perfect-foresight search, a bound, reaches 0.618 and 0.791. Its own predictions are now close to the simulated truth (optimistic by 0.054 / 0.005, v1.0 0.113 / 0.069). v1.0 re-scored in FireSim physics p2 (22 Nov 2026) stopped 0.401 and 0.629. These are simulated outcomes: the simulator gets the size of the real 72 h growth about right and its shape only partly.
models.disclaimer: Graded inside the simulator. Every outcome is a FireSim outcome on real exam landscapes, weather and detections, with a holding rule for the line; a free run of the same physics matches the observed 72 h perimeters only partly (Dice 0.40, F1 on new area 0.34), the real fires were fought, and the planner was never tested against real line-building records. A research benchmark, not a tool for directing crews.
models.reads: At the first afternoon FEDS detection, on a 90 m grid: the detected burned area; one FORECAST FireSim run from it (arrival time and flame length over 72 h, on the real LANDFIRE landscape and the HRRR weather with the forecast's wind error); the line-building cost per metre from the fuel map (grass 0.6-0.8, timber litter 1.0, shrub 1.7, slash 2.0, non-burnable 0); the crew clock (two crews, 08:00-20:00 local solar time, from 2 h after detection); and the budget in metres of line per working hour. Thirteen scenario features and 18 plan-against-forecast features per candidate plan. Never the truth world's hidden spread error.
returns: One line plan: build order (0 centre-out, 1 ends-in), centre angle φc from the forecast head (°), half-width ω (5-180°), offsets d_h at the centre and d_f at the far side (90 m-8 km). The line is the 8-connected inner boundary of {distance from the fire ≥ d(Φ)} inside the sector, d(Φ) = d_f + (d_h − d_f)·((1 + cos(Φ − φc))/2)²
The plan's line cells, each cell's build completion time (h after detection, on the crew clock's 0.05 h steps; FireSim rounds them up to 15 min) and the km built within 72 h

The network's predicted share of the no-action 72 h growth stopped, with σ (Gaussian; the widen-only factor fitted on the dev gate is 1.0). On the exam the 90 % range covered the truth on 98 % / 100 % of fires and the prediction was optimistic by 0.11 / 0.07 (300 / 1000 m/h)
models.network: MLP 31 → 64 → 64 → 2, tanh, 6,338 weights (plus 62 feature-scaling numbers). Heads: the mean saved fraction (sigmoid, MSE) and log σ (Gaussian NLL on the detached residual). 300 epochs with early stopping on a 10 % simulated selection set: RMSE 0.124, Spearman 0.82 (the geometric proxy alone 0.70). Planning: score 205 candidates (5 baselines, a 40-plan grid, 160 prior draws), then 2 rounds of CEM on the network (48 plans each) around the top 6, and take the argmax: about 3 s median on one core (53 s on the largest, 650,000-cell window). numpy + scipy inference.
models.noise: Simulated: a hidden truth-world ROS factor f_ros ~ LogNormal(0, 0.5) (the spread of the Phase 1 replay ensemble) that the planner never sees, and forecast wind errors (speed × LogNormal(0, 0.25), direction + N(0, 20°), constant over 72 h). The background is real: LANDFIRE fuels and terrain and HRRR weather from 28 dev fires in 60 % and 75 % of the training scenarios.

approach.real_backdrop: 60 % of training scenarios sit on real LANDFIRE windows of 28 dev fires and 75 % use their real HRRR weather; the rest are FireSim parametric landscapes and synthetic weather
approach.physics_inputs: Every plan feature comes from one forecast FireSim run: arrival time and flame length along the line, the share of the line built before the forecast fire arrives and the share it would overrun (flames > 2.4 m), the forecast growth in the line's shadow, and two connectivity proxies of the area saved
approach.physics_anchor: The connectivity proxy on the forecast run (rung r0, no learning) is both a feature and the planner the network had to beat; every training target and exam outcome is a FireSim truth-world simulation of the plan with the flame-length holding rule

exam.short: 48 real exam fires, outcomes simulated in FireSim, once
exam.summary: The 48-fire exam replay subset, run once after the ratchet closed (training/exam.py, training/results/exam_summary.json). Every method planned from the same forecast run and was scored in the same truth world, with a hidden spread error per fire. The metric is the share of the no-action 72 h growth a plan stops, (area without action − area with the plan) / (area without action − detected area), averaged over fires. Baselines on the same fires and draws: the five fixed plans (anchor and flank, the best of them; direct attack at the head; indirect lines at 1, 2 and 4 km), r0 (the proxy planner, no learning), the oracle pick of the best fixed plan per fire, and MPC, a cross-entropy search over plans in the forecast world with 29 FireSim runs per fire. The perfect-foresight bound runs the same search in the truth world (about 44 runs) and is a bound, not a competitor (own row). Intervals: 95 % bootstrap over fires, as shipped; the paired intervals are of FirePilot minus each baseline. A verdict is win only if FirePilot beats every baseline on the row and each paired interval excludes zero. All outcomes are simulated. v1.0 (rung r1) was graded once on 19 Nov 2026. v1.1 (rung r5vs, promoted by the ratchet on 27 Nov 2026) was graded once on the same 48 fires, budgets, hidden draws and physics p1 (training/exam.py with FIREPILOT_EXAM_TAG=v1.1; training/results/exam_summary_v1.1.json, exam_v1.1_paired_vs_v1.0.json). The rows below are v1.1's where they say so; v1.0's values stay in the notes.

wins: Simulated, on 48 real exam fires: it stops 0.474 of the no-action 72 h growth at 300 m/h and 0.644 at 1000 m/h, against 0.316 and 0.480 for anchor and flank (paired +0.16, 95 % intervals 0.08-0.23 and 0.08-0.26), and it is better than anchor and flank on 71 % of fires at both budgets.

At 300 m/h it beats the 29-simulation forecast search on the mean (0.474 against 0.400, paired +0.074, 0.012 to 0.139) with one forecast run and about 3 s of planning; it also beats the oracle pick of the best fixed plan per fire (0.401 / 0.562). Under FireSim physics p2 this 300 m/h lead over MPC is no longer clear (paired −0.013 to 0.115), while at 1000 m/h it becomes one (+0.103, 0.030 to 0.179).
It keeps 20,651 ha unburned at 300 m/h and 65,230 ha at 1000 m/h, summed over the 48 fires (MPC 18,467 and 51,543; anchor and flank 8,248 and 15,454): 77-81 % of the perfect-foresight bound's mean.
It found and worked around a FireSim bug (U1): timed suppression lines leak diagonally; its 8-connected lines hold, with the line length counted so they are not longer.
Trained only in simulation: no real fire outcome was a training target, and the exam was run once, after the ratchet closed.
losses: Per fire it beats MPC on only 46 % of fires at both budgets; at 300 m/h MPC is better on more fires (54 %).
Large fires (detected above about 160 ha): only 0.20 of the growth stopped at 300 m/h, against 0.33 for the perfect-foresight bound.
Its error bars are wide (90 % coverage 0.98-1.00; the 90 % range is often ±0.8 on a 0-1 score) and it is optimistic about its own pick by 0.07-0.11 (winner's curse).
On the 16 recent fires (2022-24) no paired interval against MPC or, at 1000 m/h, against anchor and flank excludes zero.
limits: Simulated outcomes only. Every number above is a FireSim outcome; a free run of the same physics matches the observed 72 h growth in size (×1.14) but only partly in shape (Dice 0.40, F1 on new area 0.34), the simulated fire is often in the wrong place, the real fires were fought, and FirePilot has not been tested against real line-building records (ICS-209 or similar).

FireSim upstream bug U1: its corner rule blocks a diagonal step only past permanently non-burnable cells, not past cells blocked by a timed line (t_block ≤ t), so 4-connected suppression lines leak. Every outcome here (training targets, the ratchet, the exam, all baselines) was scored in a FireSim with this bug. FirePilot's lines, and so every plan's, are 8-connected to avoid it, with the 8-boundary's cells sharing the 4-connected line length, so each cell's build time is a modelling choice made around the bug. A FireSim fix (physics p2) needs the frozen sets rebuilt and every rung and baseline re-scored; how far the numbers move is not known.

FireSim p1 bugs U12 and U13 (found 22 Nov 2026 in the physics p2 re-score): a line could take credit for cells the fire reached before the line was built (the cell stayed unburned, or spread in transit from it was cancelled at an hour boundary). Plans that close lines near the fire gained most. On the p2 frozen set (159 scenarios) r1 scores 0.460 against 0.484 on p1 and r0 0.403 (unchanged), so r1 still leads; direct attack falls from 0.107 to 0.054 and anchor and flank from 0.195 to 0.114, while the indirect plans barely move. On the p2 dev gate r1 scores 0.487 and r0 0.354 (p1 0.481 and 0.383), so the r1 decision stands. On the p2 exam r1 stops 0.401 / 0.629 (p1 0.474 / 0.644); at 300 m/h its leads over MPC (+0.050, −0.013 to 0.115) and r0 (+0.054, −0.025 to 0.131) are no longer clear, and the network's optimism grows to 0.19 / 0.09 (training/results/exam_summary_p2.json). See NOTEBOOK.md.
One line, two crews, one decision at detection: no re-planning, no aircraft, no spotting (off in the planning world), no values at risk and no line loss other than the 2.4 m flame-length rule.
The domain is the stored LANDFIRE window: on 45 of 48 exam fires the 15 km crop reaches the window edge (FireSim upstream U2), so growth beyond it is cut off for every method alike.

Training fires are synthetic fires grown from point ignitions on dev landscapes; real detections are more ragged. Live fuel moisture is constant, and FireSim's fires do not stall or burn out as real fires do (simulated fires grow on 91 % of half-days, real ones on 50 %).

Rule notes: the exam was split into two stages for compute (stage A: no action, fixed plans, r0, FirePilot; stage B: MPC and the bound in a seeded order), decided before any exam output existed; both stages finished on all 48 fires, so the split changed nothing. The 40 dev fires set the physics p1 calibration and supplied the 12 gate fires, so the gate is partly in-sample for the physics. The tercile numbers come from per-fire rows that were not shipped.

Crew clock (audit, 25 Nov 2026): every training scenario started in the afternoon, 34 working hours in 72 h, so that input has sd 1e-6. A morning clock (36 h) sits about 55,000 sd away and raised predicted savings by .05-.15 on three packaged fires. All 48 exam fires had 34 h, so the exam is unaffected. Since 27 Nov 2026 the reader warns when the clock is outside the trained range. v1.1 trained on crew starts 06-18 h local solar, which give 34.0-35.95 working hours (the input's sd is now 0.013, not 1e-6); a 36 h clock is just outside it. On a varied-start simulated set (160 scenarios) v1.1 stops 0.493 against v1.0's 0.470 (paired +0.023, 95 % −0.002 to +0.050).
help: Real suppression records (ICS-209 incident reports, line-construction and containment logs) to test any planner outside the simulator; FireSim has no validated suppression data.
Dead-fuel stick moisture from FEMS (the old NFMD has no public download) and larger LANDFIRE windows for the exam replay fires.
next: Re-plan each morning (receding horizon): run the value net at each shift with the new detection. The biggest realism gain and probably the biggest score gain; the bound is about 15 points higher.
Imitate the perfect-foresight search: use the truth-CEM plans on the training bank as targets, or a ranking loss, instead of an MSE value net that suffers the winner's curse on its own argmax.

Train in FireSim physics p2 (U1 and U12 fixed upstream on 22 Nov 2026; r1 already scored on val_p2, gate_p2 and the p2 exam): rebuild the training banks as p2, retrain and re-take the rungs against val_p2 and gate_p2, and release a p2 rung only through a new exam.
Values-at-risk targets (WUI cells), multi-segment lines, aircraft and spotting, and a fire-persistence (burnout and stall) module in FireSim.
Wider clock coverage: start hours 06-18 give only 34-36 working hours; night and split-shift clocks, and crews that start before detection, are still outside training.

physics.summary: Fire spread is FireSim (Wildfire Phase 1, shared/fire/firesim), wrapped without editing it: Rothermel 1972 surface spread with Albini 1976 on the Scott & Burgan 40 fuel models, Van Wagner 1977 crown fire, Nelson dead-fuel moisture and minimum-travel-time spread on a 16-neighbour stencil, at 90 m on real LANDFIRE fuels and terrain with hourly HRRR weather, crown fire on, no spotting, and the dev-calibrated ROS factors (physics p1). Suppression is FireSim's timed line: each line cell blocks spread from the moment it is built, unless the fire reaches it with a flame length above 2.4 m (8 ft, the NWCG hauling-chart limit), where the line fails. Two worlds per scenario: the truth world (the scenario's weather and the calibrated ROS factors × a hidden f_ros ~ LogNormal(0, 0.5)) and the forecast the planner sees (wind speed × LogNormal(0, 0.25), direction + N(0, 20°), held constant; no hidden factor).
checks: FireSim (shared/fire/checks, Phase 1): 436 of 436 published Rothermel / BehavePlus values within half the last published digit; against pyretechnics on 6,720 flat and slope cases, ROS median difference 4.9e-5; uniform-fuel ellipses 0.98 of the predicted area (0.99 with level_set); dev replays 40 fires, next-day F1 0.153 uncalibrated, 0.194 calibrated (0.184 leave-one-out)

Line geometry (training/leak_test.py, training/results/upstream_U1_leak.json): a closed ring built at t = 0 around a point ignition in uniform grass, cells burned outside after 48 h: no line 3,972; 4-connected timed line 3,551 (it leaks diagonally, FireSim upstream candidate U1); the same ring as non-burnable fuel 0; the 8-connected timed line FirePilot builds 0. The km of line are counted on the 4-connected boundary × π/4, so the 8-boundary does not inflate the line length

Fidelity on the 48 exam fires (training/results/exam_summary.json, fidelity): a free run of the truth physics with no line and no hidden error, from first detection, against the observed FEDS PM perimeters, medians: Dice on total area 0.48 / 0.43 / 0.40 at 24 / 48 / 72 h (persistence 0.47 / 0.25 / 0.19; with FireSim's 21 Nov 2026 mask-ignition fix the same run gives 0.49 / 0.44 / 0.40, planner outcomes unchanged, see NOTEBOOK.md); F1 on new area 0.27 / 0.34 / 0.34; simulated / observed new area ×1.55 / ×1.11 / ×1.14. The size of the growth is about right by 48-72 h, its shape only partly

Implementation (as shipped): numpy == torch 8.7e-8; the page's JavaScript vs Python on its six fires, 66 plans: predictions within 8.5e-7, features within 1e-7 except one timing feature off by one 0.05 h clock step (6.9e-4); the release demo reproduces the exam plans on 6 of 6 fire-budgets. Re-checked on import (21 Nov 2026): firepilot.py is byte-identical to the module build_release.py generates from training/fp; the demo reproduces 6 of 6 exam plans; the site instrument (TypeScript, with numpy's float32 line-cost arithmetic) matches firepilot.py on 90 cases to 4.4e-16

models.name: QuakeNet v2
models.tagline: Several seismometers, one earthquake.
models.question: Where, how deep, how big and when — from 2–10 seismometers together?
models.summary: QuakeNet v1.2 reads each station's 41-minute record; a graph network with stations as nodes and station pairs as edges combines those readings and the P-wave arrival times into an epicentre, depth, Mw and origin time, each with an error bar. It learned only from simulated earthquakes seen at 2-10 real stations at once, laid into real station noise, and was examined on 1,456 real earthquakes at 2 stations and 400 at up to 10.
models.reads: 2-10 stations, each with 41 minutes of three-component ground velocity (1 sample/s, response removed), its coordinates, the time of its first sample and a rough P time
returns: Epicentre (latitude, longitude) with a 68% error ellipse (km)
Depth (km) with a bar on log depth
Moment magnitude Mw ± 68% bar
Origin time ± bar (s)
models.network: Graph network, 115k weights: node and edge MLPs, 3 rounds of message passing (width 64), mean + max readout; corrects a classical anchor; bivariate Gaussian NLL on the epicentre offset, beta-NLL on log depth, Mw and origin time
models.noise: 1,284 real quiet-time windows from the 127 IU/II stations (QuakeNet v1.2's pool), from the same station where possible (80%)

approach.real_backdrop: 1,284 real quiet-time windows from the 127 GSN stations
approach.physics_inputs: ak135 P travel times and slownesses at the anchor, station geometry in the anchor's frame
approach.physics_anchor: QuakeNet v1.2's per-station readings combined classically (least squares on distance and back-azimuth; inverse-variance Mw and depth; origin time from P picks)

wins: Epicentre at every station count: median miss 427 / 279 / 188 / 127 km at 2 / 3 / 5 / all stations, against 521 / 410 / 320 / 240 km for v1.2 combined classically and 4,139 / 669 / 276 / 173 km for the travel-time locator.
Shallow depth (<= 70 km): median error 11.7 km with all stations against 29.3 km for v1.2 combined: the dev-twin depth calibration (r6) carried over.
Origin time: median 4.3 s with all stations, against 5.8 s (v1.2 combined) and 14.4 s (travel-time locator).
losses: Mw: 0.097 mean error against 0.089 for simply averaging v1.2's per-station Mw (0.114 against 0.109 at 2 stations).
Deep quakes (> 70 km) read too shallow: median depth error 38 km against 28 km for v1.2 combined (all stations).

Without catalogue help it does not locate well (supplementary exam, 27 Nov 2026, same 400 quakes, continuous records that know only the UTC hour of the origin): with P picked by a grid-search associator over each event's records, the median epicentre miss is 497 km with all stations (mean 1,346 km), against 123 km for the same records with the catalogue's predicted P as the guess. A plain per-record trigger picker gives 1,284 km. Only 40% of the associator's picks lie within 10 s of the true P.
limits: Long-period (LH) records only, 25-95 degrees, M >= 5.5; 2 to 10 stations.

The P pick searches +-30 s around a guess; in the exam (as in v1.2) the guess came from the catalogue origin. The headline exam numbers are for catalogue-assisted picking; with independent picks (supplementary exam, 27 Nov 2026) the median miss is 497 km, not 127 km. The travel-time locator baseline also picks inside the catalogue window.
Two stations leave most of the location uncertain: median miss 427 km.
Error bars: epicentre ellipses cover 62-68% and depth bars 60% for a nominal 68%.
The dev-twin calibrations (r5, r6) are shifts fitted on 40 dev quakes; deep quakes are now over-corrected.
help: EarthScope dataselect answered 'too many requests' for 51 of about 4,200 requests; events still reached 10 stations from other stations.

Catalogue arrivals (audit, 25 Nov 2026): the exam gives each station the catalogue's predicted P arrival as its pick guess. Station coordinates and those arrivals alone locate all four 10-station packaged events within 4.24 m, so the arrivals carry the location. The network does read the waveforms (zeroed or noise waveforms put the epicentre 519-16,307 km off), but jittering the guess by 60 s moves it 241-955 km. The exam's location numbers therefore describe catalogue-assisted picking, not independent detection.
next: An independent picker that works at 1 sample/s for M 5.5-6 (only 40% of associated picks lie within 10 s), or broadband (BH) picking for the P time only; the supplementary exam (training/indep_exam.py) is the benchmark.
Mw: let the classical inverse-variance Mw through unchanged (or learn a per-event bias only), and measure the deep-depth over-correction on dev by depth class.
Bigger station sets and regional distances; broadband (BH) channels and a sharper P picker for timing.
A second pass: re-linearise at the network's own epicentre and run the graph again.

models.name: TsunamiNet
models.tagline: A flow trained on simulated tsunamis reads real DART buoys and forecasts the next ones.
models.question: How big is the tsunami coming, from the first DART readings?
models.summary: From up to three DART bottom-pressure records (a 90-minute window around each buoy's predicted arrival) after a Pacific subduction earthquake, a conditional RealNVP normalizing flow gives the posterior of the seafloor source on NOAA's SIFT unit sources: magnitude, where along the trench the slip is centred, how much sits on the deeper row, and how long the rupture is. Pushing posterior samples through linear shallow-water Green's functions forecasts the maximum wave at DARTs the network did not read. Trained only on simulated tsunamis laid into real quiet DART noise; graded once on 28 real DART-recorded tsunamis (2007-2025).
models.disclaimer: Research only. Not a tsunami warning system; official forecasts come from NOAA's tsunami warning centers.
models.reads: Detided, high-passed 1-minute DART water-column height (NDBC historical files) for up to 3 DARTs, the USGS epicentre and origin time.
returns: Posterior samples of Mw, along-trench centroid (km from the epicentre's unit-source column), deep-row slip share and log10 rupture length; 68 % and 90 % ranges widened on dev (Mw x3.18, centroid x4.40)
Forecast maximum |eta| at any other DART with Green's functions, in a 190-minute window after its predicted arrival: median and 68 % range (widened x2.08 on dev)
models.network: Per-DART 1-D CNN over 20 channels (record, mask, 18 unit-source responses) x 90 minutes, permutation-invariant mean/max pooling over up to 3 DARTs, plus 23 features of the SIFT-style NNLS solution on the same windows (physics anchor), conditioning an 8-layer RealNVP flow over 4 source parameters. 520k weights.
models.noise: Real DART bottom-pressure noise: 955 quiet 24-hour windows starting at event-mode (1-minute) triggers 2006-2025 that are more than 2 days from any NGDC tsunami (712 for training, 243 for the frozen sets), with the same detiding, gaps and glitches as real records.

approach.real_backdrop: Real quiet DART noise windows (event-mode 1-minute data), with their gaps
approach.physics_inputs: Each DART's own Green's-function responses to the 18 unit sources around the epicentre, as input channels
approach.physics_anchor: The SIFT-style non-negative least-squares inversion on the same windows feeds the flow; forecasts are posterior samples pushed through the Green's functions

Dev-widened Mw ranges cover 68 % of exam truths at nominal 68 %.
losses: Reads magnitudes low (mean bias -0.22). Tohoku 2011: 8.67 [8.44, 8.92] vs 9.1.

limits: Linear propagation at 8 arc-min (not NOAA's 4'): far-field window correlation 0.73-0.81 against 4'; no dispersion, Coriolis or Kajiura filter.
Only thrust slip on the two shallowest SIFT rows; other mechanisms are read as if they were interface thrusts.
Hindcast-quality data: NDBC real-time files with event-mode gaps; the detiding is causal but tuned on the 3 days before.

Not strictly real-time: glitch removal and gap filling read up to 34 later observed samples (about 34 min at 1-minute sampling, longer across gaps), so a live input window is final only that long after its last minute. Training and the exam used the same processing.
Dev is 5 events; the widening factors (x2-4.4) rest on them.

The released widening factors were computed with the interval sides swapped (training/calibrate.py took the upper half-width for a truth below the median; fixed 22 Nov 2026, not re-run: the per-event dev rows are not shipped). The exam coverage above is for the factors as shipped.
Green's functions exist for 68 DART sites (those that recorded the eligible events); no coastal tide gauges.

models.name: LawFinder
models.tagline: What does each simulator believe, in one line, and is it true?
models.question: One-line laws extracted from the simulators, graded on real exams
models.summary: LawFinder runs symbolic regression on simulated banks from WaterSim, FireSim, GridSim, BuildingSim and RoadSim and returns short equations with error bars: the long-term runoff ratio of a basin, the next-day growth of a wildfire, GB system inertia, the GB frequency nadir after a trip, the annual energy intensity of a single-family home, and a car's energy per km on a trip. Each law is a rung on a ratchet of complexity levels and physics versions, chosen on a frozen simulated set and a small real dev set, then examined once on the platform's real exam beside the textbook law (its constant fitted on the same dev set), the collection's network and a dumb baseline.
models.reads: Per law: water - aridity PET/P, snow fraction, P-PET seasonal synchrony, soil storage index; fire - perimeter (km), daily 10 m wind (m/s), 100-h dead fuel moisture (%), fuel group; grid inertia - demand (GW), inverter-based share; grid nadir - MW lost, inertia (GVA s), demand; homes - HDD and CDD (base 18 C), floor area, year built; road - mean speed, positive kinetic energy per metre, net and absolute grade, mass, CdA, Crr, ambient temperature, hybrid and electric flags.
returns: Long-term runoff ratio: runoff ratio Q/P with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
Daily fire growth: log10(new area km² + 1 cell) with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
GB system inertia: system inertia E with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
GB frequency nadir: frequency drop to the nadir f0 - f_min with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
Home energy signature: site energy per floor area with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
Trip energy per km: energy per km, fuel at LHV or DC battery (MJ/km), with a 68 % bar (frozen-set residual sd, dev-widened)
models.network: No network: symbolic regression (lawsearch, numpy/scipy; PySR-style regularised evolution with Levenberg-Marquardt constants and a hall of fame per complexity). Operators + - * / ^ exp log sqrt inv sq; complexity = node count, up to 25.
models.noise: Platform noise models as shipped: WaterSim forcing error on the inputs the law sees; FireSim runs on real HRRR; GridSim events measured as 1 s means; BuildingSim weather shifts; RoadSim drives the true weather (ambient + N(0, 1.5) C, wind x U(0.4, 0.9)) while the law reads the observed one. No real labels in training.

approach.real_backdrop: Real ERA5-Land forcing windows, real dev LANDFIRE/HRRR, NESO train-year operating points, TMYx weather, RoadData's unlabelled VED routes

limits: Water: FlowCast, the collection's ungauged network, beats the law (MAE 0.112 vs 0.129 on 619 basins). The law beats Budyko-Fu (0.141-0.154). In snowy basins (f_s > 0.3, 88 basins) every method is poor (law 0.22). All rows share ERA5-Land forcing, which under-catches mountain precipitation: 50 basins carry more water out than ERA5 says falls in.

Fire: FireSim's own law over-predicts real next-day growth a median 36 times (bias +1.56 decades). The released law survives only because the dev gate cut it down to a saturating curve. Over all fire-days it loses to FireData's yesterday's-growth baseline (1.15 vs 0.67 mean |log₁₀|); on growth days it is the best row (0.69 vs FireCast 0.76). FireSim has no fire persistence (stalls, burnout), the platform's known gap. Slope was not an input: real exam fires have no landscape.

Grid inertia: GridSim's raw GB fleets commit about 4.5 s of inertia per MW of demand where NESO's outturn shows about 7, so the law is 33 % low (MdAPE) and loses to 7 s × demand (15.1 %) and to the dev median (24 %). Its ranking is the best of all rows (ρ 0.975).

Grid nadir: the loss labels are noisy (REMIT/FUELINST matches); 148 events. The dev gate had only 4 events, one of them (9 Aug 2019) a cascade. The 68 % bar (±0.31 Hz) is far too wide: it covers 100 % of exam events.

Homes: the law loses to the dumb dev median (MdAPE 39.3 % vs 33.4 %) and to a log-linear fit on dev (26.6 %). BuildingSim's homes are about 1.4 times too energy-intensive at physics 1.0; 1.4 fixes the median but not the spread. RECS energy is EIA's billing-based estimate, and home-to-home variation (occupants, setpoints) is not in the inputs.

Road: the law loses to EnergyNet everywhere and, on real VED trips, to RoadData's MOVES-like and window-label baselines (18.6 % against 11.8 % and 14.1 %; EnergyNet 10.1 %). It beats road-load on EPA petrol and hybrid tests (17.3 % and 13.1 % against 25.0 % and 19.6 %) and loses to it on electric cars: it reads the 2 VED Leafs 42 % low and EPA BEVs 42 % high, one exponent for every electric car. RoadSim's own shorter law (p2-c10) beats the released one on VED petrol (14.0 %) and on EPA (15.1 %); the dev gate (14 dev cars, 1,178 EPA dev tests) picked the longer law. Real CdA and Crr are class defaults on VED (EPA: from the road-load coefficients); VED fuel is MAF-estimated for most cars. Exam run 1 mis-scaled EnergyNet's VED rows (units); they were re-computed from its stored predictions.

Method: one search per physics version, time-boxed at 4-7 minutes on a shared core; another seed can give a different front. Dev sets are small (4 grid events, 40 fires, 52 basins), so the gate is coarse. The road law (RoadSim trip energy) was added on 22 Nov 2026, after the other four.

Road, electric cars and grade: the released law's energy falls as the road gets steeper. On one battery-electric drive (same speed trace, start charge and seed) it gives 0.512, 0.408 and 0.324 MJ/km at -2 %, 0 and +2 % net grade, where RoadSim's battery energy is 0.009, 0.332 and 0.659 MJ/km (audit, 25 Nov 2026). At e = 1 the exponent's base is below one, so the sign holds for every BEV. Six of the 21 logged p2 candidates rise with grade; all six missed the pooled promotion margin. A sign-checked search (27 Nov 2026) found no replacement that passed the ratchet.

Input ranges: each law is fitted inside its bank's input ranges (var_info in lawfinder_laws.json) and extrapolates freely outside them. The homes law's heating slope turns negative for homes built after 2020 (+1.87 at 2020, -3.13 at 2025, kWh/m² per 1000 K·d). Chaining the two grid laws, 615 of 2,356 inertia predictions on a regular grid fall below the nadir law's 90 GVA·s floor. Since 27 Nov 2026 predict() warns outside the declared ranges (strict=True raises). One of the demo's real grid events is outside them (a loss above 2 GW).
help: Daymet/NLDAS forcing would separate law skill from ERA5-Land bias (WaterData help_wanted)
next: Fire: add a persistence module to FireSim (stall and burnout probability by fuel and weather) and re-run the search; the law ladder shows exactly where FireSim's growth departs from reality.
Grid inertia: rescale GridSim's GB fleet to NESO's inertia per MW (the GridPulse wrapper's fix) as physics i2, and re-take the ladder; the shape term (1 − 0.85 s) should survive.
Water: a recession law −dQ/dt = a Q^b on the same banks, and a Daymet/NLDAS exam to separate law skill from ERA5-Land bias.
Road: give the law the car's engine size or label fuel economy, cold start and trip length as inputs (RoadData has them), and widen the generator toward lighter cars.

Road: a powertrain-aware grade term. The sign-checked search (27 Nov 2026, rungs p2s-*) found no law that reads grade with the right sign; its best, p2s-c19, ignores grade and scored R^2 0.757 against 0.767, so it was rejected and p1-c23 stays. Options for the owner: an EV dev check as a rule, or a search seeded with a road-load grade term per powertrain.
Homes: add heating fuel and system as inputs (a law per fuel) and occupants; RECS dev shows the fuel matters most.

physics.summary: No new physics: the collection's shared simulators are used unchanged (WaterSim v1, FireSim v1, GridSim 1.1 via GridPulse's GB state sampler, BuildingSim 1.0/1.4, RoadSim physics v1/v2). Each law is a statement about what one simulator implies.
checks: lawsearch recovers a planted Budyko-Fu law with 1 % noise to the noise floor (MSE 1.0e-4 vs 1.0e-4)
Every simulator's own Phase 1 checks apply (shared/*/checks)
Release evaluator (numpy) equals the search engine to machine precision; the page's JS equals numpy (training/results/js_parity.json; road law: 6e-16 on 1,500 points, js_parity_road.json)

models.name: AirfoilNet
models.tagline: The wind tunnel: an airfoil polar from its shape, graded on real tunnel data.
models.question: What polar will this airfoil have, and where does it stall?
models.summary: From an airfoil's coordinates and a Reynolds number (4e4-6e5), AirfoilNet predicts Cl, Cd and Cm against angle of attack, with 68% error bars, and from them Cl max and the stall angle. It learned only from 151 alpha sweeps of mfoil, an XFOIL-class viscous-inviscid solver, on airfoil shapes from the UIUC database with every tested airfoil removed. It was examined once on the clean wind-tunnel polars of 75 airfoils from 34 families in the UIUC Low-Speed Airfoil Tests. It beats NeuralFoil on maximum lift and stall angle and loses to it on lift before stall, drag and moment.
models.reads: Airfoil coordinates (any .dat, Selig or Lednicer; refitted with an 18-parameter CST), Reynolds number 4e4-6e5, angles of attack (deg). Incompressible, clean (free transition).
returns: Cl(alpha) +- 68% bar
Cd(alpha) with a bar on ln Cd
Cm about c/4 (alpha) +- 68% bar
Cl max and stall angle from the predicted polar
models.network: MLP on polars: 50 shape/Re features + 3 alpha features -> 3 hidden layers of 128 (SiLU) -> Cl, ln Cd, Cm and their log-sigmas; beta-NLL; 3 seeds averaged (3 x 40,710 parameters)
models.noise: None injected: no public record of tunnel noise for these polars. Scatter comes from the solver itself (loose-convergence points, different panelings).

approach.physics_inputs: CST thickness and camber at 24 stations (a shape fit, not a solver output)

rows.note: Paired subset. Where it converges the raw solver is the most accurate method before stall.

wins: Cl max: 0.082 mean error against 0.096 for NeuralFoil and 0.22 for the raw solver.
Stall angle: 1.76 deg against 2.19 for NeuralFoil and 4.0 for the raw solver, which stops converging before stall.
losses: Lift before stall (0.091 vs 0.082), drag (|ln ratio| 0.177 vs 0.126) and moment (0.0173 vs 0.0153) all lose to NeuralFoil, trained on far more XFOIL runs.
Where the raw solver converges it beats both networks before stall (Cl 0.071).
limits: Low Reynolds numbers (4e4-6e5), incompressible, clean airfoils only: no trips, flaps or roughness.
Trained on 151 sweeps (1,305 points); more simulations improved the simulated score but not the dev airfoils.
The solver gives no answer near stall on many airfoils, so stall was learned from incomplete polars; predicted stall is 1.3 deg early on average.
Error bars: Cm bars widened x4.75 on dev cover 83% (too wide); Cl and Cd cover 69% and 74%.
help: XFOIL itself (needs gfortran, not installable on the build machine); websites.umich.edu (mfoil home) and github.com answered 403 from the build machine.

Coordinates (audit, 25 Nov 2026; fixed 27 Nov 2026): polar(coords=...) assumed Selig order, so Lednicer blocks passed directly moved lift by up to 5.44; they are now reordered (the four packaged airfoils give identical lift either way). Reflecting a shape and the angle should reverse lift; the network's sum stays 0.20-1.13 within -6 to +6°, a symmetry it was not trained to keep.
next: Stall: a solver that converges past separation (XFOIL proper, or mfoil with a better Newton globalisation) so the bank has post-stall polars.
A bigger bank on a free machine (the 2-core build ran 30-50 s per sweep).
Ncrit and tunnel-turbulence nuisance (draw Ncrit per sweep), judged on the dev twins.

physics.summary: XFOIL-class viscous-inviscid analysis: linear-vorticity panel method with transpiration, two-equation integral boundary layer (Drela closures), e^N transition (Ncrit 9), lag-entrainment turbulent shear, wake, all coupled in one global Newton solve (mfoil by K. Fidkowski).
checks: Panel method vs exact Joukowski airfoil: Cl within 0.10-0.22%, Cp mean abs error 0.0012 (training/verify_physics.json)

backlog.name: GridSim GB inertia level
backlog.question: GridSim's GB fleets commit too little inertia: about 4.5 s per MW of demand where NESO's outturn shows about 7, roughly 35 % low. Fix the level in GridSim itself, not only in GridPulse's wrapper.

backlog.name: Forecast-weather archive
backlog.question: A day-ahead forecast-weather archive for 2022-2025 so DemandCast can be graded as it would be used (today its headline uses actual weather, an upper bound) and trained on real forecast errors.

backlog.name: Sub-second grid frequency
backlog.question: PMU-grade frequency (10-100 samples a second) so GridPulse can read inertia from the first 500 ms instead of from demand.

backlog.name: BuildingSim v2 calibration
backlog.question: Close BuildingSim's measured gaps (campus district energy, the heat-pump signature, generator intensity by use type, multi-zone), then re-train and re-score all four building models on the new physics version.

backlog.name: Independent forcing for the water exams
backlog.question: How much of each water model's exam gap is the method, and how much is ERA5-Land? Re-run every water exam (models and baselines) with Daymet or NLDAS forcing in place of ERA5-Land.

backlog.name: WaterSim v1.1
backlog.question: Fold the physics the four water models found into WaterSim, version the frozen sets, and re-score every rung.

backlog.name: FireSim physics p2
backlog.question: Fix the diagonal line leak (U1), add fire persistence, fold the physics the four fire models found into FireSim, then rebuild the frozen sets and re-score every rung.

backlog.name: Fire data the models are missing
backlog.question: Real dead-fuel moisture, suppression records and per-fire burn severity, so FireSim's moisture, suppression and severity can be checked against real data instead of proxies.

backlog.name: FireSim next-day growth level
backlog.question: FireSim grows fires far too much: at the same perimeter, wind and moisture its implied next-day growth is a median 36 times the real one (+1.56 decades). Bring the growth level to real fire-days.

backlog.name: Sun-to-grid space weather
backlog.question: From the solar wind at L1 to currents induced in power lines: how strong will the ground magnetic disturbance be, where, and what will it do to the grid?

backlog.name: Coast & Ocean
backlog.question: How high will the water get at this tide gauge, from tides, surge and waves?

backlog.name: RoomSense
backlog.question: How big is this room and how long does it ring, from one recorded clap?

backlog.name: GPSQuake
backlog.question: How far did the ground move, and was it an earthquake, slow slip or the seasons?

backlog.name: XRDNet
backlog.question: Which crystal phases are in this powder, from its X-ray diffraction pattern?

backlog.name: FRBNet
backlog.question: How much plasma did this fast radio burst cross, and how much was it scattered?

backlog.name: SpinNet
backlog.question: How fast and which way is this pitch spinning, from its flight alone?

backlog.name: SpinRock
backlog.question: How fast is this asteroid spinning, and what shape is it, from sparse survey photometry?

backlog.name: SpectraNet
backlog.question: Which gases, and how much of each, are in this infrared spectrum?

backlog.name: JetNet
backlog.question: Which particle started this jet?

backlog.name: DiffusionNet
backlog.question: From one tracked particle's wiggles inside a living cell: what kind of motion is it (Brownian, confined, anomalous, directed), and with what exponent?

backlog.name: Real-train ladder
backlog.question: How much does real labelled data add on top of physics? A possible direction, not planned work: a second ladder per model that may also train on a third real split, published beside the simulation-only ladder.

backlog.name: Prior Wars (TabPFN vs the physics prior)
backlog.question: Does a domain simulator beat a generic synthetic prior (TabPFN) on the collection's real exams, and how many real labels does the generic prior need to catch up?

backlog.name: River Bake-off (learner families on streamflow)
backlog.question: On one real problem (FlowCast's ungauged CAMELS-US streamflow plus a gauged nowcast), with the same simulated bank and compute for every arm, which learner family wins, and why?

backlog.name: Vehicle Bake-off (learner families on trip energy)
backlog.question: Does River's finding (families converge; the simulator is the lever) hold for a problem with strong physics: EnergyNet's trip energy, from EnergyNet's 151 features or the 1 Hz trace?

backlog.name: TreeTwin + ConformalRatchet (physics-trained GBDTs, exact TreeSHAP twin diagnostics & Mondrian conformal)
backlog.question: Can pure-numpy physics-trained GBDTs, exact real-vs-twin TreeSHAP attribution, and per-stratum Mondrian conformal calibration close the gap on tabular models, turn the twin test into a ranked physical bug list, and cut worst-stratum under-coverage?

backlog.name: River digital twin
backlog.question: Can a filter on WaterSim, fed by real gauges, beat FlowCast's learned nowcast?

backlog.name: Unlabelled real inputs
backlog.question: Does domain adaptation on real inputs, with no labels, close the sim-to-real gap while keeping the zero-real-labels claim?

backlog.name: Simulators in the browser (Rust to WebAssembly)
backlog.question: Run a shared simulator itself live on the site, not only the networks: first FireSim's spread kernel, ported to one Rust crate with a WebAssembly front end for the browser and a PyO3 front end for Python.
